XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Canlyniadau Economaidd yng Ngheredigion Penfro
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Economic Outcomes in Ceredigion Penfro

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Pa gamau y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn eu cymryd i wella canlyniadau economaidd yng Ngheredigion Penfro? OQ64513
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. What action is the Cabinet Minister taking to improve economic outcomes in Ceredigion Penfro? OQ64513

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Improving economic outcomes in Ceredigion Penfro means backing local businesses, strengthening rural economies, and creating better paid jobs. We're delivering our commitment to support Welsh firms, align skills with employer needs, invest in infrastructure and procurement, and ensure communities across west Wales share in economic growth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae gwella canlyniadau economaidd yng Ngheredigion Penfro yn golygu cefnogi busnesau lleol, cryfhau economïau gwledig, a chreu swyddi sy'n talu'n well. Rydym yn cyflawni ein hymrwymiad i gefnogi cwmnïau Cymreig, alinio sgiliau ag anghenion cyflogwyr, buddsoddi mewn seilwaith a chaffael, a sicrhau bod cymunedau ledled gorllewin Cymru yn rhannu twf economaidd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, thank you for your response. Yesterday, you told this Chamber that new defence-related investment decisions should, where possible, wait for your ethical defence investment framework. Yet Ceredigion Penfro should be benefiting directly from the £50 million defence growth deal, with Ministry of Defence Aberporth offering skilled jobs, investment and opportunities for local business. So, a simple question, Minister: are the defence growth deal and Aberporth both exempt from that pause? And if not, can you guarantee that not one job or contract, and not one pound of investment in Ceredigion Penfro will be lost or delayed as a result? West Wales needs certainty and investment now, not another framework standing in the way. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, diolch am eich ymateb. Ddoe, fe ddywedoch chi wrth y Siambr y dylai penderfyniadau buddsoddi newydd sy'n gysylltiedig ag amddiffyn aros lle bo'n bosibl am eich fframwaith ar gyfer buddsoddi moesegol mewn amddiffyn. Ond dylai Ceredigion Penfro elwa'n uniongyrchol o'r fargen twf amddiffyn gwerth £50 miliwn, gyda'r Weinyddiaeth Amddiffyn yn Aberporth yn cynnig swyddi medrus, buddsoddiad a chyfleoedd i fusnesau lleol. Felly, cwestiwn syml, Weinidog: a yw'r fargen twf amddiffyn ac Aberporth ill dau wedi'u heithrio o'r saib hwnnw? Ac os na, a allwch chi warantu na fydd un swydd neu gontract, na'r un bunt o fuddsoddiad yng Ngheredigion Penfro yn cael eu colli neu eu hoedi o ganlyniad? Mae angen sicrwydd a buddsoddiad ar orllewin Cymru nawr, nid fframwaith arall sy'n sefyll yn y ffordd. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm grateful to the Member for his question. I think I set it out clearly yesterday that we, obviously, are working at pace on the framework. The framework, actually, is a solid foundation for us to work with the sector in Wales, and we'll be working with companies in the sector as part of the process of developing it. Where there are decisions that—. We are trying—. Obviously, where it's possible to defer, partly out of respect for this Senedd, really—. But where it's not possible, in situations where decisions, for practical reasons, have to be made before the framework is finalised, we have allowed that exceptional flexibility, partly for the reasons that the Member describes, that we do not want to lose opportunities in cases that, actually, would be well within the framework. So, we have that flexibility, and I can assure him, as the economy Minister, I will be mindful of the need to use that flexibility where necessary.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n ddiolchgar i'r Aelod am ei gwestiwn. Rwy'n credu fy mod wedi nodi'n glir ddoe ein bod ni, yn amlwg, yn gweithio'n gyflym ar y fframwaith. Mae'r fframwaith, mewn gwirionedd, yn sylfaen gadarn i ni weithio gyda'r sector yng Nghymru, a byddwn yn gweithio gyda chwmnïau yn y sector yn rhan o'r broses o'i ddatblygu. Lle mae penderfyniadau sydd—. Rydym yn ceisio—. Yn amlwg, lle mae'n bosibl gohirio, yn rhannol o barch at y Senedd hon, mewn gwirionedd—. Ond lle nad yw'n bosibl, mewn sefyllfaoedd lle mae'n rhaid gwneud penderfyniadau, am resymau ymarferol, cyn i'r fframwaith gael ei gwblhau, rydym wedi caniatáu hyblygrwydd eithriadol, yn rhannol am y rhesymau y mae'r Aelod yn eu disgrifio, sef nad ydym am golli cyfleoedd mewn achosion a fyddai'n bendant o fewn y fframwaith mewn gwirionedd. Felly, mae gennym yr hyblygrwydd hwnnw, a gallaf ei sicrhau, fel Gweinidog yr economi, y byddaf yn ymwybodol o'r angen i ddefnyddio'r hyblygrwydd hwnnw lle bo angen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae cwestiwn 5 [OQ64492] gan Tom Montgomery wedi'i dynnu'n ôl. Felly, cwestiwn 6—Anna Nicholl.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Question 5 [OQ64492] by Tom Montgomery has been withdrawn. Therefore, question 6—Anna Nicholl.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: National Energy Strategy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. Sut y bydd y Gweinidog Cabinet yn sicrhau bod manteision strategaeth ynni genedlaethol newydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn cael eu cadw o fewn cymunedau lleol? OQ64542
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. How will the Cabinet Minister ensure that the benefits of the Welsh Government's new national energy strategy are retained within local communities? OQ64542

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We are determined that the communities hosting energy developments are genuine beneficiaries. The national energy strategy will identify the clean energy that Wales needs and how more of this can be owned through minimum community ownership requirements and investment from the new Welsh public energy company.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym yn benderfynol fod y cymunedau sy'n cynnal datblygiadau ynni yn fuddiolwyr go iawn. Bydd y strategaeth ynni genedlaethol yn nodi'r ynni glân sydd ei angen ar Gymru a sut y gellir perchnogi mwy ohono trwy isafswm o ofynion perchnogaeth gymunedol a buddsoddiad gan gwmni ynni cyhoeddus newydd Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. I welcome this Government's commitment to a renewable energy strategy that retains value in Welsh communities. The net-zero economy is already a significant and high-value component of the Welsh economy. There are particular opportunities in Ceredigion Penfro, with 1,600 jobs in the sector in Pembrokeshire alone already, and billions set to be invested in upcoming projects. This ranges from successful community-owned projects, such as Cwm Arian, to large-scale initiatives, like the Celtic Freeport.

Net zero is now an integral part of Welsh industry, and we've got huge potential to develop this further. The transition to net zero is a major economic opportunity, but I also welcome what the Minister has said here, that there needs to be a proper, planned strategy as to how we do this, both spatially and to balance the benefits for our economy, our communities and the environment. So, could the Cabinet Minister describe, as more energy infrastructure is developed in our rural communities, how Government will now ensure genuine benefit through local ownership jobs and skills and lower energy bills?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Rwy'n croesawu ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth hon i strategaeth ynni adnewyddadwy sy'n cadw gwerth yng nghymunedau Cymru. Mae'r economi sero net eisoes yn elfen arwyddocaol ac uchel ei gwerth yn economi Cymru. Mae cyfleoedd arbennig yng Ngheredigion Penfro, gyda 1,600 o swyddi yn y sector yn sir Benfro yn unig eisoes, a biliynau ar fin cael eu buddsoddi mewn prosiectau sydd ar y ffordd. Maent yn amrywio o brosiectau cymunedol llwyddiannus, fel Cwm Arian, i fentrau mawr, fel y Porthladd Rhydd Celtaidd.

Mae sero net bellach yn rhan annatod o ddiwydiant Cymru, ac mae gennym botensial enfawr i ddatblygu hyn ymhellach. Mae'r trawsnewid i sero net yn gyfle economaidd mawr, ond rwyf hefyd yn croesawu'r hyn y mae'r Gweinidog wedi'i ddweud yma, fod angen strategaeth briodol, wedi'i chynllunio ar gyfer sut y gwnawn hyn, yn ofodol ac i gydbwyso'r manteision i'n heconomi, ein cymunedau a'r amgylchedd. Felly, a allai'r Gweinidog Cabinet ddisgrifio, wrth i fwy o seilwaith ynni gael ei ddatblygu yn ein cymunedau gwledig, sut y bydd y Llywodraeth nawr yn sicrhau budd gwirioneddol trwy berchnogaeth leol, swyddi a sgiliau, a biliau ynni is?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm really grateful for the question—part of an emerging theme this afternoon. It's such an important opportunity for us nationally and locally to make sure that we create an energy system where we benefit from the energy resources that we have. We can do that at different scales; we can do it through the Welsh public energy company at a larger scale, publicly owned, delivering benefit across the whole of Wales, for the people of Wales; we can do it through supporting community ownership, of which there are some good examples in the Member's constituency already. One of the reasons for doing that is precisely to get to grips with the energy costs problem that we face. Wales has some of the highest energy costs relatively compared to other parts of the UK. The UK has some of the highest energy costs in Europe. There's good evidence that community ownership actually is a means by which you can begin to deliver lower costs to households. And similarly, a publicly owned energy company, which is free not to follow the market price in energy, but to say, 'Let's actually engage in contracts with large-scale industrial users in Wales to create a Welsh energy advantage using our renewable energy resources, but for the benefit of our economy', that's precisely why we're creating a Welsh public energy company, and we're supporting public ownership and local ownership in a variety of ways at different scales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n wirioneddol ddiolchgar am y cwestiwn—rhan o thema sy'n dod i'r amlwg y prynhawn yma. Mae'n gyfle mor bwysig i ni, yn genedlaethol ac yn lleol, i sicrhau ein bod yn creu system ynni lle rydym yn elwa ar yr adnoddau ynni sydd gennym. Gallwn wneud hynny ar raddfeydd gwahanol; gallwn ei wneud drwy gwmni ynni cyhoeddus Cymru ar raddfa fwy, cwmni sy’n eiddo cyhoeddus ac sy'n darparu budd i Gymru gyfan ac i bobl Cymru; gallwn ei wneud drwy gefnogi perchnogaeth gymunedol, ac mae enghreifftiau da o hynny eisoes yn etholaeth yr Aelod. Un o'r rhesymau dros wneud hynny yn benodol yw er mwyn mynd i'r afael â'r broblem costau ynni a wynebwn. Cymru sydd â rhai o'r costau ynni uchaf, o gymharu â rhannau eraill o'r DU. Y DU sydd â rhai o'r costau ynni uchaf yn Ewrop. Ceir tystiolaeth dda fod perchnogaeth gymunedol yn ffordd o ddechrau sicrhau costau is i aelwydydd. Ac yn yr un modd, cwmni ynni sy'n eiddo cyhoeddus, sy'n rhydd i beidio â dilyn pris y farchnad o ran ynni, ond yn hytrach i ddweud, 'Gadewch inni ymrwymo i gontractau gyda defnyddwyr diwydiannol mawr yng Nghymru i greu mantais ynni i Gymru gan ddefnyddio ein hadnoddau ynni adnewyddadwy, ond er budd ein heconomi', dyna'n union pam ein bod yn creu cwmni ynni cyhoeddus i Gymru, ac yn cefnogi perchnogaeth gyhoeddus a pherchnogaeth leol mewn amrywiaeth o ffyrdd ac ar raddfeydd gwahanol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I welcome the Welsh Government's guidance published in June on behind-the-meter energy systems, and I was pleased to see the Government recognising the potential for businesses to generate, use and sell locally produced energy. These are exactly the sorts of arrangements that can deliver real economic benefit to Welsh communities and ensure that solar panels are installed on industrial units rather than prime agricultural land.

I have heard from business owners who tell me that the financial return from exporting surplus electricity to the grid can be low, that it's so low that it simply does not provide enough incentive to install solar panels on large commercial or industrial buildings. Suppliers setting their own export tariffs turns this on its head. So, can the Minister outline what they are doing to actively promote private-wire and licence-exempt arrangements, allowing businesses to sell surplus power directly to neighbouring businesses at an agreed price?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy’n croesawu canllawiau Llywodraeth Cymru a gyhoeddwyd ym mis Mehefin ynghylch systemau ynni y tu ôl i'r mesurydd, ac roeddwn yn falch o weld y Llywodraeth yn cydnabod y potensial i fusnesau gynhyrchu, defnyddio a gwerthu ynni a gynhyrchir yn lleol. Dyma'n union y mathau o drefniadau a all ddod â budd economaidd gwirioneddol i gymunedau yng Nghymru a sicrhau bod paneli solar yn cael eu gosod ar unedau diwydiannol yn hytrach nag ar dir amaethyddol o'r radd flaenaf.

Clywais gan berchnogion busnesau sy'n dweud wrthyf y gall yr enillion ariannol o allforio trydan dros ben i'r grid fod yn isel, ei fod mor isel fel nad yw'n darparu digon o gymhelliant i osod paneli solar ar adeiladau masnachol neu ddiwydiannol mawr. Mae cyflenwyr sy'n gosod eu tariffau allforio eu hunain yn troi hyn ar ei ben. Felly, a all y Gweinidog amlinellu beth y maent yn ei wneud i fynd ati'n weithredol i hyrwyddo trefniadau gwifrenni preifat ac a eithrir rhag trwydded, gan ganiatáu i fusnesau werthu pŵer dros ben yn uniongyrchol i fusnesau cyfagos am bris wedi’i gytuno?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm really grateful to the Member for his question. He's absolutely right: I think that private-wire, behind-the-meter opportunities are actually one of the ways in which we can do what I just described, really, which is to create that energy advantage, particularly in the context of businesses. Because it can be done, there is a means to do it, but we've got to get organised to see where we can build that out at scale to facilitate businesses, because if they can avoid the network costs—. Although there's been some movement from the UK Government on network costs to large industrial users, by and large, there's still a huge network cost element. If we can devise different ways, it could be on-site microgeneration in some circumstances; in larger scales, there could be local energy systems, which are behind the wire, which could actually provide low-cost energy for a wide range of businesses. There's some work we've got to do with some of the stakeholders in order to ensure that the arrangement that you just described in terms of connection, maybe with the grid, can be part of it. So, we're working on it. It's absolutely one of the areas where, if we work smart, we could build that Welsh energy advantage, which will be such a critical determinant of our economic success.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n wirioneddol ddiolchgar i'r Aelod am ei gwestiwn. Mae'n hollol gywir: rwy'n credu bod cyfleoedd gwifrenni preifat, y tu ôl i'r mesurydd yn un o'r ffyrdd y gallwn gyflawni'r hyn a ddisgrifiais nawr, sef creu mantais ynni, yn enwedig yng nghyd-destun busnesau. Oherwydd fe ellir ei wneud, mae'r dulliau ar gael i'w wneud, ond mae angen inni gael pethau mewn trefn er mwyn gweld ble y gallwn ehangu hynny ar raddfa fawr er budd busnesau, oherwydd os gallant osgoi’r costau rhwydwaith—. Er bod Llywodraeth y DU wedi symud rhywfaint ar gostau rhwydwaith i ddefnyddwyr diwydiannol mawr, at ei gilydd, mae elfen enfawr o gostau rhwydwaith o hyd. Os gallwn geisio dyfeisio dulliau gwahanol, fel microgynhyrchu ar y safle mewn rhai amgylchiadau; ar raddfa fwy, gallai systemau ynni lleol sy'n gweithredu y tu ôl i'r wifren ddarparu ynni cost isel i ystod eang o fusnesau. Mae angen inni gydweithio â rhai o'r rhanddeiliaid i sicrhau y gall y trefniant a ddisgrifioch chi mewn perthynas â chysylltedd, â'r grid efallai, fod yn rhan ohono. Felly, rydym yn gweithio ar hynny. Yn sicr, mae'n un o'r meysydd lle gallwn, drwy weithio'n ddoeth, greu'r fantais ynni Gymreig honno, a fydd yn ffactor mor allweddol yn ein llwyddiant economaidd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 7. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet roi diweddariad am berfformiad Banc Datblygu Cymru? OQ64545
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 7. Will the Cabinet Minister provide an update on the performance of the Development Bank of Wales? OQ64545

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Development Bank of Wales continues to deliver finance and investment support to businesses across Wales. The bank has reported strong performance during the year and remains a key economic development partner. Its 2025-26 annual report will be published later this month, setting out its full performance and economic impact.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Banc Datblygu Cymru yn parhau i ddarparu cymorth ariannu a buddsoddi i fusnesau ledled Cymru. Mae'r banc wedi adrodd am berfformiad cryf yn ystod y flwyddyn ac yn parhau i fod yn bartner datblygu economaidd allweddol. Cyhoeddir ei adroddiad blynyddol ar gyfer 2025-26 yn ddiweddarach y mis hwn, gan amlinellu ei berfformiad llawn a'i effaith economaidd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: While of course I support ethical guidelines of conduct for the Development Bank of Wales, I worry about the politicisation of the bank and that investment decisions are based more off the whims of the Welsh Government rather than sensible financial criteria. For example, climate change is now a political priority that's been forced on the bank by the Government to meet mad net-zero targets. In the programme for government announced yesterday, we heard new economic criteria and possibly restrictions on defence investments for the bank. We have already had plenty of controversy with the bank in recent years, with concerns over political donations and alleged blacklisting of certain businesses. Can the Minister confirm whether the new defence ethical framework announced yesterday will apply to the Development Bank of Wales, and, if so, when? And will the Government publish a consolidated ethical and policy criteria that the development bank is expected to follow so that businesses and the Senedd can now understand how investment decisions are being made and scrutinise any further changes? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Er fy mod yn cefnogi canllawiau ymddygiad moesegol ar gyfer Banc Datblygu Cymru wrth gwrs, rwy’n poeni am wleidyddoli’r banc a’r ffaith bod penderfyniadau buddsoddi yn fwy seiliedig ar fympwyon Llywodraeth Cymru nag ar feini prawf ariannol synhwyrol. Er enghraifft, mae newid hinsawdd bellach yn flaenoriaeth wleidyddol a orfodwyd ar y banc gan y Llywodraeth er mwyn cyrraedd targedau sero net gwallgof. Hefyd, yn y rhaglen lywodraethu a gyhoeddwyd ddoe, clywsom am feini prawf economaidd newydd ac o bosibl, cyfyngiadau ar fuddsoddiadau amddiffyn ar gyfer y banc. Rydym eisoes wedi gweld cryn ddadlau ynghylch y banc yn y blynyddoedd diweddar, gyda phryderon ynghylch rhoddion gwleidyddol a honiadau fod busnesau penodol wedi'u gosod ar restr ddu. A all y Gweinidog gadarnhau y bydd y fframwaith moesegol newydd ar gyfer amddiffyn a gyhoeddwyd ddoe yn berthnasol i Fanc Datblygu Cymru, ac os felly, pryd? Ac a fydd y Llywodraeth yn cyhoeddi set gyfunol o feini prawf moesegol a pholisi y disgwylir i’r banc datblygu eu dilyn, fel bod busnesau a’r Senedd yn gallu deall sut y gwneir penderfyniadau buddsoddi a chraffu ar unrhyw newidiadau pellach? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I intend to issue the bank's remit letter in the coming weeks, which will set out clear priorities for the bank, supporting this Government's ambitions for investment, productivity and growth. That's a standard approach that every Government uses. There's nothing to see there. It's how every Government relates to arm's-length bodies, setting out the way in which the arm's-length body can deliver to the wider ambitions of the Government, particularly in the economic sphere.

Of course, we would expect the ethical framework that we are setting out in the defence sector to be cross-Government. It's there to govern the use of public money, including by the development bank, and it will also govern the development agency. Again, it's fairly normal. There are policies around fair work, for example. You would expect these to be reflected across the whole range of agencies.

I was at the launch of the development bank's Economic Intelligence Wales 'Productivity Heroes' report, and there's fantastic news here; let's remind ourselves of that. Over 1,700 high-growth firms are delivering higher productivity, higher employment and higher profits for those businesses so that they can continue to reinvest in their future trajectory of growth. I recognise scrutiny is an important part of our work here, but also let's not lose the opportunity to celebrate Welsh economic success. Because there are great things happening in Wales, and some of it is down to the work of the development bank.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n bwriadu cyhoeddi llythyr cylch gwaith y banc yn ystod yr wythnosau nesaf, ac fe fydd yn nodi blaenoriaethau clir i'r banc, gan gefnogi uchelgeisiau'r Llywodraeth hon ar gyfer buddsoddi, cynhyrchiant a thwf. Mae hwnnw'n ddull safonol y mae pob Llywodraeth yn ei ddefnyddio. Nid oes dim yn anarferol yn hynny. Dyma sut y mae pob Llywodraeth yn ymwneud â chyrff hyd braich, gan nodi sut y gall y corff hyd braich hwnnw gyfrannu at uchelgeisiau ehangach y Llywodraeth, yn enwedig yn y maes economaidd.

Wrth gwrs, byddem yn disgwyl i'r fframwaith moesegol a nodwn ar gyfer y sector amddiffyn fod yn drawslywodraethol. Mae yno i lywodraethu'r defnydd o arian cyhoeddus, gan gynnwys gan y banc datblygu, a bydd hefyd yn llywodraethu'r awdurdod ddatblygu. Unwaith eto, mae'n eithaf arferol. Byddech yn disgwyl i bolisïau ynghylch gwaith teg, er enghraifft, gael eu hadlewyrchu ar draws yr ystod lawn o asiantaethau.

Roeddwn i'n bresennol yn lansiad adroddiad 'Arwyr Cynhyrchiant' Dirnad Economi Cymru y banc datblygu, ac mae yna newyddion gwych yma; gadewch inni atgoffa ein hunain o hynny. Mae dros 1,700 o gwmnïau twf uchel yn cyflawni cynhyrchiant uwch, lefelau uwch o gyflogaeth ac elw uwch i'r busnesau hynny, gan eu galluogi i barhau i ailfuddsoddi yn eu llwybr twf yn y dyfodol. Rwy'n cydnabod bod craffu yn rhan bwysig o'n gwaith yma, ond hefyd, gadewch inni beidio â cholli cyfle i ddathlu llwyddiant economaidd Cymru. Oherwydd mae pethau gwych yn digwydd yng Nghymru, ac mae peth ohono'n deillio o waith y banc datblygu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. The final question to you, Minister. Question 8—Elfed Williams.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 8. What action is the Welsh Government taking to maximise the local economic opportunities arising from the Gwyndod project in Bangor Conwy Môn? OQ64550

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cydweithio'n agos gyda Great British Energy—Nuclear a Rolls-Royce SMR i sicrhau'r manteision mwyaf posibl i'r gymuned leol o Gwyndod. Rydym yn cefnogi busnesau Cymru i ddefnyddio cyfleoedd y gadwyn gyflenwi ac yn gweithio gyda phartneriaid addysg i alluogi pobl leol i ddatblygu'r sgiliau sydd eu hangen ar gyfer y prosiect.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh Government is working closely with Great British Energy—Nuclear and Rolls-Royce SMR to maximise local benefits from Gwyndod. We are helping Welsh businesses to access supply chain opportunities and working with education partners to enable local people to develop the required skills that will be required for the project.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Gweinidog Cabinet am yr ymateb. Ar fy ymweliad â safle Gwyndod yr wythnos diwethaf, roedd hi'n amlwg fod hwn nid yn unig yn gyfle i sicrhau ynni dibynadwy am ddegawdau, ond yn gyfle unwaith mewn cenedlaeth i economi Ynys Môn a'r gogledd-orllewin. Os ydym am i bobl leol elwa go iawn, mae angen dechrau paratoi nawr. Mae hynny'n golygu gweithio gyda'r colegau lleol i sicrhau prentisiaethau a'r sgiliau fydd eu hangen, ac, yn bwysig, sicrhau bod ganddynt y cyllid i wneud hynny. Mae hefyd yn golygu rhoi cyfle teg i fusnesau lleol ennill gwaith drwy'r gadwyn gyflenwi. A wnaiff y Gweinidog felly ymrwymo i sicrhau mai swyddi, sgiliau a busnesau lleol fydd wrth galon strategaeth Llywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer Gwyndod? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Cabinet Minister for that response. On my visit to the Gwyndod site last week, it was clear that this is not only an opportunity to secure energy for decades, but also a once-in-a-generation opportunity for the economy of Ynys Môn and north-west Wales. If we want local people to truly benefit, we need to start to prepare now. That means working with local colleges to ensure that apprenticeships and the required skills are in place, and, importantly, that they have the funding to deliver those. It also means giving fair opportunities to local businesses to get work through the supply chain. Will the Minister therefore commit to ensuring that jobs, skills and local businesses will be at the heart of the Welsh Government's strategy for Gwyndod? Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yn sicr, mae hwn yn gyfle euraid o ran economi Cymru gyfan, a hefyd yn rhanbarthol ac yn lleol. Rydym ni eisiau gwneud y mwyaf o'r cyfle hwnnw ar draws yr amrediad o ddimensiynau o ran sgiliau. Mae'r Sefydliad Dysgu a Gwaith wedi cael ei gomisiynu i wneud archwiliad sgiliau cenedlaethol ar gyfer Cymru. Yn y cyd-destun yma, mae GBE-N wedi cael ei wahodd i gyfrannu at y galw am dystiolaeth, fel y gall gyfynion y gweithlu penodol ar gyfer Gwyndod fod yn ganolog i'r strategaeth a ddaw yn ei sgil. Mae canolfan sgiliau niwclear Cymru a grŵp llywio wedi'u sefydlu i ddod â diwydiant, Llywodraeth Cymru, llywodraeth leol, darparwyr a chymunedau ynghyd o amgylch dull cydlynol, i sicrhau bod gyda ni y system sydd ei hangen er mwyn sicrhau bod pobl leol yn cael y mwyaf o'r cyfle sydd yno.

O ran y gadwyn gyflenwi ar gyfer busnesau lleol, bydd swyddogion Llywodraeth Cymru yn chwarae rôl ganolog mewn digwyddiad cyflenwyr Gwyndod—mae'n falch gen i geisio hysbysu hynny yn fwy eang—a fydd yn digwydd dros ddau ddiwrnod yng Ngholeg Menai yn Llangefni ar 22 a 23 Hydref, ochr yn ochr â GBE-N a Rolls-Royce SMR. Felly, mae yna lot mwy yn digwydd, ond dyma ryw fraslun o'r hyn sy'n bosib. Mae'n enghraifft arall, gan fod y penderfyniad wedi cael ei wneud, o sut mae Cymru yn bwysig nid yn unig o ran ynni adnewyddol—ac mae yna lot o gyfleoedd fanna yng ngogledd Cymru—ond ein bod ni hefyd yno ar ddechrau technoleg newydd o ran SMR ym Mhrydain, ac mae Cymru mewn safle arbennig o dda i elwa yn economaidd o hynny am genedlaethau i ddod.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Certainly, this is a golden opportunity in terms of the economy of the whole of Wales, and also regionally and locally. We want to maximise the benefits of that opportunity across the range of dimensions in terms of skills. The Learning and Work Institute has been commissioned to carry out a skills review for Wales. In this context, Great British Energy—Nuclear has been invited to contribute to the call for evidence, so that the needs of the specific workforce for Gwyndod can be at the heart of the strategy that will emerge. The nuclear skills centre and a working group has been drawn together to bring together industry, the Welsh Government, local government and community representatives around a co-ordinated approach, to ensure that we have the system that we need in place to ensure that local people can derive the maximum benefit from the opportunities available.

In terms of the supply chain for local businesses, Welsh Government officials will be playing a central role in the Gwyndod suppliers event—and I'm pleased to publicise this more widely—that will be held over two days in Coleg Menai in Llangefni, on 22 and 23 October, alongside GBE-N and Rolls-Royce SMR. So, there is a great deal of work being done, but that's an overview of what's possible. It's another example, because the decision has already been made, of Wales's importance not just in terms of renewable energy—there are many opportunities in that regard in north Wales—but that we are also there at the beginning of this new technology of SMRs in the United Kingdom, and Wales is in a very good position to benefit economically from these for generations to come.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet sicrhau bod oedolion sy'n dymuno dysgu Cymraeg yn cael mynediad at fwy o gyfleoedd i ddatblygu eu sgiliau iaith? OQ64524

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Dirprwy Weinidog Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn am y cwestiwn. Y newyddion da yw bod mwy o bobl yn dysgu Cymraeg nag erioed o'r blaen, ac mae'n braf gweld diddordeb yn tyfu ymysg pobl o bob oedran ac o bob cefndir. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn buddsoddi dros £18 miliwn yn y Ganolfan Dysgu Cymraeg Genedlaethol eleni i greu cyfleoedd i oedolion a phobl ifanc i ddysgu'r iaith. Mae'r ganolfan yn cynnig darpariaeth ar-lein, wyneb yn wyneb neu hybrid ar draws pob lefel i'w dysgwyr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for the question. The good news is that more people are learning Welsh than ever before, and it's wonderful to see interest growing amongst people of all ages and of all backgrounds. The Welsh Government is investing over £18 million in the National Centre for Learning Welsh this year to create opportunities for adults and young people to learn Welsh. The centre provides online provision, face-to-face provision and hybrid provision across all levels to its learners.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. It's widely accepted that one of the most effective ways for a child to learn the Welsh language, or any language, is through immersion. Simply put, the more Welsh a child hears and uses, the more likely they are to develop the language effectively. The trochi method, or immersion, can also foster a deeper understanding of, and a connection to, Welsh culture and history. However, for too many children, this immersion stops at the school gates. Many children come from English-speaking homes, which is the case in my home, and may have limited opportunities to hear or use Welsh within their wider communities. This is particularly prevalent in north-east Wales, where I am an elected representative. I'm regularly told that the issue is not a lack of desire to learn Welsh, but a lack of opportunities for adults to develop their language skills to a conversational standard. Will the Minister work with partner organisations and external agencies to provide additional opportunities for adult learners to use the language they have, helping to create stronger Welsh-speaking communities and in turn support the next generation of Welsh speakers?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Derbynnir yn eang mai un o'r ffyrdd mwyaf effeithiol i blentyn ddysgu'r Gymraeg, neu unrhyw iaith, yw trwy drochi. Yn syml, po fwyaf o Gymraeg y mae plentyn yn ei glywed ac yn ei ddefnyddio, y mwyaf tebygol yw hi y byddant yn datblygu'r iaith yn effeithiol. Gall y dull trochi feithrin dealltwriaeth ddyfnach hefyd o ddiwylliant a hanes Cymru, ac ymdeimlad o gysylltiad â nhw. Fodd bynnag, i ormod o blant, daw trochi o'r fath i ben wrth gatiau ysgol. Daw llawer o blant o gartrefi Saesneg eu hiaith, sy'n wir yn fy nghartref i, ac efallai mai cyfleoedd cyfyngedig a gânt i glywed neu ddefnyddio Cymraeg yn eu cymunedau ehangach. Mae hyn yn arbennig o berthnasol yng ngogledd-ddwyrain Cymru, lle rwy'n gynrychiolydd etholedig. Dywedir wrthyf yn rheolaidd nad diffyg awydd i ddysgu Cymraeg yw'r broblem, ond diffyg cyfleoedd i oedolion ddatblygu eu sgiliau iaith i safon sgwrsio. A wnaiff y Gweinidog weithio gyda sefydliadau partner ac asiantaethau allanol i ddarparu cyfleoedd ychwanegol i oedolion sy'n dysgu ddefnyddio'r iaith sydd ganddynt, gan helpu i greu cymunedau Cymraeg cryfach, a chefnogi'r genhedlaeth nesaf o siaradwyr Cymraeg?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. Thank you very much indeed. Immersion teaching has been with us in Wales for many years, and it's the proven way of ensuring that children acquire the Welsh language, the target language, in the most effective way possible. This was based on work that was done in Canada, where they have immersion programmes. We know that children from non-Welsh-speaking backgrounds acquire the Welsh language fluently through immersion schools. But what we need as well is support for the parents, like yourself, who are learning with their children. I know the national language centre does provide funding and support for parents through various programmes, so that they can learn with their children at the pace their children are developing.

This is equally important in terms of helping parents to help their children with homework, which is one of the barriers that many parents have about putting their children into Welsh-medium schools: 'How can I help with homework?' I can provide many answers to that. First, it's not their parents' homework anyway, but I could go on and on. But where they feel that they can help, learning Welsh is important and helps develop a bond between parents and their children through that second language. I think that sends a positive signal to families about the importance of bilingualism and living in a bilingual Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. Mae addysg drochi wedi bod gyda ni yng Nghymru ers blynyddoedd lawer, ac mae'n ffordd brofedig o sicrhau bod plant yn caffael y Gymraeg, yr iaith darged, yn y ffordd fwyaf effeithiol sy'n bosibl. Seiliwyd hyn ar waith a wnaed yng Nghanada, lle mae ganddynt raglenni trochi ar waith. Gwyddom fod plant o gefndiroedd di-Gymraeg yn caffael y Gymraeg yn rhugl trwy ysgolion trochi. Ond yr hyn sydd ei angen arnom hefyd yw cefnogaeth i rieni, fel chi eich hun, sy'n dysgu gyda'u plant. Gwn fod y ganolfan iaith genedlaethol yn darparu cyllid a chefnogaeth i rieni trwy amrywiol raglenni, fel y gallant ddysgu gyda'u plant ar y cyflymder y mae eu plant yn datblygu.

Mae hyn yr un mor bwysig o ran helpu rhieni i gynorthwyo eu plant gyda gwaith cartref, sy'n un o'r rhwystrau sy'n wynebu llawer o rieni wrth ystyried anfon eu plant i ysgolion cyfrwng Cymraeg: 'Sut y gallaf helpu gyda gwaith cartref?' Gallaf roi llawer o atebion i hynny. Yn gyntaf, nid gwaith cartref y rhieni ydyw beth bynnag, ond gallwn ddweud llawer am hynny. Ond lle maent yn teimlo y gallant helpu, mae dysgu Cymraeg yn bwysig ac yn helpu i feithrin cwlwm rhwng rhieni a'u plant trwy'r ail iaith honno. Credaf fod hynny'n anfon neges gadarnhaol i deuluoedd ynghylch pwysigrwydd dwyieithrwydd a byw mewn Cymru ddwyieithog.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Can the Cabinet Minister comment on what provisions are being set out by the Welsh Government to upgrade Welsh language learning facilities in my own constituency of rural Carmarthenshire? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A all y Gweinidog Cabinet wneud sylwadau ar ba ddarpariaethau sy'n cael eu gosod gan Lywodraeth Cymru i uwchraddio cyfleusterau dysgu Cymraeg yn fy etholaeth fy hun yng nghefn gwlad sir Gaerfyrddin? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llongyfarchiadau mawr am ddysgu Cymraeg. Rŷch chi'n byw, fel fi, mewn sir lle mae'r Gymraeg yn rhan bwysig o'r gymuned.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Congratulations for learning Welsh. You live, like I do, in a county where the Welsh language is an important part of the community.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Carmarthenshire, which we share in terms of our constituency, is a predominantly Welsh-speaking area, and it is great that people like you are learning the language. The national centre that I referred to earlier on provides funding, and the Welsh Government gives them £18 million to provide funding for courses that are tailored to the needs of people, whether that is in the community, in the Senedd, in workplaces, and online as well. As a former Welsh language tutor myself, I know how important it is for those courses to be available in workplaces in particular, but also in the community.

The joy of the workplace is that a place like the Senedd does give you opportunities not only to learn the language, but to use the language as well, as you have effectively done this afternoon. I would encourage all Members and all staff members in the Senedd, and other workplaces across Wales, to learn the language and be supported in a sensitive and effective way by those of us who are Welsh speakers by engaging with you and practising the language with you. Because learning Welsh is a virtuous cycle in many different ways. It's to do with confidence, it's to do with opportunity and it's to do with developing skills. That cycle needs to be continued and developed until you become fluent to use the language in all kinds of different ways in life. Da iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae sir Gaerfyrddin, etholaeth a rannwn, yn ardal lle mae'r Gymraeg yn cael ei siarad yn helaeth, ac mae'n wych fod pobl fel chi yn dysgu'r iaith. Mae'r ganolfan genedlaethol y cyfeiriais ati yn gynharach yn darparu cyllid, ac mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn rhoi £18 miliwn iddynt i ariannu cyrsiau wedi'u teilwra i anghenion pobl, boed hynny yn y gymuned, yn y Senedd, mewn gweithleoedd, ac ar-lein hefyd. Fel cyn diwtor Cymraeg fy hun, gwn pa mor bwysig yw hi fod y cyrsiau hynny ar gael yn y gweithle yn enwedig, ond hefyd yn y gymuned.

Un o fanteision y gweithle yw bod lle fel y Senedd yn rhoi cyfleoedd i chi nid yn unig i ddysgu'r iaith ond i'w defnyddio hefyd, fel rydych chi wedi'i wneud yn effeithiol y prynhawn yma. A dyna rwy'n annog yr holl Aelodau a'r holl staff yn y Senedd, a gweithleoedd eraill ledled Cymru, i'w wneud, dysgu'r iaith a chael cefnogaeth sensitif ac effeithiol gan y rhai ohonom sy'n siaradwyr Cymraeg drwy ymgysylltu â chi ac ymarfer yr iaith gyda chi. Oherwydd mae dysgu Cymraeg yn gylch rhinweddol mewn sawl ffordd wahanol. Mae'n ymwneud â hyder, cyfleoedd a datblygu sgiliau. Mae angen parhau a datblygu'r cylch hwnnw hyd nes y dowch yn rhugl a gallu defnyddio'r iaith mewn pob math o ffyrdd gwahanol mewn bywyd. Da iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Our priority is to raise standards for every child, wherever in Wales they go to school. We want to see sustained improvement in literacy and numeracy, more children and young people making good progress from where they start, and more school leavers earning useful qualifications ready for further study, training or work.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ein blaenoriaeth yw codi safonau i bob plentyn, lle bynnag y maent yn mynd i'r ysgol yng Nghymru. Rydym am weld gwelliant cynaliadwy mewn llythrennedd a rhifedd, mwy o blant a phobl ifanc yn gwneud cynnydd da o'u man cychwyn, a mwy o'r rhai sy'n gadael ysgol yn ennill cymwysterau defnyddiol yn barod ar gyfer astudio pellach, hyfforddiant neu waith.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for that response, Cabinet Minister. There are some serious concerns regarding the future of faith education in our schools in Pembrokeshire, following a number of controversial decisions that have been taken by Pembrokeshire County Council in recent months. As you may be aware, the council decided in May to remove the voluntary controlled status of Ysgol Cilgerran Church in Wales school. This was followed in June by a decision to close Manorbier Church in Wales VC School, while proposals are also being considered to discontinue Tenby Church in Wales VC Primary School.

These decisions have raised some serious concerns amongst parents, governors, church representatives and local communities about the long-term future of faith-based education in Pembrokeshire. So, Cabinet Minister, do you agree with me that no faith school should be lost or lose its status against the will of its school community? And can you tell us what action the Welsh Government is willing to take to support schools that wish to retain their faith status in Pembrokeshire and, indeed, across the whole of Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am yr ymateb hwnnw, Weinidog Cabinet. Mae pryderon difrifol ynghylch dyfodol addysg ffydd yn ein hysgolion yn sir Benfro, yn dilyn nifer o benderfyniadau dadleuol a wnaed gan Gyngor Sir Penfro yn y misoedd diwethaf. Fel y gwyddoch efallai, ym mis Mai penderfynodd y cyngor ddileu statws ysgol wirfoddol a reolir Ysgol yr Eglwys yng Nghymru Cilgerran. Dilynwyd hyn ym mis Mehefin gan benderfyniad i gau Ysgol yr Eglwys yng Nghymru Maenorbŷr, ysgol wirfoddol a reolir, tra bod cynigion dan ystyriaeth hefyd i gau Ysgol yr Eglwys yng Nghymru Dinbych-y-pysgod, ysgol wirfoddol a reolir arall.

Mae'r penderfyniadau hyn wedi codi pryderon difrifol ymhlith rhieni, llywodraethwyr, cynrychiolwyr eglwysig a chymunedau lleol am ddyfodol hirdymor addysg ffydd yn sir Benfro. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, a ydych chi'n cytuno â mi na ddylai unrhyw ysgol ffydd gael ei cholli neu golli ei statws yn erbyn ewyllys ei chymuned ysgol? A allwch chi ddweud wrthym pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn fodlon eu cymryd i gefnogi ysgolion sy'n dymuno cadw eu statws ffydd yn sir Benfro, ac ar draws Cymru gyfan, yn wir?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm aware obviously of the plans that he raises with me in terms of school organisation proposals from Pembrokeshire County Council. He has been here far longer than I have and will be equally aware that I am unable to comment on the merits or otherwise of any local authority proposals, which may later be referred to Ministers for determination.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n ymwybodol, wrth gwrs, o'r cynlluniau y mae'n eu codi gyda mi o ran cynigion trefniadaeth ysgolion Cyngor Sir Penfro. Mae wedi bod yma yn llawer hirach na mi, a bydd yr un mor ymwybodol na allaf wneud sylwadau ar rinweddau neu fel arall unrhyw gynigion gan awdurdodau lleol, a allai gael eu cyfeirio at Weinidogion i wneud penderfyniadau arnynt yn nes ymlaen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd just like to say 'thank you' to my constituency Member, because it is something that is very close to my heart—church schools. So, I just wanted to get that out there.

Policies promoting inclusive physical activity are welcome and many disabled pupils and their families continue to report barriers to meaningful participation in school sports, such as wheelchair-bound children being made to take timings for their peers rather than actively taking part. Can you therefore outline what specific measures the Welsh Government is taking to monitor participation rates amongst disabled learners, how it evaluates whether policies are translating into outcomes on the ground and whether it will commit to publishing data, so that Members can assess if disabled pupils are participating in curriculum-based sport at the same rate as their non-disabled peers? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn ddweud 'diolch' wrth fy Aelod etholaethol, gan fod hyn yn rhywbeth sy'n agos iawn at fy nghalon—ysgolion eglwysig. Felly, roeddwn eisiau nodi hynny.

Mae polisïau sy'n hyrwyddo gweithgarwch corfforol cynhwysol i'w croesawu, ac mae llawer o ddisgyblion anabl a'u teuluoedd yn parhau i nodi rhwystrau i gyfranogiad ystyrlon mewn chwaraeon ysgol, fel plant mewn cadair olwyn yn cael eu gorfodi i amseru eu cyfoedion yn hytrach na chymryd rhan weithredol. Felly, a allwch chi amlinellu pa gamau penodol y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i fonitro cyfraddau cyfranogiad ymhlith dysgwyr anabl, sut y mae'n gwerthuso i ba raddau y mae polisïau'n trosi'n ganlyniadau ar lawr gwlad ac a wnaiff ymrwymo i gyhoeddi'r data, fel y gall Aelodau asesu i ba raddau y mae disgyblion anabl yn cymryd rhan mewn chwaraeon sy'n seiliedig ar y cwricwlwm ar yr un gyfradd â'u cyfoedion nad ydynt yn anabl? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Thank you. And I too want to see all pupils in Wales being able to engage in all aspects of the curriculum, including, obviously, sport and physical activity. We know how important that is for their development, for their health, for their inclusion in school and in society, and I think I've referred in previous answers to our focus on that inclusion. We want our system and access to curriculum to be available for all our learners. I don't have to hand the numbers that she asks for, but I can look into that and share that with her. But I can assure her that all pupils will be a focus of all our work in terms of education standards and the accessibility of the curriculum for learners across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Ac rwyf innau hefyd eisiau gweld pob disgybl yng Nghymru yn gallu cymryd rhan ym mhob agwedd ar y cwricwlwm, gan gynnwys, yn amlwg, chwaraeon a gweithgarwch corfforol. Gwyddom pa mor bwysig yw hynny ar gyfer eu datblygiad, eu hiechyd, eu cynhwysiant yn yr ysgol ac yn y gymdeithas, a chredaf fy mod wedi cyfeirio mewn atebion blaenorol at ein ffocws ar y cynhwysiant hwnnw. Rydym eisiau i'n system a mynediad at y cwricwlwm fod ar gael i'n holl ddysgwyr. Nid oes gennyf y ffigurau y gofynna amdanynt wrth law, ond gallaf edrych ar hynny a rhannu hynny gyda hi. Ond gallaf roi sicrwydd iddi y bydd ein holl waith ar safonau addysg a hygyrchedd y cwricwlwm i ddysgwyr ledled Cymru yn canolbwyntio ar bob disgybl.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
