XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf nawr ar lefarwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Gweinidog Cabinet. Llefarydd Reform UK, Stephen Senior.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minister. Reform UK spokesperson, Stephen Senior.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. Cabinet Minister, let's just have a little look back over 20 years of the Programme for International Student Assessment in Wales. Back in 2006, Jane Hutt:

'we can learn from the best and most effective practice'.

We move on to Leighton Andrews, who, to his credit, had a bit of a crack at this, quite forthright. He talked about 'systemic failure'. A few more years to Huw Lewis—'no quick fixes'. Kirsty Williams, who was in post for quite a while:

'it will take time for Welsh education reforms to be reflected in PISA results'.

Well, a Liberal did get one prediction correct there. Jeremy Miles:

'a renewed national focus on reading, numeracy and science'. 

And then, obviously, a few years later, yourself:

'not where we want them'.

I should say, during that period, I actually was partly responsible for administering PISA in a couple of schools in Wales, so I know a little bit about it. It's a grim tale, Minister. It feels like groundhog day for the younger Members. Perhaps that's a film well worth watching. We feel stuck in a loop. My question is: why should we think that this Welsh Government's announcements will make any difference?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Weinidog Cabinet, gadewch inni edrych yn ôl ar 20 mlynedd o'r Rhaglen Ryngwladol Asesu Myfyrwyr yng Nghymru. Yn ôl yn 2006, dywedodd Jane Hutt:

'gallwn ddysgu o'r arferion gorau a mwyaf effeithiol'.

Symudwn ymlaen at Leighton Andrews, a aeth i'r afael â hyn, er clod iddo, ac a oedd yn eithaf di-flewyn-ar-dafod. Siaradodd am 'fethiant systemig'. Ychydig flynyddoedd yn ddiweddarach, Huw Lewis—'dim atebion cyflym'. Kirsty Williams, a oedd yn y swydd am beth amser:

'bydd yn cymryd amser i ddiwygiadau addysg Cymru gael eu hadlewyrchu yn y canlyniadau PISA'.

Wel, fe wnaeth y Democrat Rhyddfrydol ddarogan un peth yn gywir yno. Jeremy Miles:

'adnewyddu’r ffocws cenedlaethol ar ddarllen, mathemateg a gwyddoniaeth'.

Ac yna, yn amlwg, ychydig flynyddoedd yn ddiweddarach, chi eich hun:

'nid yw'r canlyniadau hyn lle'r hoffem iddynt fod'.

Dylwn ddweud, yn y cyfnod hwnnw, fy mod i mewn gwirionedd yn rhannol gyfrifol am weinyddu PISA mewn un neu ddwy o ysgolion yng Nghymru, felly rwy'n gwybod rhywfaint am hyn. Mae'n stori enbyd, Weinidog. Mae'n teimlo fel y ffilm Groundhog Day i'r Aelodau iau. Efallai fod honno'n ffilm sy'n werth ei gwylio. Rydym yn teimlo fel pe baem mewn cylch diddiwedd. Fy nghwestiwn yw: pam y dylem feddwl y bydd cyhoeddiadau'r Llywodraeth hon yng Nghymru yn gwneud unrhyw wahaniaeth?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for the gallop through PISA in Wales that I think most of us are familiar with and has got us to a place where we don't want to be. What is different about this plan is its focus on nought to 16 as the first element in that. We recognise that the very earliest years have an impact on learners' development in schools. We're tying it in very firmly with all the interventions that we are making in that space, in order that we can apply the support for those learners and for staff that is appropriate. I'm also—and this too is new—looking at a baseline for entry into schools, a year 6 indicator, which I and others will be able to be held to account for the trajectory we are making in literacy and numeracy, and we also want to see improvements in qualifications outcomes at 16.

What I am keen to do is to make live in our schools system the ability to demonstrate what we are doing, what you can hold me to account on, and the clarity that we give school staff about those expectations. The plan will be published in detail for consultation, in terms of what those expectations look like, very soon. And we will be able to see, on literacy and numeracy specifically, in which direction we are going, and that is different from the responses in the past.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am y wibdaith drwy PISA yng Nghymru, rhywbeth y credaf fod y rhan fwyaf ohonom yn gyfarwydd ag ef, ac sydd wedi ein harwain at sefyllfa nad ydym am fod ynddi. Yr hyn sy'n wahanol am y cynllun hwn yw ei ffocws ar addysg hyd at 16 oed fel yr elfen gyntaf yn hynny. Rydym yn cydnabod bod y blynyddoedd cynharaf yn cael effaith ar ddatblygiad dysgwyr mewn ysgolion. Rydym yn cysylltu hyn yn gadarn iawn â'r holl ymyriadau rydym yn eu gwneud yn y gofod hwnnw, er mwyn inni allu rhoi'r gefnogaeth briodol i'r dysgwyr hynny ac i staff. Rwyf hefyd—ac mae hyn yn newydd yn ogystal—yn edrych ar linell sylfaen ar gyfer mynediad i ysgolion, dangosydd blwyddyn 6, fel y gallaf i ac eraill gael ein dwyn i gyfrif am y trywydd rydym arno o ran llythrennedd a rhifedd, ac rydym hefyd am weld gwelliannau yng nghanlyniadau cymwysterau pobl ifanc 16 oed.

Rwy'n awyddus i gyflwyno gallu yn ein system ysgolion i ddangos yr hyn a wnawn, yr hyn y gallwch fy nwyn i gyfrif yn ei gylch, a'r eglurder rydym yn ei roi i staff ysgolion ynghylch y disgwyliadau hynny. Bydd manylion y cynllun yn cael eu cyhoeddi cyn bo hir er mwyn ymgynghori ar ffurf y disgwyliadau hynny. A byddwn yn gallu gweld, gyda llythrennedd a rhifedd yn benodol, i ba gyfeiriad rydym ni'n mynd, ac mae hynny'n wahanol i'r ymatebion yn y gorffennol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Cabinet Secretary. I hear what you're saying, but there's nothing new in baseline assessment. Perhaps it'll be different from what we've had previously. [Interruption.] Yes. I mean, we can go back to 1998, and there was the literacy and numeracy framework, which never got adopted—didn't see its way through devolution.

Putting that to one side, I'm going to talk about the Curriculum for Wales, because the Curriculum for Wales will be cited as having the potential to improve pupil outcomes. But last week, the Scottish Government announced its largest ever review of the curriculum up there in over 15 years, because of their poor PISA results. And unfortunately, for those who don't know, the Curriculum for Wales was largely based, not exclusively, but largely based on their Curriculum for Excellence in Scotland, as it was called. Its DNA runs right through our curriculum here. I describe it as the mashed potato of the curriculum—it's bland and of little nutritious value.

Minister, since we've not yet seen the impact of the new curriculum on PISA results, and Scotland has, my fear is that matters are going to get worse, and potentially a lot worse. Will you follow the lead of Scotland and announce your own review of the Welsh school curriculum?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ysgrifennydd y Cabinet. Rwy'n clywed yr hyn a ddywedwch, ond nid oes unrhyw beth newydd yn yr asesiad sylfaenol. Efallai y bydd yn wahanol i'r hyn rydym wedi'i gael o'r blaen. [Torri ar draws.] Ie. Hynny yw, gallwn fynd yn ôl i 1998, ac roedd gennych y fframwaith llythrennedd a rhifedd, na chafodd ei fabwysiadu—ni welodd ei ffordd drwy ddatganoli.

Gan roi hynny ar y naill ochr, rwy’n mynd i sôn am y Cwricwlwm i Gymru, gan y bydd y Cwricwlwm i Gymru yn cael ei grybwyll fel rhywbeth sydd â'r potensial i wella canlyniadau disgyblion. Ond yr wythnos diwethaf, cyhoeddodd Llywodraeth yr Alban ei hadolygiad mwyaf erioed o'r cwricwlwm yno mewn dros 15 mlynedd, oherwydd eu canlyniadau PISA gwael. Ac yn anffodus, i'r rhai nad ydynt yn gwybod, roedd y Cwricwlwm i Gymru wedi'i seilio'n bennaf, nid yn gyfan gwbl, ond yn bennaf, ar Gwricwlwm Rhagoriaeth yr Alban, fel y'i gelwid. Mae ei DNA yn rhedeg drwy ein cwricwlwm ni yma. Rwy’n ei ddisgrifio fel tatws stwnsh y cwricwlwm—mae'n ddi-flas ac o fawr o werth maethol.

Weinidog, gan nad ydym wedi gweld effaith y cwricwlwm newydd ar ganlyniadau PISA eto, ac mae'r Alban wedi gweld hynny, fy ofn yw y bydd pethau'n gwaethygu, ac o bosibl yn mynd yn llawer gwaeth. A wnewch chi ddilyn esiampl yr Alban a chyhoeddi eich adolygiad eich hun o gwricwlwm ysgolion Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I think, to go back to your first point, on the literacy and numeracy framework, one was introduced in Wales, but the sustained focus on it was not maintained. And I said last week that one of the factors that does make a difference in jurisdictions across the world is that sustained focus, which is what we are offering.

On Curriculum for Wales, you are right that there are similarities in the way these have evolved, but while we might learn from Scotland in some respects, you will find that a lot of the emerging research now suggests that they might very well learn from us too.

I have announced that I will begin a targeted review of the curriculum, in order that we have greater clarity around expectations regarding the content of that curriculum. I don't want to start again, because 15 years of further reform would not be helpful, and the curriculum is being applied well in very many schools—I have seen that. So, there will be a review; I will come back and explain how that will work and the timeline for it. There is a need for a review, but I think that we are not in the same place as Scotland, and that lessons work both ways.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I fynd yn ôl at eich pwynt cyntaf, ar y fframwaith llythrennedd a rhifedd, cyflwynwyd un yng Nghymru, ond ni chynhaliwyd y ffocws parhaus arno. A dywedais yr wythnos diwethaf mai un o'r ffactorau sy'n gwneud gwahaniaeth mewn awdurdodaethau ledled y byd yw'r ffocws parhaus hwnnw, sef yr hyn rydym ni'n ei gynnig.

Ar y Cwricwlwm i Gymru, rydych chi'n llygad eich lle fod tebygrwydd yn y ffordd y mae'r rhain wedi esblygu, ond er y gallem ddysgu gan yr Alban mewn rhai ffyrdd, fe welwch fod llawer o'r ymchwil sy'n dod i'r amlwg bellach yn awgrymu y gallent hwy ddysgu gennym ninnau hefyd.

Rwyf wedi cyhoeddi y byddaf yn dechrau adolygiad wedi'i dargedu o'r cwricwlwm, er mwyn inni gael mwy o eglurder o ran y disgwyliadau ynghylch cynnwys y cwricwlwm hwnnw. Nid wyf eisiau dechrau eto, gan na fyddai 15 mlynedd o ddiwygio pellach yn ddefnyddiol, ac mae'r cwricwlwm yn cael ei roi ar waith yn dda mewn llawer iawn o ysgolion—rwyf wedi gweld hynny. Felly, bydd adolygiad; fe ddof yn ôl i egluro sut y bydd yn gweithio a'r amserlen ar ei gyfer. Mae angen adolygiad, ond ni chredaf ein bod yn yr un lle â'r Alban, ac rwy'n credu bod y gwersi'n gweithio'r ddwy ffordd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Okay. Finally, you touched on qualifications at 16—I'm just going to touch on those at 18. There are those who believe that PISA results are stand-alone and don't contribute to anything in particular, because we've got GCSE and A-level results. Let's just look at A-level results, because you can't really compare them to England any longer, because both GCSEs and A-levels, whilst they're branded the same, have not got the same structure, and have not necessarily got the same gradings either.

But we do have comparative data for university entry, and I'm just going to focus on Cambridge University. This is not the complete picture, but when we look at some of the data published by Cambridge University, going back over a decade, a few things come to light. During the last three years, there were 325 applicants from Wales to Cambridge, and 21 per cent of those were ultimately successful. If we roll back a decade, we're at 260 applicants, so fewer applicants, but 30 per cent were successful. And I should point out the success rate for Scotland last year was just 12 per cent, and that's a real worry, because we've adopted that curriculum. It's the trend that matters—there are more applying, but fewer are successful.

My question to you, Minister, is: would you commission—because I've only had a snapshot there—some independent research to see whether fewer students from Wales are successful in their applications to the competitive universities and the competitive courses?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Iawn. I gloi, fe sonioch chi am gymwysterau yn 16 oed—hoffwn sôn am gymwysterau yn 18 oed. Mae rhai'n credu bod canlyniadau PISA yn sefyll ar eu pen eu hunain ac nad ydynt yn cyfrannu at unrhyw beth penodol, gan fod gennym ganlyniadau TGAU a Safon Uwch. Gadewch inni edrych ar ganlyniadau Safon Uwch, gan na allwch eu cymharu â Lloegr mwyach, gan nad oes yr un strwythur i TGAU a Safon Uwch, er bod ganddynt yr un enw, ac nid ydynt yn cael eu graddio'r un fath o reidrwydd chwaith.

Ond mae gennym ddata cymharol ar gyfer mynediad i'r brifysgol, ac rwy'n mynd i ganolbwyntio ar Brifysgol Caergrawnt. Nid dyma'r darlun cyflawn, ond pan edrychwn ar rywfaint o'r data a gyhoeddwyd gan Brifysgol Caergrawnt, gan fynd yn ôl dros ddegawd, daw rhai pethau'n amlwg. Yn y tair blynedd diwethaf, roedd 325 o ymgeiswyr o Gymru i Gaergrawnt, ac roedd 21 y cant o'r rheini'n llwyddiannus yn y pen draw. Os awn yn ôl ddegawd, rydym ar 260 o ymgeiswyr, felly llai o ymgeiswyr, ond roedd 30 y cant yn llwyddiannus. A dylwn nodi mai dim ond 12 y cant oedd y gyfradd lwyddiant ar gyfer yr Alban y llynedd, ac mae hynny'n bryder gwirioneddol, gan ein bod wedi mabwysiadu'r cwricwlwm hwnnw. Y duedd sy'n bwysig—mae mwy yn ymgeisio, ond mae llai yn llwyddiannus.

Fy nghwestiwn i chi, Weinidog, yw: a wnewch chi gomisiynu ymchwil annibynnol—gan mai dim ond ciplun rwyf wedi'i gael—i weld a oes llai o fyfyrwyr o Gymru yn llwyddiannus yn eu ceisiadau i'r prifysgolion cystadleuol a'r cyrsiau cystadleuol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
There are two points there to take up, I think. Looking at the trajectory and progression of students into post-18 and post-16 education is part, I think, of my colleague's review, and that will feature in that regard.

I think, on GCSEs and A-levels, it is important to remember that none of the pupils, the learners, who have done Curriculum for Wales have yet gone through these qualifications. So, drawing lessons about Curriculum for Wales with these particular cohorts may not be as helpful as we need at this point.

I think, also, it's important to remember that the consistency of testing—. PISA is one test and it tells us valuable things, and I want to draw on the detail and the granular detail of what that tells us, particularly how good we are at stretching our most able learners. I want to look at that and feed that knowledge and information into our plan. What is also clear, though, is that it doesn't measure everything. GCSEs measure something slightly different. A-levels, in which we perform, actually, very well, measure something else. So, I think it is important and is a responsibility to think of all these results in the round, while also being clear about what our expectations are, particularly around foundational skills, which is what our plan is about.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n credu bod dau bwynt i'w hateb yno. Rwy'n credu bod edrych ar lwybr a chynnydd myfyrwyr i addysg ôl-18 ac ôl-16 yn rhan o adolygiad fy nghyd-Aelod, a bydd hynny'n rhan o hwnnw.

Ar TGAU a Safon Uwch, rwy'n credu ei bod yn bwysig cofio nad oes unrhyw un o'r disgyblion, y dysgwyr, sydd wedi dilyn y Cwricwlwm i Gymru wedi cwblhau'r cymwysterau hyn eto. Felly, efallai na fydd dysgu gwersi am y Cwricwlwm i Gymru gyda'r carfanau penodol hyn mor ddefnyddiol ag sydd ei angen arnom ar hyn o bryd.

Hefyd, rwy'n credu ei bod yn bwysig cofio bod cysondeb profi—. Mae PISA yn un prawf ac mae'n dweud pethau gwerthfawr wrthym, a hoffwn drafod manylion yr hyn y mae hynny'n ei ddweud wrthym, yn enwedig pa mor dda rydym ni am ymestyn ein dysgwyr mwyaf galluog. Hoffwn edrych ar hynny a bwydo'r wybodaeth honno i'n cynllun. Mae'n glir hefyd, serch hynny, nad yw'n mesur popeth. Mae TGAU yn mesur rhywbeth ychydig yn wahanol. Mae Safon Uwch, lle rydym yn perfformio'n dda iawn mewn gwirionedd, yn mesur rhywbeth arall. Felly, credaf ei bod yn bwysig ac yn gyfrifoldeb i feddwl am yr holl ganlyniadau hyn yn eu cyfanrwydd, gan fod yn glir hefyd ynglŷn â beth yw ein disgwyliadau, yn enwedig o ran sgiliau sylfaenol, sef hanfod ein cynllun.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Lynne Neagle.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Labour spokesperson, Lynne Neagle.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. If I could start by respectfully saying to the Cabinet Minister that the work on age-related expectations and, indeed, a lot of what's in the literacy and numeracy plan was begun under the previous Government and therefore is a continuation of that work. But what I wanted to ask about today was school support staff. And I know you understand how vital school support staff are, and, indeed, I think they are the glue that holds the schools together. But on too many occasions, we know that school support staff are asked to help with complex medical issues in schools, including things like attending to catheters and feeding lines.

I know that guidance is being developed on supporting learners with healthcare needs, but there is a lack of clarity on when that guidance will be published. Again, I know that this is a challenging area, because it involves the interface between health and education. But it is crucial that we get that guidance in place, so that children with complex health needs don't face barriers in school, and so that school support staff aren't asked to do tasks that they're either not trained for—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Os caf ddechrau drwy ddweud yn barchus wrth y Gweinidog Cabinet fod y gwaith ar ddisgwyliadau sy'n gysylltiedig ag oedran, ac yn wir, llawer o'r hyn sydd yn y cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd, wedi dechrau o dan y Llywodraeth flaenorol, ac felly mae hyn yn barhad o'r gwaith hwnnw. Ond yr hyn roeddwn am ofyn amdano heddiw oedd staff cymorth ysgolion. A gwn eich bod yn deall pa mor hanfodol yw staff cymorth ysgolion, ac yn wir, rwy'n credu mai nhw yw'r glud sy'n dal yr ysgolion at ei gilydd. Ond ar ormod o achlysuron, gwyddom fod gofyn i staff cymorth ysgolion helpu gyda materion meddygol cymhleth mewn ysgolion, gan gynnwys pethau fel trin cathetrau a phibellau bwydo.

Gwn fod canllawiau'n cael eu datblygu ar gefnogi dysgwyr ag anghenion gofal iechyd, ond mae diffyg eglurder ynghylch pryd y caiff y canllawiau hynny eu cyhoeddi. Unwaith eto, gwn fod hwn yn faes heriol, gan ei fod yn ymwneud â'r rhyngwyneb rhwng iechyd ac addysg. Ond mae'n hanfodol fod y canllawiau hynny ar waith gennym, fel nad yw plant ag anghenion iechyd cymhleth yn wynebu rhwystrau yn yr ysgol, ac fel na ofynnir i staff cymorth ysgolion wneud tasgau nad ydynt wedi'u hyfforddi ar eu cyfer—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Can we have a question, Lynne?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A gawn ni gwestiwn, Lynne?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: —or certainly not remunerated for. When can we expect that guidance to be available?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: —neu'n sicr na chânt eu talu i'w gwneud. Pryd y gallwn ddisgwyl i'r canllawiau hynny fod ar gael?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
On one thing I do agree with you: the support staff in our schools do an enormously positive and important job. And any teacher and, indeed, any learner you talk to will attest to that. 

She's also quite right that these are issues that need to be considered across portfolios. Health in particular and arguably, also, preventative health are going to be key partners in deciding how the education system and how we support support staff, but, more crucially also, the learners, in this work. I can't give her a timeline at this point, but I can assure her that, in pursuit of the breaking down of silos that I think every Minister on this bench has mentioned over the past few weeks, that is one of the very clear areas of focus that we have. Because, again, to go back to an associated point to yours, making sure that all our learners are able to make the best progress that they can, and that they are well supported whatever their needs are, is a priority for us.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n cytuno â chi ar un peth: mae staff cymorth ein hysgolion yn gwneud gwaith hynod gadarnhaol a phwysig. A bydd unrhyw athro, ac yn wir, unrhyw ddysgwr y siaradwch â nhw'n tystio i hynny.

Mae hefyd yn llygad ei lle fod y rhain yn faterion y mae angen eu hystyried ar draws portffolios. Bydd iechyd yn benodol ac iechyd ataliol hefyd, gellid dadlau, yn bartneriaid allweddol wrth benderfynu sut y mae'r system addysg a ninnau'n cefnogi staff cymorth, ond yn bwysicach fyth hefyd, y dysgwyr, yn y gwaith hwn. Ni allaf roi amserlen iddi ar hyn o bryd, ond gallaf roi sicrwydd iddi, wrth geisio chwalu'r seilos y credaf fod pob Gweinidog ar y fainc hon wedi'u crybwyll dros yr ychydig wythnosau diwethaf, fod hynny'n un o'r meysydd ffocws clir iawn sydd gennym. Oherwydd unwaith eto, i fynd yn ôl at bwynt sy'n gysylltiedig â'ch un chi, mae sicrhau bod ein holl ddysgwyr yn gallu gwneud y cynnydd gorau a allant, a'u bod yn cael eu cefnogi'n dda beth bynnag y bo'u hanghenion, yn flaenoriaeth i ni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. You may be aware that a safeguarding letter was issued by Estyn to Ysgol Heol Goffa special school in Llanelli following the inspection last year, and that that was around issues around healthcare support in school. Now, a letter that the Cabinet Minister for health sent to one of the people who made representations about the school indicated that the guidance would be published some time in 2027, whereas your last written answer to me said that

'this work is at an early stage and...we are not yet in a position to confirm a timescale for the publication of revised guidance.'

So, there is a difference there between what two Ministers have said. Now, I entirely agree with you about the dangers of silos. And I wonder whether you would agree with me that this is not just a matter for local authorities and health boards, and that if this work is to be done, it has to be driven at Government level by the Cabinet Ministers responsible, in both health and education. What assurance can you give that you will be working closely with the health Minister's team to make sure that that interface between health and education, when it comes to children's education, is absolutely seamless?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Efallai eich bod yn ymwybodol fod llythyr diogelu wedi'i anfon gan Estyn at ysgol arbennig Heol Goffa yn Llanelli yn dilyn yr arolwg y llynedd, a'i fod yn ymwneud â materion yn gysylltiedig â chymorth gofal iechyd yn yr ysgol. Nawr, nododd llythyr a anfonodd y Gweinidog Cabinet dros iechyd at un o'r bobl a wnaeth sylwadau am yr ysgol y byddai'r canllawiau'n cael eu cyhoeddi rywbryd yn 2027, ond roedd eich ateb ysgrifenedig diwethaf chi ataf yn nodi bod

'y gwaith hwn yn ei gamau cynnar ac...nid ydym mewn sefyllfa eto i gadarnhau amserlen ar gyfer cyhoeddi canllawiau diwygiedig.'

Felly, mae gwahaniaeth yno rhwng yr hyn y mae dau Weinidog wedi'i ddweud. Nawr, rwy'n cytuno'n llwyr â chi ynglŷn â pheryglon seilos. A tybed a fyddech chi'n cytuno â mi nad mater i awdurdodau lleol a byrddau iechyd yn unig yw hwn, ac os yw'r gwaith hwn i gael ei wneud, rhaid iddo gael ei lywio ar lefel y Llywodraeth gan y Gweinidogion Cabinet sy'n gyfrifol, ym maes iechyd ac addysg. Pa sicrwydd y gallwch ei roi y byddwch yn gweithio'n agos gyda thîm y Gweinidog iechyd i sicrhau bod y rhyngwyneb rhwng iechyd ac addysg, o ran addysg plant, yn gwbl ddi-dor?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yes, that is an assurance I can absolutely give her. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wrth gwrs, gallaf roi sicrwydd llwyr iddi ynglŷn â hynny. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. Cabinet Minister, what is your view on the impact of school closures on communities, parents, teachers and learners across Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Weinidog Cabinet, beth yw eich barn ar effaith cau ysgolion ar gymunedau, rhieni, athrawon a dysgwyr ledled Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for the question. I'm afraid I have to refer you to the previous answer that I gave to your colleague, in that, obviously, these are decisions for local authorities. There are clear codes that govern the process that need to be followed in order to look at school organisation, and, particularly in relation to smaller schools, you will see a commitment in our manifesto to make sure that those codes are well applied. But I cannot, as Minister, comment on any particular plans in any local authority in Wales, as I am conscious that some of these decisions may at some point be referred to Welsh Ministers.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich cwestiwn. Mae arnaf ofn fod yn rhaid imi eich cyfeirio at yr ateb blaenorol a roddais i'ch cyd-Aelod, sef yn amlwg, fod y rhain yn benderfyniadau i awdurdodau lleol. Mae codau clir sy'n llywodraethu'r broses y mae angen ei dilyn er mwyn edrych ar drefniadaeth ysgolion, ac yn enwedig mewn perthynas ag ysgolion llai, fe welwch ymrwymiad yn ein maniffesto i sicrhau bod y codau hynny'n cael eu rhoi ar waith yn dda. Ond fel Gweinidog, ni allaf wneud sylwadau ar unrhyw gynlluniau penodol mewn unrhyw awdurdod lleol yng Nghymru, gan fy mod yn ymwybodol y gallai rhai o'r penderfyniadau hyn gael eu cyfeirio at Weinidogion Cymru maes o law.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Cabinet Minister. I appreciate the position you take on that, but, as you point out, on the process, it's important throughout that this is being adhered to properly, because communities are concerned when school closures and mergers are threatened for schools in their areas. You'll be aware, in my own constituency, that Flintshire council has proposed the merger of four schools into one superschool, with communities at the periphery of that, such as in Saltney, with St Anthony's school, and in Mold, with St David's school—where my colleague Darren Millar is the Member for—particularly concerned about the impact from the distance of the site that's being proposed.

The point here, Cabinet Minister, is that the consultation for the proposal has been rejected by more than 96 per cent of respondents. Schools are at the heart of our communities, and their closures have a particularly stark impact on rural areas, where schools serve as important community buildings and set habits of a lifetime for travel to and from school. Councils should not be imposing school closures on communities that do not want them. Instead, closures should only be considered where there's significant evidence, considerable public support and action to mitigate impacts on those communities. So, within the powers that you do have, Cabinet Minister, will you commit today to supporting parents, teachers and learners in disputes over school closures?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Rwy'n derbyn eich safbwynt ar hynny, ond fel y nodwch, o ran y broses, mae'n bwysig glynu at hyn drwy gydol yr amser, gan fod cymunedau'n pryderu pan fydd bygythiad o gau ysgolion ac uno ysgolion yn eu hardaloedd. Fe fyddwch yn ymwybodol, yn fy etholaeth i, fod Cyngor Sir y Fflint wedi cynnig uno pedair ysgol yn un uwchysgol, gyda chymunedau ar y cyrion, fel yn Saltney, gydag ysgol Sant Anthony, ac yn yr Wyddgrug, gydag ysgol Dewi Sant—ardal y mae fy nghyd-Aelod Darren Millar yn ei chynrychioli—yn arbennig o bryderus ynglŷn ag effaith pellter y safle arfaethedig.

Y pwynt yma, Weinidog Cabinet, yw bod yr ymgynghoriad ar gyfer y cynnig wedi'i wrthod gan fwy na 96 y cant o'r ymatebwyr. Mae ysgolion yn galon ein cymunedau, ac mae eu cau'n cael effaith arbennig o wael ar ardaloedd gwledig, lle mae ysgolion yn gwasanaethu fel adeiladau cymunedol pwysig ac yn sefydlu arferion gydol oes ar gyfer teithio i'r ysgol ac yn ôl. Ni ddylai cynghorau orfodi ysgolion i gau mewn cymunedau nad ydynt eisiau hynny. Yn hytrach, dim ond lle mae tystiolaeth sylweddol, cefnogaeth gyhoeddus sylweddol a chamau gweithredu i liniaru'r effeithiau ar y cymunedau hynny y dylid ystyried cau. Felly, o fewn y pwerau sydd gennych, Weinidog Cabinet, a wnewch chi ymrwymo heddiw i gefnogi rhieni, athrawon a dysgwyr mewn anghydfodau ynghylch cau ysgolion?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. I can't commit to that, for the reasons that I mentioned earlier on. But I think your question does illustrate the importance of schools in our communities, and I wouldn't dispute that for a second. They are key institutions in all our communities. We all have a vested interest in their success and in the success of the learners who are in those schools. So, while, obviously, for your constituents this will be an issue that they will want to pursue with you and with others, I will leave it there.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Ni allaf ymrwymo i hynny, am y rhesymau a nodais yn gynharach. Ond credaf fod eich cwestiwn yn dangos pwysigrwydd ysgolion yn ein cymunedau, ac ni fuaswn yn anghytuno â hynny am eiliad. Maent yn sefydliadau allweddol yn ein holl gymunedau. Mae buddiant personol gan bob un ohonom yn eu llwyddiant ac yn llwyddiant y dysgwyr yn yr ysgolion hynny. Felly, er y bydd hyn, yn amlwg, yn fater y bydd eich etholwyr eisiau mynd ar ei drywydd gyda chi a chyda phobl eraill, fe'i gadawaf yno.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i sicrhau bod gan bobl ifanc yng Nghaerdydd Penarth fynediad cyfartal at addysg ysgol uwchradd cyfrwng Cymraeg? OQ64509
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What is the Welsh Government doing to ensure that young people in Caerdydd Penarth have equal access to Welsh-medium high school education? OQ64509

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Cardiff Council is implementing its Welsh in education strategic plan to ensure sufficient Welsh-medium secondary education in all areas of Cardiff. I understand that the council is currently developing strategic, long-term options for Welsh-medium secondary school provision, and we should await the outcomes of that work.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Mae Cyngor Caerdydd yn gweithredu ei gynllun strategol Cymraeg mewn addysg i sicrhau digon o addysg uwchradd cyfrwng Cymraeg ym mhob ardal o Gaerdydd. Rwy'n deall bod y cyngor wrthi'n datblygu opsiynau strategol, hirdymor ar gyfer darpariaeth ysgolion uwchradd cyfrwng Cymraeg, a dylem aros am ganlyniadau'r gwaith hwnnw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. Diolch. I know a family in Butetown whose daughter must leave the house by 7.30 a.m. every morning to get to Glantaf high school in time for registration—just one of many young people and their families whose decision to continue Welsh-language education wasn't and isn't straightforward. Travelling through an already broken transport system from one side of the city to another is not sustainable. It is expensive and difficult for parents, and stressful for vulnerable 11-year-olds starting high school. Many who want to stay for after-school clubs can't due to the lack of safe transport options home. The lack of access to Welsh-medium education for Grangetown, Butetown and the surrounding areas disproportionately impacts those on the doorstep of this very Siambr. I stand with the campaigners who call this a social injustice. It is structural discrimination against the most multicultural communities in our city. The public sector has a duty under the Equality Act 2010 to address the imbalance, irrespective of any discussions as to the viability of Callaghan Square—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Rwy'n adnabod teulu yn Butetown y mae'n rhaid i'w merch adael y tŷ erbyn 7.30 a.m. bob bore i gyrraedd ysgol uwchradd Glantaf mewn pryd i gofrestru—dim ond un o lawer o bobl ifanc a'u teuluoedd nad oedd ac nad yw eu penderfyniad i barhau ag addysg iaith Gymraeg yn syml. Nid yw teithio drwy system drafnidiaeth sydd eisoes wedi torri o un ochr i'r ddinas i'r llall yn gynaliadwy. Mae'n ddrud ac yn anodd i rieni, ac yn peri straen i blant 11 oed agored i niwed sy'n dechrau yn yr ysgol uwchradd. Ni all llawer sydd eisiau aros i fynd i glybiau ar ôl ysgol wneud hynny oherwydd diffyg opsiynau trafnidiaeth diogel adref. Mae diffyg mynediad at addysg cyfrwng Cymraeg ar gyfer Grangetown, Butetown a'r ardaloedd cyfagos yn effeithio'n anghymesur ar y rhai sydd ar garreg drws y Siambr hon. Rwy'n cyd-sefyll gyda'r ymgyrchwyr sy'n galw hyn yn anghyfiawnder cymdeithasol. Mae'n gyfystyr â gwahaniaethu strwythurol yn erbyn y cymunedau mwyaf amlddiwylliannol yn ein dinas. Mae gan y sector cyhoeddus ddyletswydd o dan Ddeddf Cydraddoldeb 2010 i fynd i'r afael â'r anghydbwysedd, yn annibynnol ar unrhyw drafodaethau ynghylch hyfywedd Sgwâr Callaghan—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Sorry, Anthony, can we come to a question?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae’n ddrwg gennyf, Anthony, a gawn ni gwestiwn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: —as a potential site. I'm aware, Minister, that you have previously expressed support for a fourth Welsh-medium secondary school in the city. While acknowledging Cardiff Council's ongoing role, what assurances can the Minister give to local families in south Cardiff of the Welsh Government's commitment to securing a Welsh-medium secondary school in de Caerdydd? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: —fel safle posibl. Rwy'n ymwybodol, Weinidog, eich bod eisoes wedi mynegi cefnogaeth i bedwaredd ysgol uwchradd cyfrwng Cymraeg yn y ddinas. Gan gydnabod rôl barhaus Cyngor Caerdydd, pa sicrwydd y gall y Gweinidog ei roi i deuluoedd lleol yn ne Caerdydd ynghylch ymrwymiad Llywodraeth Cymru i sicrhau ysgol uwchradd cyfrwng Cymraeg yng Nghaerdydd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. The Welsh Government's commitment to developing Welsh language schools and opportunities for learners across Wales is clear. It is expressed, again, in our manifesto. We are consulting very soon in this autumn term on the broader strategy around Welsh and the implementation of the Welsh language and education Act—Deddf y Gymraeg ac Addysg (Cymru) 2025. I may not have translated that wholly accurately. That is a focus for our work as a Government, and I would invite him to look in detail at that consultation when it is issued. Additionally, we have just conducted a rapid review of the Welsh in education strategic plans that all local authorities are required to develop to demonstrate how they propose to develop these options for all learners in Cardiff and elsewhere.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr. Mae ymrwymiad Llywodraeth Cymru i ddatblygu ysgolion a chyfleoedd Cymraeg i ddysgwyr ledled Cymru’n glir. Mae wedi'i fynegi, unwaith eto, yn ein maniffesto. Byddwn yn ymgynghori cyn bo hir yn nhymor yr hydref ar y strategaeth ehangach ynghylch y Gymraeg a gweithrediad Deddf y Gymraeg ac Addysg (Cymru) 2025. Mae hynny'n ffocws ar gyfer ein gwaith ni fel Llywodraeth, a buaswn yn ei wahodd i edrych yn fanwl ar yr ymgynghoriad hwnnw pan gaiff ei gyhoeddi. Yn ogystal, rydym newydd gynnal adolygiad cyflym o'r cynlluniau strategol Cymraeg mewn addysg y mae'n ofynnol i bob awdurdod lleol eu datblygu er mwyn dangos sut y maent yn bwriadu datblygu'r opsiynau hyn ar gyfer pob dysgwr yng Nghaerdydd ac mewn mannau eraill.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, it's vitally important that Wales's unique culture is not only preserved but nurtured. Access to Welsh-medium education for those who want it will be an important part of that process. More than that, bilingualism is literally good for the brain. It leads to better executive function, better memory, problem solving, and even delays dementia onset by an average of around five years. Of course, Wales isn't the only country that recognises the importance of language in the transmission of culture. There are examples that we can learn from from across the globe. I'd be interested to know if the Welsh Government has learned or is trying to learn anything from Catalonia and the Basque region in successfully promoting bilingualism.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, mae'n hanfodol bwysig fod diwylliant unigryw Cymru nid yn unig yn cael ei gadw ond yn cael ei feithrin. Bydd mynediad at addysg cyfrwng Cymraeg i'r rhai sydd ei heisiau yn rhan bwysig o'r broses honno. Yn fwy na hynny, mae dwyieithrwydd yn dda i'r ymennydd yn llythrennol. Mae'n arwain at well gweithrediad goruchwyliol, cof gwell, gwell gallu i ddatrys problemau, a hyd yn oed yn gohirio camau cyntaf dementia am oddeutu pum mlynedd ar gyfartaledd. Wrth gwrs, nid Cymru yw'r unig wlad sy'n cydnabod pwysigrwydd iaith wrth drosglwyddo diwylliant. Mae enghreifftiau o bob cwr o'r byd y gallwn ddysgu oddi wrthynt. Hoffwn wybod a yw Llywodraeth Cymru wedi dysgu neu'n ceisio dysgu unrhyw beth gan Gatalwnia a rhanbarth Gwlad y Basg ynghylch hyrwyddo dwyieithrwydd yn llwyddiannus.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. I know my predecessors and I are very keen to learn from examples of successful bilingual countries and cultures across the world. It always strikes me as interesting that we consider this in some way unusual. In most places in the world, bilingualism is an accepted part of life—it's just the way things are. Learning from those countries, learning from those jurisdictions, has always, I think, been important to this Government and the previous one. Certainly, I can commit to continuing that interest in the way things are done elsewhere and to learn appropriately from that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Gwn fod fy rhagflaenwyr a minnau'n awyddus iawn i ddysgu oddi wrth enghreifftiau o wledydd a diwylliannau dwyieithog llwyddiannus ledled y byd. Mae bob amser yn ddiddorol i mi ein bod yn meddwl bod hyn rywsut yn anarferol. Yn y rhan fwyaf o leoedd yn y byd, mae dwyieithrwydd yn rhan dderbyniol o fywyd—dyna sut y mae pethau. Credaf fod dysgu oddi wrth y gwledydd hynny, dysgu oddi wrth yr awdurdodaethau hynny, bob amser wedi bod yn bwysig i'r Llywodraeth hon a'r un flaenorol. Yn sicr, gallaf ymrwymo i barhau â'r diddordeb hwnnw yn y ffordd y caiff pethau eu gwneud mewn mannau eraill ac i ddysgu'n briodol oddi wrth hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mae'r Aelod wedi crybwyll Gwlad y Basg. A gaf i gyfeirio'r Gweinidog tuag at ysgol Groes-wen, hefyd yng Nghaerdydd Penarth, sydd yn enghraifft arloesol yma yng Nghymru, ar fodel sydd wedi'i gymryd o gynlluniau addysg yng Ngwlad y Basg, sydd yn tyfu dwyieithrwydd drwy ddwy ffrwd, Cymraeg a Saesneg? Dwi eisiau cydnabod cefnogaeth y Gweinidog yn lleol i'r ymgyrch dros bedwaredd ysgol Gymraeg yn ne Caerdydd. Dwi hefyd yn gwerthfawrogi'r conflict personol sydd nawr yn ei rôl fel Gweinidog.

Ond, wedi dweud hynny, allaf i jest godi eto y mater yma o'r safle? Fe fydd hi'n deall yn ei rôl fel Gweinidog yr heriau ymarferol sydd yna o ran sicrhau pedwaredd ysgol, o ran twf niferoedd a chynaliadwyedd ysgolion eraill yng Nghaerdydd. Ond mae'r dyhead yna yn y cyngor a, dwi'n credu, yn y Siambr yma hefyd i weld pedwaredd ysgol i ateb y consýrn sydd wedi cael ei godi ynghylch access rhwydd ledled y ddinas i addysg Gymraeg. Felly, tra bo'r cyngor yn mynd rhagddo â'r gwaith o baratoi cynllun busnes, dwi wedi ysgrifennu ac wedi cyfeirio at yr issue hyn gyda'r safle yn Callaghan Square. Mae de Caerdydd wedi datblygu yn sylweddol a does yna ddim llawer o safleoedd—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
The Member mentioned the Basque Country. May I refer the Minister to ysgol Groes-wen, also in Caerdydd Penarth, which is an innovative example here in Wales, on a model that has been adopted from education plans in the Basque Country and which is developing bilingualism through having two streams, Welsh and English? I want to recognise the Minister's support locally for a fourth Welsh-medium secondary school in south Cardiff. I also appreciate the personal conflict that exists in her role as a Minister.

But, having said that, can I just raise once again this issue of site? She will know in her role as the Minister the practical challenges in ensuring a fourth secondary school, in terms of the growth in numbers and the sustainability of other schools in Cardiff. But that aspiration exists in the council and in this Chamber, I believe, to see a fourth secondary school to respond to some of the concerns that have been raised on easy access across the city to Welsh-medium education. So, whilst the council proceeds with the preparatory work in terms of a business plan, I have written on the issue of the site at Callaghan Square. Cardiff south has developed a great deal and there are not many sites—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Huw, can you move to a question, please?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae Elin Jones newydd adael y Siambr, yn anffodus. A wnewch chi weithio gyda'r Gweinidog cyllid i dynnu'r safle yna oddi ar y farchnad—safle sy'n eiddo i Lywodraeth Cymru—fel bod yr opsiwn yna i ddatgloi ysgol Gymraeg yn ne Caerdydd?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Elin Jones has just left the Chamber, unfortunately. Will you work with the Minister for finance to take that site off the market, as it belongs to the Welsh Government, so that the option exists and we can unlock a new secondary school in south Cardiff?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. Diolch yn fawr am gydnabod hefyd fod y sefyllfa hon yn gallu bod yn ddyrys i rywun fel fi, sydd hefyd, wrth gwrs, yn byw yn Grangetown. Ond, wedi dweud hynny, rwy'n ymwybodol, rwy’n credu, fod yr Aelod wedi ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog cyllid, ac rwy'n hyderus y bydd hi'n ateb hynny yn fuan. Fe fyddwn i yn nodi ar y pwynt hwn nad ydyn ni wedi cael gohebiaeth swyddogol gan Gyngor Caerdydd ar y mater hwn, ac efallai fod hwnna’n rhywbeth i edrych arno fe.

Ond i fynd nôl at fy ateb blaenorol, mae datblygu addysg Gymraeg ym mhob awdurdod lleol yng Nghymru, cynnydd yn nifer y disgyblion sydd yn gallu cael mynediad rhwydd at addysg gyfrwng Gymraeg, a bod dysgwyr yn ein system ni, pa bynnag ysgol maen nhw wedi mynd iddi hi, yn gadael yr ysgol yn 16 yn siaradwyr hyderus o'r Gymraeg yn ganolog i weledigaeth y Llywodraeth hon ar gyfer y Gymraeg. Bydd yna ymgynghori helaeth iawn ar yr amryw ffyrdd y byddwn ni'n symud i'r cyfeiriad hwnnw dros gyfnod y Llywodraeth hon.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much. Thank you also for recognising that this situation can be quite complex for someone like me, who also, of course, lives in Grangetown. However, having said that, I'm aware, I think, that the Member wrote to the Minister for finance, and I am confident that she will respond shortly. I would like to note on this point that we haven't received any correspondence officially from Cardiff Council on this issue, and perhaps that would be something to look at.

But to return to my previous answer, developing Welsh-medium education in every local authority in Wales, increasing the number of pupils who can have easy access to Welsh-medium education, and that learners in our system, whatever school they attended, can leave the school aged 16 as confident, proficient Welsh speakers are central to this Government's vision for the Welsh language. There will be very extensive consultation on the variety of ways in which we will be moving in that direction through the period of this Government term.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Everybody should have access to Welsh-medium education. Sadly, I missed out on this when I was growing up and I'm now having to learn as an adult. At the moment, our constituency of Caerdydd Penarth is only served by one Welsh-medium secondary school. We know that communities in the south of Cardiff are travelling further to access Welsh-medium education, which is disincentivising parents and guardians from sending their children to Welsh-medium education. I am mindful, though, that responsibility for the planning of local schools does rest with local authorities and that statutory procedures have to be followed. So, I was wondering if the Cabinet Minister could confirm what communication she's had with Cardiff Council in relation to this matter.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Dylai pawb gael mynediad at addysg cyfrwng Cymraeg. Yn anffodus, ni chefais hyn pan oeddwn yn tyfu i fyny, ac rwy'n gorfod dysgu fel oedolyn nawr. Ar hyn o bryd, dim ond un ysgol uwchradd cyfrwng Cymraeg sydd yn ein hetholaeth ni, Caerdydd Penarth. Gwyddom fod cymunedau yn ne Caerdydd yn teithio ymhellach i gael mynediad at addysg cyfrwng Cymraeg, sy'n datgymell rhieni a gwarcheidwaid rhag anfon eu plant i addysg cyfrwng Cymraeg. Rwy'n ymwybodol, serch hynny, mai awdurdodau lleol sy'n gyfrifol am gynllunio ysgolion lleol a bod yn rhaid dilyn gweithdrefnau statudol. Felly, roeddwn yn meddwl tybed a allai'r Gweinidog Cabinet gadarnhau pa gyfathrebiad y mae hi wedi eu cael â Chyngor Caerdydd mewn perthynas â'r mater hwn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Specifically—I think I mentioned this in my earlier answer—on the location, I haven't. But, of course, alongside what is happening is that we are looking at the Welsh in education strategic plans, and these have now been submitted, the review has concluded, and we will be communicating with all local authorities in October to discuss the progress that has been made and the national picture that we can glean from those plans aligned, then, with the priority we as a Government give to developing Welsh language education. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn benodol—credaf imi grybwyll hyn yn fy ateb cynharach—nid wyf wedi trafod y lleoliad. Ond wrth gwrs, ochr yn ochr â'r hyn sy'n digwydd, rydym yn edrych ar y cynlluniau strategol Cymraeg mewn addysg, ac mae'r rhain bellach wedi'u cyflwyno, mae'r adolygiad wedi'i gwblhau, a byddwn yn cyfathrebu â phob awdurdod lleol ym mis Hydref i drafod y cynnydd a wnaed a'r darlun cenedlaethol y gallwn ei gael o'r cynlluniau hynny, wedi'i alinio, felly, â'r flaenoriaeth rydym yn ei rhoi fel Llywodraeth i ddatblygu addysg Gymraeg. Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Improving educational standards for learners in Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr, and indeed in every community across Wales, is a core mission of this Government. Last week, I published the foundational literacy and numeracy plan, which represents an important first step in our vision for an education system that works for all learners and supports key partners to succeed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Mae gwella safonau addysgol i ddysgwyr ym Mhontypridd Cynon Merthyr, ac yn wir ym mhob cymuned ledled Cymru, yn genhadaeth graidd i'r Llywodraeth hon. Yr wythnos diwethaf, cyhoeddais y cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol, sy'n gam cyntaf pwysig yn ein gweledigaeth ar gyfer system addysg sy'n gweithio i bob dysgwr ac yn cefnogi partneriaid allweddol i lwyddo.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Cabinet Minister. We can't ignore the clear link between social deprivation, child poverty and educational attainment, which I think are all areas that successive Governments have failed to address. The latest PISA results should be a wake-up call for this Government. Wales is bottom of the UK in maths, reading and science. Maths has fallen significantly, and your own Government acknowledges that Wales has constantly lagged behind other UK nations. But nowhere should that failure concern us more than in communities such as the one I represent in Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr. Your own deprivation figures show that 83 per cent of areas in Merthyr Tydfil are among the most educationally deprived areas of Wales. So, Cabinet Minister, those statistics aren't just something to read on a Government spreadsheet; they represent children whose future opportunities depend upon the education they receive today.

Now, I appreciate the PISA records aren't yours to own, as they're based on 2025 results, and Labour spent years reforming the curriculum, changing qualifications and moving away. However, it's not lost on anyone on this side of the Chamber that Plaid Cymru supported that, so you can no longer blame the system you inherited. So, the question is: do you commit to working across Government departments to ensure that socially deprived areas in Wales are prioritised to make sure that we close the gap between those and any educational achievements for PISA? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog Cabinet. Ni allwn anwybyddu'r cysylltiad clir rhwng amddifadedd cymdeithasol, tlodi plant a chyrhaeddiad addysgol, sydd, yn fy marn i, oll yn feysydd y mae Llywodraethau olynol wedi methu mynd i'r afael â nhw. Dylai'r canlyniadau PISA diweddaraf fod yn rhybudd i'r Llywodraeth hon. Cymru sydd ar y gwaelod yn y DU mewn mathemateg, darllen a gwyddoniaeth. Mae mathemateg wedi gostwng yn sylweddol, ac mae eich Llywodraeth eich hun yn cydnabod bod Cymru wedi bod ar ei hôl hi'n gyson o gymharu â gwledydd eraill y DU. Ond dylai'r methiant hwn beri'r pryder mwyaf i ni mewn cymunedau fel yr un rwy'n ei chynrychioli ym Mhontypridd Cynon Merthyr. Mae eich ffigurau amddifadedd eich hun yn dangos bod 83 y cant o ardaloedd ym Merthyr Tudful ymhlith yr ardaloedd mwyaf difreintiedig yn addysgol yng Nghymru. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, nid rhywbeth i'w ddarllen ar un o daenlenni'r Llywodraeth yn unig yw'r ystadegau hynny; maent yn cynrychioli plant y mae eu cyfleoedd yn y dyfodol yn dibynnu ar yr addysg a gânt heddiw.

Nawr, rwy'n sylweddoli nad chi sy'n gyfrifol am y canlyniadau PISA, gan eu bod yn seiliedig ar ganlyniadau 2025, a threuliodd Llafur flynyddoedd yn diwygio'r cwricwlwm, yn newid cymwysterau ac yn ymbellhau. Fodd bynnag, nid oes unrhyw un ar yr ochr hon i'r Siambr wedi anghofio bod Plaid Cymru wedi cefnogi hynny, felly ni allwch feio'r system a etifeddwyd gennych mwyach. Felly, y cwestiwn yw: a ydych chi'n ymrwymo i weithio ar draws adrannau'r Llywodraeth i sicrhau bod ardaloedd o amddifadedd cymdeithasol yng Nghymru yn cael eu blaenoriaethu er mwyn sicrhau ein bod yn cau'r bwlch rhyngddynt ac unrhyw gyflawniadau addysgol ar gyfer PISA? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. Spending time litigating previous Governments' records is not how I intend to use my time, because I want to move forward from here, so I have no intention of starting today. I think you will see a commitment across this Government particularly to tackle the impact of poverty on children across Wales, both in schools and more broadly in our society. That's why the childcare offer, for example, is such a focus for us. You will see, in each of our portfolios, I think, a strategic commitment to tackling the impact of poverty in Wales on children and on societies and on families across our country, including in your constituency.

You will see also, in the foundational literacy and numeracy plan that I published last week, that there is in that explicitly a commitment to looking at our success in delivering this plan in terms of how well we are getting to grips with those gaps, because some of these statistics are alarmingly and stubbornly high and have been for a very long time. And I hope you will have heard, over the past few weeks, how important that is, in all its complexity, for all of us.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr. Nid dadlau ynghylch hanes Llywodraethau blaenorol yw'r ffordd rwy'n bwriadu defnyddio fy amser, gan fy mod am symud ymlaen o fan hyn, felly nid oes gennyf unrhyw fwriad o ddechrau heddiw. Rwy'n credu y gwelwch ymrwymiad ar draws y Llywodraeth hon i fynd i'r afael yn arbennig ag effaith tlodi ar blant ledled Cymru, mewn ysgolion ac yn ehangach yn ein cymdeithas. Dyna pam y mae'r cynnig gofal plant, er enghraifft, yn ffocws mor bwysig i ni. Rwy'n credu y gwelwch ymrwymiad strategol ym mhob un o'n portffolios i fynd i'r afael ag effaith tlodi yng Nghymru ar blant ac ar gymdeithasau ac ar deuluoedd ledled ein gwlad, gan gynnwys yn eich etholaeth chi.

Fe welwch hefyd, yn y cynllun llythrennedd a rhifedd sylfaenol a gyhoeddais yr wythnos diwethaf, fod ymrwymiad penodol ynddo i edrych ar ein llwyddiant wrth gyflawni'r cynllun hwn o ran pa mor dda yr awn i'r afael â'r bylchau hynny, gan fod rhai o'r ystadegau hyn yn frawychus ac yn ystyfnig o uchel ac wedi bod felly ers amser maith. Ac rwy'n gobeithio y byddwch wedi clywed, dros yr ychydig wythnosau diwethaf, pa mor bwysig yw hynny, yn ei holl gymhlethdod, i bob un ohonom.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae addysg Gymraeg yn llwyddo pan fydd pob plentyn yn dysgu yn y ffordd sydd yn addas iddyn nhw fel unigolion. Mae ŵyr gyda fi sydd yn byw gydag awtistiaeth. Mae mewn ysgol Gymraeg ac mae'n cael cefnogaeth ffantastig, mae'n rhaid imi ddweud—hollol wych—a dwi'n ddiolchgar iawn am hynny. Yn anffodus, dyw pob teulu ddim yn yr un sefyllfa, achos dyw hyn ddim yn wir mewn ardaloedd eraill yng Nghymru. Ni ddylai cael anghenion dysgu ychwanegol olygu bod yn rhaid i ddysgwyr roi'r gorau i'w hawl i gael addysg drwy'r Gymraeg. Dylai pob plentyn a pherson ifanc, beth bynnag fo'u hanghenion dysgu, allu cael mynediad at y cymorth a'r ddarpariaeth sydd eu hangen arnynt drwy gyfrwng y Gymraeg. Felly, a wnaiff Gweinidog y Cabinet roi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf am gynlluniau'r Llywodraeth i sicrhau bod darpariaeth anghenion dysgu ychwanegol drwy gyfrwng y Gymraeg yr un mor hygyrch, cynhwysfawr ac effeithiol â'r ddarpariaeth drwy gyfrwng y Saesneg?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh-medium education succeeds when every child learns in the way that's appropriate to them as individuals, of course. I have a grandson who's living with autism. He's in a Welsh-medium school and he's getting excellent support, I have to say—it's excellent and I'm very grateful for that. Unfortunately, not every family is in that same situation, because this isn't true across other areas in Wales. Having additional learning needs shouldn't mean that learners have to give up their right to Welsh-medium education. Every child and young person, whatever their needs, should be able to access the support and provision that they need through the medium of Welsh. So, will the Cabinet Minister provide an update on the Welsh Government's plans to ensure that additional learning needs provision through the medium of Welsh is just as accessible, inclusive and effective as the provision through the medium of English?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Rwy'n credu ein bod ni wedi clywed yn yr wythnosau diwethaf gan rai o'n cydweithwyr hefyd amboutu'r impact personol mae rhai o'r dewisiadau anodd yma wedi'i gael pan nad oes modd cael y gefnogaeth addas ar gyfer anghenion dysgu ychwanegol yn y Gymraeg, ac i ddysgwyr mewn ysgolion Cymraeg hefyd. Rydyn ni wedi edrych yn fanwl ar hwn, yn benodol ar y ddarpariaeth hynny o safbwynt dysgwyr mewn ysgolion Cymraeg, ac mae e'n sicr yn flaenoriaeth i ni. Mi allaf i anfon mwy o fanylion ynglŷn ag amserlen, efallai, iddi y tu allan i'r cyfarfod y prynhawn yma, ond rwy'n moyn ei sicrhau hi ein bod ni yn sylweddoli bod hwn yn broblem benodol ac mae cefnogi teuluoedd sydd yn dymuno cael addysg Gymraeg i'w plant a chael y gefnogaeth sydd ei hangen arnyn nhw yn sicr yn rhywbeth y byddwn ni yn barnu ein llwyddiant arno fe dros gyfnod y Llywodraeth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. I think we've heard in the past weeks from some of our colleagues as well about the personal impact that some of these difficult decisions have had when suitable support hasn't been available for ALN through the medium of Welsh, and for learners in Welsh-medium schools as well. We have looked at this in detail, in particular at that provision from the perspective of students in Welsh-medium schools, and certainly it is a priority for us. I can send you some more details about the timetable, perhaps, outside of this meeting this afternoon, but I want to assure you that we do realise that this is a particular problem and that supporting families who would like to have Welsh-medium education for their children and get that support that they need is certainly something that we would judge our success on over the period of this Government.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Dwi'n ymwybodol iawn o amser, a hoffwn i gyrraedd o leiaf hanner ffordd drwy'r cwestiynau. Felly, fyddaf i ddim yn gallu galw unrhyw gyfraniadau ychwanegol, yn anffodus. Symudwn ymlaen i gwestiwn 5—Andrew R.T. Davies.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. I'm highly aware of time and I would like to get at least halfway through the questions. So, I won't be able to call any additional contributions from here on in, unfortunately. We'll move to question 5—Andrew R.T. Davies.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. What action is the Cabinet Minister taking to support school budgets in Pen-y-bont Bro Morgannwg? OQ64533

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Decisions on the level of funding available to schools are made by each local authority as part of their overall budget setting. I'm committed to working collaboratively with local authorities to consider how education funding is used most effectively.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae penderfyniadau ar lefel y cyllid sydd ar gael i ysgolion yn cael eu gwneud gan bob awdurdod lleol yn rhan o'r broses o osod eu cyllideb gyffredinol. Rwy'n ymrwymedig i weithio ar y cyd ag awdurdodau lleol i ystyried sut i ddefnyddio cyllid addysg yn y ffordd fwyaf effeithiol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, what are your asks of the finance Minister in supporting your portfolio? Many schools in Pen-y-bont Bro Morgannwg are in a deficit situation and are looking to you as a new Minister to secure additional funding in the current budget settlement round. So, could you identify, given your experience in the education sector, especially as a former representative of the National Association of Head Teachers, what your asks are of the finance Minister, so that headteachers can have confidence that they will see more resource in the new financial year?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, am beth y gofynnwch gan y Gweinidog cyllid i gefnogi eich portffolio? Mae llawer o ysgolion ym Mhen-y-bont Bro Morgannwg mewn diffyg ac yn troi atoch chi fel Gweinidog newydd i sicrhau cyllid ychwanegol yn y setliad cyllideb presennol. Felly, a allech chi nodi, o ystyried eich profiad yn y sector addysg, yn enwedig fel cyn-gynrychiolydd Cymdeithas Genedlaethol y Prifathrawon, am beth y gofynnwch i'r Gweinidog cyllid, er mwyn i benaethiaid fod yn hyderus y gwelant fwy o adnoddau yn y flwyddyn ariannol newydd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. I can assure him certainly that education is a priority for the entire Government, and that I, as an advocate for support for it in all aspects, will be delivering with determination. I think it is important to note the funding settlements that are in place at the moment. He may remember, in the last budget negotiations, that an additional £112.8 million was sourced for local government, which resulted in £6.56 billion in core funding for local authorities, and that is an increase of 4.5 per cent.

I know that there are issues around funding in education and in our schools. I am determined to work with all partners to try and resolve some of the more outstanding issues, and assure him that the Vale of Glamorgan and all the other 21 authorities will be in my mind as I do that, because, as I said, we recognise the importance of education, and success in delivering for our learners is a key measure of our success as a Government.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Gallaf ei sicrhau yn bendant fod addysg yn flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth gyfan, ac y byddaf i, fel eiriolwr dros gefnogaeth i bob agwedd arni, yn cyflawni gyda phenderfyniad. Rwy'n credu ei bod yn bwysig nodi'r setliadau cyllido sydd ar waith ar hyn o bryd. Efallai y cofiwch, yn y trafodaethau cyllidebol diwethaf, fod £112.8 miliwn ychwanegol wedi'i ddarparu ar gyfer llywodraeth leol, a arweiniodd at £6.56 biliwn mewn cyllid craidd i awdurdodau lleol, sef cynnydd o 4.5 y cant.

Gwn fod problemau'n gysylltiedig â chyllid mewn addysg ac yn ein hysgolion. Rwy'n benderfynol o weithio gyda'r holl bartneriaid i geisio datrys rhai o'r materion mwyaf dwfn, a'i sicrhau y bydd Bro Morgannwg a'r 21 awdurdod arall i gyd yn fy meddwl wrth imi wneud hynny, oherwydd, fel y dywedais, rydym yn cydnabod pwysigrwydd addysg, ac mae llwyddiant ein gallu i gyflawni ar gyfer ein dysgwyr yn fesur allweddol o'n llwyddiant fel Llywodraeth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. How does the Welsh Government support adult learners in Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr? OQ64486

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Deputy Minister for Skills and Tertiary Education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Dirprwy Weinidog Sgiliau ac Addysg Drydyddol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Wel, diolch am y cwestiwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for the question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Welsh Government supports adult learners across Wales through investment in further education, community learning, personal learning accounts, employability programmes and essential skills provision. Working with local providers, including Coleg y Cymoedd and Merthyr college in your constituency, we are helping adults to gain skills, progress in work and access lifelong learning opportunities.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cefnogi oedolion sy'n dysgu ledled Cymru drwy fuddsoddi mewn addysg bellach, dysgu cymunedol, cofnodion dysgu personol, rhaglenni cyflogadwyedd a darpariaeth sgiliau hanfodol. Gan weithio gyda darparwyr lleol, yn cynnwys Coleg y Cymoedd a choleg Merthyr yn eich etholaeth chi, rydym yn helpu oedolion i ennill sgiliau, i gamu ymlaen mewn gwaith a chael mynediad at gyfleoedd dysgu gydol oes.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, Deputy Minister, it is, of course, Adult Learners Week this week, and I was really grateful to the adult learners who met me in Coleg y Cymoedd in Aberdare on Monday, who spoke about their experiences of re-entering education.

We know that there's considerable demand for adult education, but figures that I've seen from Adult Learning Wales suggest that demand in 2026-27 outstrips their funding by almost 10 percent, and that means that around 850 potential learners are missing out. I'm told by Adult Learning Wales that they could put additional funding to use immediately, upskilling workers and allowing for more flexible delivery. So, how is Welsh Government making meeting this demand a priority?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, Ddirprwy Weinidog, mae'n Wythnos Addysg Oedolion yr wythnos hon, wrth gwrs, ac roeddwn yn ddiolchgar iawn i'r oedolion a gyfarfu â mi yng Ngholeg y Cymoedd yn Aberdâr ddydd Llun, ac a siaradodd am eu profiadau o ailymuno ag addysg.

Gwyddom fod galw sylweddol am addysg oedolion, ond mae'r ffigurau a welais gan Addysg Oedolion Cymru yn awgrymu bod y galw yn 2026-27 bron 10 y cant yn fwy na'r hyn y mae  eu cyllid yn darparu ar ei gyfer, ac mae hynny'n golygu bod tua 850 o ddysgwyr posibl ar eu colled. Mae Addysg Oedolion Cymru yn dweud wrthyf y gallent ddefnyddio cyllid ychwanegol ar unwaith, gan uwchsgilio gweithwyr a chaniatáu mwy o hyblygrwydd yn y ddarpariaeth. Felly, sut y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn gwneud bodloni'r galw hwn yn flaenoriaeth?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Education and Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, again, you make a really important point. Let me just agree with you that, with adult learning, the benefits are so wide-ranging. It supports the development of skills, improves health and well-being and is a catalyst for social engagement and integration. It also shows that well-paid work, through developing skills, is the best route out of poverty, and helping people to gain the skills they need to thrive and work is a clear priority for this Welsh Government. And I'm looking forward to the awards ceremony this evening as well, the Inspire! adult learning awards. It is, for me—and I've been to many over recent years—one of the highlights of the year, when you see the outstanding achievements of learners whose passion, commitment and dedication I think demonstrates the transformative power of lifelong learning.

But, to answer your question briefly, we are keeping a very close watch on the increased enrolments in FE colleges in particular. We know that that creates funding pressures for FE colleges. And I'm aware that Medr have given £6.25 million in this financial year, which straddles half the academic year, to help FE colleges, but we are monitoring the situation with Medr, and, if funding allows, we will try and support the FE sector but also adult learning in general as best as we can.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, unwaith eto, rydych chi'n gwneud pwynt pwysig iawn. Gadewch imi gytuno â chi fod y manteision sy'n deillio o addysg oedolion mor bellgyrhaeddol. Mae'n cefnogi datblygu sgiliau, yn gwella iechyd a lles, ac yn sbardun i ymgysylltu ac integreiddio cymdeithasol. Mae hefyd yn dangos mai gwaith ar gyflog da, drwy ddatblygu sgiliau, yw'r ffordd orau allan o dlodi, ac mae helpu pobl i ennill y sgiliau sydd eu hangen arnynt i ffynnu a gweithio yn flaenoriaeth glir i'r Llywodraeth hon yng Nghymru. Ac rwy'n edrych ymlaen at y seremoni wobrwyo heno hefyd, gwobrau addysg oedolion 'Ysbrydoli!'. I mi—ac rwyf wedi mynychu llawer ohonynt yn y blynyddoedd diweddar—dyma un o uchafbwyntiau'r flwyddyn, pan welwch gyflawniadau rhagorol dysgwyr y mae eu hangerdd, eu hymrwymiad a'u hymroddiad yn dangos pŵer trawsnewidiol dysgu gydol oes.

Ond i ateb eich cwestiwn yn fyr, rydym yn cadw golwg agos iawn ar y cynnydd yng nghofrestriadau colegau addysg bellach yn enwedig. Rydym yn gwybod bod hynny'n creu pwysau ariannu i golegau addysg bellach. Ac rwy'n ymwybodol fod Medr wedi rhoi £6.25 miliwn yn y flwyddyn ariannol hon, sy'n rhychwantu hanner y flwyddyn academaidd, i helpu colegau addysg bellach, ond rydym yn monitro'r sefyllfa gyda Medr, ac os bydd cyllid yn caniatáu, byddwn yn ceisio cefnogi'r sector addysg bellach ac addysg oedolion yn gyffredinol hefyd gystal ag y gallwn.
