XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cynnig NDM9301 Lynne Neagle [R]

Cynnig bod y Senedd:

1. Yn nodi'r argyfwng parhaus o bobl ifanc nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant a'r effaith andwyol hirdymor y mae hyn yn ei chael ar eu hiechyd, eu henillion a'u cyfleoedd bywyd yn y dyfodol.

2. Yn croesawu'r cynnydd yn nifer y bobl ifanc sy'n cymryd rhan mewn colegau addysg bellach ledled Cymru, gan gynnwys y galw cynyddol am addysg alwedigaethol a thechnegol.

3. Yn cydnabod y pwysau ariannol ar golegau i gwrdd â'r lefelau uchaf erioed o alw y flwyddyn academaidd hon.

4. Yn galw ar Lywodraeth Cymru i gyhoeddi asesiad effaith ar gyfer peidio ag ariannu'r cynnydd mewn cyfranogiad yn y blynyddoedd academaidd 2026-27 a 2027-28, ac i ymrwymo i flaenoriaethu addysg bellach yn y broses o osod cyllideb 2027-28.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Motion NDM9301 Lynne Neagle [R]

To propose that the Senedd:

1. Notes the continuing crisis of young people not being in education, employment or training and the long-term scarring impact this has on their future health, earnings and life chances.

2. Welcomes the increased participation of young people in further education colleges across Wales, including rising demand for vocational and technical education.

3. Recognises the financial pressures on colleges to meet record levels of demand this academic year.

4. Calls on the Welsh Government to publish an impact assessment for not funding increased participation in the 2026-27 and 2027-28 academic years, and to commit to prioritising further education in the 2027-28 budget-setting process.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Addysg Bellach
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Welsh Labour Debate: Further education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. Can I draw Members' attention to my register of interests and the fact that I'm an adult learner in Cardiff and Vale College?

Today, I want to focus on one of Wales's greatest success stories and one that too often does not receive the recognition it deserves: our further education colleges. Across Wales, colleges are changing lives every day. For young people, they are the chance to take that first step after school and progress to work, an apprenticeship or to university. For adults, they are access to lifelong learning, and for employers, they are the support they need to upskill their workforce, improve productivity and compete for new business.

Across Wales, colleges have shown that they are innovators and are ready to meet new challenges. In north Wales, they are helping to drive the new tertiary alliance with our university sector. In south-west Wales, the four colleges have come together to form a new partnership to maximise opportunities from the Celtic Freeport. And in south-east Wales, colleges have pioneered new ways of supporting learners, including the junior apprenticeship programme I was so proud to support in Government. The evidence of their value is clear.

This year, colleges across Wales have seen record levels of demand, with every college reporting increased participation. More learners than ever are choosing further education as their route into skills, qualifications and careers. Demand is particularly strong in vocational and technical subjects, such as construction, engineering and health and care—precisely the sectors we know are critical to Wales's future prosperity. Colleges are also providing opportunities for those who need them most. They are supporting thousands of learners who are returning to education, improving literacy and numeracy and rebuilding confidence after difficult experiences in school or elsewhere.

This is a Welsh success story, but it is fragile, and more learners means more pressure on space and on budgets. And the pressures are urgent, with ColegauCymru estimating the sector will have enrolled a record 50,000 young people this academic year. At a time when we are in the middle of a crisis with the number of young people who are not in employment, education or training, and when we are weeks away from the publication of the Milburn review, there has never been a more important time to invest in further education.

So, rising participation is a good news story. It is a sign that colleges are succeeding, it is a sign that further education is delivering for Wales and it is an opportunity for Wales. However, record demand brings with it a significant challenge. We know that funding has not kept pace with participation. Last year, I was able to put an additional £20 million in to support participation in the sector, but this year, the shortfall is estimated by both the sector and by Medr to be around £23.5 million. To stop even more learners missing out on places, colleges have been forced to make the difficult choice of moving funding from adult part-time provision to pay for full-time learner numbers. This all means there are around 5,000 learners who are studying for whom the sector isn't receiving any funding. Hundreds of learners have not got a place at all, and hundreds more did not get their first-choice course because of a shortage of places.

As well as pressure on places, it is also stretching vital support, such as well-being services, mental health support, financial hardship provision and learner travel. I hope Members know my own personal commitment to supporting learners with additional learning needs, and I am concerned about the impact of underfunding. Early data from ColegauCymru suggests an additional 65 per cent increase in learners with individual development plans, and it is essential that they can access the funding they need.

Looking ahead, the pressures in 2027-28 are even greater. The sector estimates that at least £40 million will be required in the 2027-28 academic year simply to maintain existing participation levels and respond to sustained learner demand. Pay and other inflationary pressures will push this even higher. If that funding is not available, the consequences could be significant. We risk more young people becoming disconnected from education and training. We risk job losses in the sector and cuts to support services. We risk cutting progression routes to our universities and stopping young people from taking that first step on their career paths. And we risk cutting off the skills pipeline that businesses need to compete and grow.

That is why this motion is important. It calls for a clear assessment of the consequences of failing to fund increased participation in further education. We need to understand the impact on learner pathways, on not in education, employment or training levels, on staff, on learner support services, and on progression into employment and higher education. Further education colleges take a much greater proportion of learners from lower income backgrounds. It is vital that we understand the impact on deprived communities across Wales. For many young people, particularly those with the fewest qualifications, college is their second chance, and they have very few options if they don't get a place. We owe it to the young people and to the adults who rely on further education to ensure our colleges have the resources they need.

Llywydd, this debate is ultimately about opportunity. When people want to learn, train and improve their prospects, our response should not be to limit opportunity, our response should be to understand the consequences of inaction and ensure that Wales continues to invest in success. Our colleges have demonstrated their value. They are helping young people realise their potential, supporting employers and strengthening communities across Wales. Now we must ensure that the resources available to them reflect the vital role they play. I urge Members to support our motion. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. A gaf i dynnu sylw'r Aelodau at fy nghofrestr buddiannau a'r ffaith fy mod yn ddysgwr sy'n oedolyn yng Ngholeg Caerdydd a'r Fro?

Heddiw, hoffwn ganolbwyntio ar un o lwyddiannau mwyaf Cymru ac un nad yw'n aml yn cael y gydnabyddiaeth y mae'n ei haeddu: ein colegau addysg bellach. Ledled Cymru, mae colegau'n newid bywydau bob dydd. I bobl ifanc, maent yn gyfle i gymryd y cam cyntaf hwnnw ar ôl ysgol a chamu ymlaen i waith, prentisiaeth neu brifysgol. I oedolion, maent yn cynnig mynediad at ddysgu gydol oes, ac i gyflogwyr, y cymorth sydd ei angen arnynt i uwchsgilio eu gweithlu, gwella cynhyrchiant a chystadlu am fusnes newydd.

Ledled Cymru, mae colegau wedi dangos eu bod yn arloeswyr ac yn barod i wynebu heriau newydd. Yng ngogledd Cymru, maent yn helpu i gynnal y gynghrair drydyddol newydd gyda'n sector prifysgolion. Yn y de-orllewin, mae'r pedwar coleg wedi dod ynghyd i ffurfio partneriaeth newydd i wneud y mwyaf o'r cyfleoedd a ddarperir drwy'r Porthladd Rhydd Celtaidd. Ac yn y de-ddwyrain, mae colegau wedi arloesi ffyrdd newydd o gefnogi dysgwyr, gan gynnwys y rhaglen prentisiaethau iau yr oeddwn mor falch o'i chefnogi pan oeddwn yn y Llywodraeth. Mae'r dystiolaeth o'u gwerth yn glir.

Eleni, mae colegau ledled Cymru wedi gweld y lefelau uchaf erioed o alw, gyda phob coleg yn nodi cynnydd mewn cyfranogiad. Mae mwy o ddysgwyr nag erioed yn dewis addysg bellach fel eu llwybr tuag at sgiliau, cymwysterau a gyrfaoedd. Mae'r galw'n arbennig o gryf mewn pynciau galwedigaethol a thechnegol, fel adeiladu, peirianneg ac iechyd a gofal—yr union sectorau y gwyddom eu bod yn hanfodol i ffyniant Cymru yn y dyfodol. Mae colegau hefyd yn darparu cyfleoedd i'r rhai sydd eu hangen fwyaf. Maent yn cefnogi miloedd o ddysgwyr sy'n dychwelyd at addysg, yn gwella llythrennedd a rhifedd ac yn ailadeiladu hyder ar ôl profiadau anodd yn yr ysgol neu mewn mannau eraill.

Mae wedi bod yn llwyddiant yng Nghymru, ond mae'n fregus, ac mae mwy o ddysgwyr yn golygu mwy o bwysau ar ofod ac ar gyllidebau. Ac mae'r pwysau'n fater brys, gyda ColegauCymru yn amcangyfrif y bydd y sector wedi cofrestru 50,000 o bobl ifanc yn y flwyddyn academaidd hon, sef y nifer uchaf erioed. Ar adeg pan fo gennym argyfwng o ran nifer y bobl ifanc nad ydynt mewn cyflogaeth, addysg na hyfforddiant, ac wythnosau tan y bydd adolygiad Milburn yn cael ei gyhoeddi, ni fu erioed adeg bwysicach i fuddsoddi mewn addysg bellach.

Felly, mae cyfranogiad cynyddol yn newyddion da. Mae'n arwydd fod colegau'n llwyddo, mae'n arwydd fod addysg bellach yn cyflawni i Gymru ac mae'n gyfle i Gymru. Fodd bynnag, mae'r galw uchaf erioed yn creu her sylweddol. Gwyddom nad yw'r cyllid wedi dal i fyny â chyfranogiad. Y llynedd, darperais £20 miliwn yn ychwanegol i gefnogi cyfranogiad yn y sector, ond eleni, mae'r sector a Medr yn amcangyfrif bod y diffyg oddeutu £23.5 miliwn. Er mwyn atal hyd yn oed mwy o ddysgwyr rhag colli lleoedd, mae colegau wedi gorfod gwneud y dewis anodd o symud cyllid o ddarpariaeth ran-amser i oedolion i dalu am niferoedd y dysgwyr amser llawn. Mae hyn oll yn golygu bod oddeutu 5,000 o ddysgwyr yn astudio nad yw'r sector yn derbyn unrhyw gyllid ar eu cyfer. Mae cannoedd o ddysgwyr wedi methu cael lle o gwbl, ac ni chafodd cannoedd yn rhagor le ar y cwrs a oedd yn ddewis cyntaf iddynt oherwydd prinder lleoedd.

Yn ogystal â phwysau ar leoedd, mae hefyd yn rhoi pwysau ar gymorth hanfodol, fel gwasanaethau lles, cymorth iechyd meddwl, darpariaeth caledi ariannol a theithio gan ddysgwyr. Rwy'n gobeithio bod yr Aelodau'n gwybod am fy ymrwymiad personol fy hun i gefnogi dysgwyr ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, ac rwy'n pryderu am effaith tanariannu. Mae data cynnar gan ColegauCymru yn awgrymu cynnydd ychwanegol o 65 y cant yn nifer y dysgwyr sydd â chynlluniau datblygu unigol, ac mae'n hanfodol eu bod yn gallu cael mynediad at y cyllid sydd ei angen arnynt.

Wrth edrych ymlaen, mae'r pwysau yn 2027-28 hyd yn oed yn fwy. Mae'r sector yn amcangyfrif y bydd angen o leiaf £40 miliwn ym mlwyddyn academaidd 2027-28 i gynnal lefelau cyfranogiad presennol ac ymateb i alw parhaus gan ddysgwyr. Bydd pwysau cyflog a phwysau chwyddiant arall yn gwthio hyn hyd yn oed yn uwch. Os nad yw'r cyllid hwnnw ar gael, gallai'r canlyniadau fod yn sylweddol. Rydym mewn perygl o weld mwy o bobl ifanc yn ymddieithrio rhag addysg a hyfforddiant. Rydym mewn perygl o golli swyddi yn y sector a thoriadau i wasanaethau cymorth. Rydym mewn perygl o dorri llwybrau cynnydd i'n prifysgolion ac atal pobl ifanc rhag cymryd y cam cyntaf ar eu llwybrau gyrfa. Ac rydym mewn perygl o dorri'r ddarpariaeth o sgiliau sydd eu hangen ar fusnesau i gystadlu a thyfu.

Dyna pam y mae'r cynnig hwn yn bwysig. Mae'n galw am asesiad clir o ganlyniadau methu ariannu mwy o gyfranogiad mewn addysg bellach. Mae angen inni ddeall yr effaith ar lwybrau dysgwyr, ar niferoedd y bobl nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant, ar staff, ar wasanaethau cymorth i ddysgwyr, ac ar gamu ymlaen i gyflogaeth ac addysg uwch. Mae colegau addysg bellach yn derbyn cyfran lawer mwy o ddysgwyr o gefndiroedd incwm is. Mae'n hanfodol ein bod yn deall yr effaith ar gymunedau difreintiedig ledled Cymru. I lawer o bobl ifanc, yn enwedig y rhai sydd â'r nifer lleiaf o gymwysterau, coleg yw eu hail gyfle, ac ychydig iawn o opsiynau sydd ganddynt os na chânt le. Ein dyletswydd i'r bobl ifanc ac i'r oedolion sy'n dibynnu ar addysg bellach yw sicrhau bod yr adnoddau sydd eu hangen arnynt gan ein colegau.

Lywydd, yn y pen draw, mae a wnelo'r ddadl â chyfle. Pan fydd pobl eisiau dysgu, hyfforddi a gwella eu rhagolygon, ni ddylem ymateb drwy gyfyngu ar gyfleoedd, dylem ymateb drwy ddeall canlyniadau diffyg gweithredu a sicrhau bod Cymru'n parhau i fuddsoddi mewn llwyddiant. Mae ein colegau wedi dangos eu gwerth. Maent yn helpu pobl ifanc i wireddu eu potensial, yn cefnogi cyflogwyr ac yn cryfhau cymunedau ledled Cymru. Nawr, mae’n rhaid inni sicrhau bod yr adnoddau sydd ar gael iddynt yn adlewyrchu'r rôl hanfodol y maent yn ei chwarae. Rwy'n annog yr Aelodau i gefnogi ein cynnig. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Welsh Labour Debate: Further education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. I move the amendment in the name of my colleague Paul Davies. I'd like to thank Labour colleagues for bringing this debate forward today; a really important issue has been highlighted in this Chamber. I certainly support the opening remarks by their spokesperson here this afternoon. We know, don't we, that the latest Welsh Government figures show that 17 per cent of 16 to 24-year-olds in Wales were not in employment, education or training in the year ending December 2025. That's an increase of 5.5 percentage points in just one year. That's nearly one in every five young adults that we would meet not in education, employment or training. Quite stark figures. Sometimes, Llywydd, we get so used to these numbers being bandied about, but it's pretty shocking, actually, that nearly one in five young adults are not in education, training or in employment.

We must remember that behind every one of those numbers is a young person who wants to get on with their life, to continue education, develop their skills, or step into the world of work. When they're unable to do so, as this motion recognises, the consequences can be long-lasting, affecting their health, earnings, life chances and ultimately affecting our society as a whole. That's why the role that further education colleges play in tackling this is so, so important. I know the Welsh Government do understand this, but what we need to see today as a result of this motion is action off the back of words.

We know, of course, that record numbers of learners are choosing further education colleges as a route into qualifications, skills and careers, with every college in Wales reporting an increase in participation this academic year. Minister, you'll be pleased to hear, of course, that I visited a college on Friday just gone. It was Coleg Cambria's Yale site in Wrexham. They had me playing pickleball in one of their sports halls, they had me observing some pickle being prepared in the restaurant, and I hope to God that there's no footage of me getting in a pickle on the dance floor in their dance studio.

What they told me about also was the increased demand that they're seeing at their own site there in Wrexham, which I know reflects colleges across Wales experiencing the same kinds of pressures. We know that there's particularly a strong demand in vocational and technical education areas, such as construction, engineering and healthcare, which happen to be precisely the sectors where Wales needs skilled workers today. And as we've already heard in the opening remarks, Llywydd, the increased demand is not being met with the funding that is required.

We've already heard about the 5,000 learners across colleges in Wales who are studying without the associated funding to properly support them. In my own constituency, there are around 1,000 students currently in colleges without the funding in place to provide the support that they need. We've failed to fund that demand. We risk fewer places, fewer courses and less support for the young people that I talked about right at the opening of my contribution today, which are those young people who aren't in work, those young people who aren't currently in training and aren't able to see that future that we need them to be able to see.  The risk is a NEET crisis getting worse and not better.

But funding is only one part of the solution, and that's why our Welsh Conservative amendment is so important, and that's why we're calling on the Welsh Government to encourage that greater collaboration between those colleges and the private sector. Because we do have a bit of a strange situation in Wales at the moment, where many of us across the Chamber will be aware that employers are struggling to find people with the right skills while young people are struggling to find clear routes into work. So, something's not quite matching up. I'm sure that the Minister will speak about the skills audit that's under way, and I really hope that business is right at the heart of that thinking as well. Because employers can help those colleges understand the skills that industries need, colleges can give businesses access to the next generation of talent, and learners can gain the experience and understanding of the workplace that make the difference between finishing education and finding a career.

An example of this, Llywydd, is in the defence sector. We know that UK defence investment in Wales accounts for around about £1 billion a year into our Welsh industries. So, why wouldn't we want Welsh colleges to work with the defence sector to make sure our young people are equipped to take advantage of the opportunities that are there for them in the future? The same applies to construction, engineering, energy and many other sectors on which Wales's economy depends so importantly.

So, this isn't about telling young people what career they should choose, it's about giving them the opportunity, the experience and the choice to be able to move into a world of work. The Welsh Conservatives believe that every learner should be able to choose a path that works for them. That's why it's important that this motion and our amendment is supported. We need properly funded colleges, stronger links between education and industry and a Welsh Government focused on creating opportunities for our young people. Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Rwy'n gwneud y gwelliant yn enw fy nghyd-Aelod Paul Davies. Hoffwn ddiolch i'm cyd-Aelodau Llafur am gyflwyno'r ddadl hon heddiw; mae mater pwysig iawn wedi cael sylw yn y Siambr hon. Rwy'n sicr yn cefnogi'r sylwadau agoriadol gan eu llefarydd y prynhawn yma. Gwyddom, oni wyddom, fod ffigurau diweddaraf Llywodraeth Cymru yn dangos nad oedd 17 y cant o bobl 16 i 24 oed yng Nghymru mewn cyflogaeth, addysg na hyfforddiant yn y flwyddyn a ddaeth i ben ym mis Rhagfyr 2025. Mae hynny'n gynnydd o 5.5 pwynt canran mewn un flwyddyn yn unig. Golyga hynny nad yw bron i un o bob pum oedolyn ifanc y byddem yn cyfarfod â nhw mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant. Ffigurau eithaf llwm. Weithiau, Lywydd, rydym yn dod i arfer â'r niferoedd hyn yn cael eu crybwyll, ond mae'n eithaf syfrdanol, mewn gwirionedd, nad yw bron i un o bob pum oedolyn ifanc mewn addysg, hyfforddiant na chyflogaeth.

Rhaid inni gofio bod unigolyn ifanc y tu ôl i bob un o'r ffigurau hynny sydd eisiau bwrw ymlaen â'u bywyd, parhau ag addysg, datblygu eu sgiliau, neu gamu ymlaen i fyd gwaith. Pan na allant wneud hynny, fel y mae'r cynnig hwn yn ei gydnabod, gall y canlyniadau fod yn hirhoedlog, gan effeithio ar eu hiechyd, eu henillion, eu cyfleoedd bywyd, ac yn y pen draw, ar ein cymdeithas gyfan. Dyna pam fod y rôl y mae colegau addysg bellach yn ei chwarae yn mynd i'r afael â hyn mor bwysig. Gwn fod Llywodraeth Cymru yn deall hyn, ond mae angen inni weld gweithredu i ddilyn y geiriau o ganlyniad i'r cynnig hwn heddiw.

Gwyddom, wrth gwrs, fod y nifer uchaf erioed o ddysgwyr yn dewis colegau addysg bellach fel llwybr i gymwysterau, sgiliau a gyrfaoedd, gyda phob coleg yng Nghymru yn nodi cynnydd mewn cyfranogiad yn y flwyddyn academaidd hon. Weinidog, fe fyddwch yn falch o glywed, wrth gwrs, fy mod wedi ymweld â choleg ddydd Gwener. Ymwelais â safle Iâl Coleg Cambria yn Wrecsam. Bûm yn chwarae pêl-bicl yn un o'u neuaddau chwaraeon, bûm yn gwylio rhywfaint o bicl yn cael ei baratoi yn y bwyty, ac rwy'n gobeithio'r nefoedd nad oes unrhyw luniau ohonof yn mynd i bicl wrth ddawnsio yn eu stiwdio ddawns.

Yr hyn y soniasant amdano hefyd oedd y galw cynyddol y maent yn ei weld ar eu safle eu hunain yno yn Wrecsam, a gwn fod hynny'n adlewyrchu'r sefyllfa mewn colegau ledled Cymru sy'n wynebu'r un mathau o bwysau. Gwyddom fod galw arbennig o gryf mewn meysydd addysg galwedigaethol a thechnegol, fel adeiladu, peirianneg a gofal iechyd, sef yr union y sectorau, fel mae'n digwydd, lle mae angen gweithwyr medrus ar Gymru heddiw. Ac fel y clywsom eisoes yn y sylwadau agoriadol, Lywydd, nid yw'r cyllid angenrheidiol ar gael i ateb y galw cynyddol.

Rydym eisoes wedi clywed am y 5,000 o ddysgwyr ar draws y colegau yng Nghymru sy'n astudio heb y cyllid cysylltiedig i'w cefnogi'n briodol. Yn fy etholaeth i, mae oddeutu 1,000 o fyfyrwyr ar hyn o bryd mewn colegau heb y cyllid ar waith i ddarparu'r gefnogaeth sydd ei hangen arnynt. Rydym wedi methu ariannu'r galw hwnnw. Rydym mewn perygl o weld llai o leoedd, llai o gyrsiau a llai o gefnogaeth i'r bobl ifanc y soniais amdanynt ar ddechrau fy nghyfraniad heddiw, sef y bobl ifanc hynny nad ydynt mewn gwaith, y bobl ifanc hynny nad ydynt mewn hyfforddiant ar hyn o bryd ac nad ydynt yn gallu gweld y dyfodol y mae angen iddynt allu ei weld. Y perygl yw y bydd yr argyfwng NEET yn gwaethygu ac nid yn gwella.

Ond un rhan o'r ateb yn unig yw cyllid, a dyna pam y mae gwelliant y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig mor bwysig, a dyna pam ein bod yn galw ar Lywodraeth Cymru i annog mwy o gydweithio rhwng y colegau hynny a'r sector preifat. Oherwydd mae gennym sefyllfa ryfedd yng Nghymru ar hyn o bryd, lle bydd llawer ohonom ar draws y Siambr yn ymwybodol fod cyflogwyr yn ei chael hi'n anodd dod o hyd i bobl â'r sgiliau cywir tra bod pobl ifanc yn ei chael hi'n anodd dod o hyd i lwybrau clir i mewn i waith. Felly, mae rhywbeth o'i le. Rwy'n siŵr y bydd y Gweinidog yn sôn am yr archwiliad sgiliau sydd ar y gweill, ac rwy'n gobeithio'n fawr fod busnes yn ystyriaeth bwysig yn hwnnw hefyd. Oherwydd gall cyflogwyr helpu'r colegau hynny i ddeall y sgiliau sydd eu hangen ar ddiwydiannau, gall colegau ddarparu'r genhedlaeth nesaf o dalent i fusnesau, a gall dysgwyr ennill y profiad a'r ddealltwriaeth o'r gweithle sy'n gwneud y gwahaniaeth rhwng gorffen addysg a dod o hyd i yrfa.

Enghraifft o hyn, Lywydd, yw'r sector amddiffyn. Gwyddom fod sector amddiffyn y DU yn darparu oddeutu £1 biliwn y flwyddyn o fuddsoddiad i'n diwydiannau yng Nghymru. Felly, pam na fyddem eisiau i golegau Cymru weithio gyda'r sector amddiffyn i sicrhau bod ein pobl ifanc wedi'u paratoi i fanteisio ar y cyfleoedd sydd ar gael iddynt yn y dyfodol? Mae'r un peth yn wir am adeiladu, peirianneg, ynni a llawer o sectorau eraill y mae economi Cymru’n dibynnu cymaint arnynt.

Felly, nid oes a wnelo hyn â dweud wrth bobl ifanc pa yrfa y dylent ei dewis, mae a wnelo â rhoi'r cyfle, y profiad a'r dewis iddynt allu camu ymlaen i fyd gwaith. Mae'r Ceidwadwyr Cymreig yn credu y dylai pob dysgwr allu dewis llwybr sy'n gweithio iddynt hwy. Dyna pam ei bod yn bwysig fod y cynnig hwn a'n gwelliant yn cael eu cefnogi. Mae angen colegau sydd wedi'u hariannu'n iawn, cysylltiadau cryfach rhwng addysg a diwydiant a Llywodraeth Cymru sy'n canolbwyntio ar greu cyfleoedd i'n pobl ifanc. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd like to thank Lynne Neagle for bringing this important debate to the Chamber today. Before the summer recess, I raised the situation at Coleg y Cymoedd, which has a campus in my constituency, in Nantgarw. Across its four campuses, there were hundreds of prospective learners placed on waiting lists due to funding constraints at that point. Many had applied for construction, manufacturing and other vocational courses, but even now, with the term under way, 400 learners have had to enrol on their second or third-choice courses, while 40 of them remain on waiting lists.

So, we are now just a year away from the roll-out of VCSEs, the vocational certificate of secondary education, for 14 to 16-year-olds. The situation at Coleg y Cymoedd clearly demonstrates there is already strong demand among young people for vocational education. So, with just one year to go until the roll-out, I wondered how the Welsh Government is planning to ensure the VCSEs are delivered consistently across all schools in Wales and, crucially, joined up with further education, apprenticeships and the skills needs that employers want.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn ddiolch i Lynne Neagle am gyflwyno'r ddadl bwysig hon i'r Siambr heddiw. Cyn gwyliau'r haf, nodais y sefyllfa yng Ngholeg y Cymoedd, sydd â champws yn fy etholaeth i, yn Nantgarw. Ar draws ei bedwar campws, roedd cannoedd o ddarpar ddysgwyr ar restrau aros oherwydd cyfyngiadau cyllido ar y pryd. Roedd llawer wedi gwneud ceisiadau am gyrsiau adeiladu, gweithgynhyrchu a chyrsiau galwedigaethol eraill, ond hyd yn oed nawr, gyda'r tymor wedi cychwyn, mae 400 o ddysgwyr wedi gorfod cofrestru ar eu hail neu drydydd dewis o gyrsiau, tra bo 40 ohonynt ar restrau aros o hyd.

Felly, blwyddyn yn unig sydd i fynd bellach cyn inni gyflwyno’r TAAU, y dystysgrif alwedigaethol addysg uwchradd, ar gyfer pobl 14 i 16 oed. Mae’r sefyllfa yng Ngholeg y Cymoedd yn dangos yn glir fod galw cryf eisoes ymhlith pobl ifanc am addysg alwedigaethol. Felly, gyda blwyddyn yn unig i fynd cyn ei chyflwyno, tybed sut y mae Llywodraeth Cymru’n bwriadu sicrhau bod y cymwysterau TAAU yn cael eu cyflwyno’n gyson ar draws pob ysgol yng Nghymru, ac yn hollbwysig, eu bod yn cysylltu ag addysg bellach, prentisiaethau a’r anghenion sgiliau y mae cyflogwyr eu heisiau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I stand today in support of the motion, not because I agree with everything that Labour did in Government—and, to be clear, I don't—but because the facts in the motion today are true: too many young people in Wales are not in education, employment or training. Demand for college places is up, but the funding has not followed suit, and that is a crucial policy failure that must be addressed.

The motion today discusses a crisis amongst young people who are not in education, employment or training, alongside the lifelong scarring that follows. Now, we know that the statistics are dire. As Sam just shared with us, in the year ending December 2025, 17 per cent of 16 to 24-year-olds were not in education, employment or training. That's 56,800 young people who are unable to participate in the economy. Wales was the only UK nation where those statistics rose year on year, with a 5.5 per cent increase. That is a stark failure of the Government in this place to deliver for our young people. It's also a huge missed opportunity for our economy and for our public finances. If we could get just half of those young people into full-time employment, the Welsh Government would generate over £90 million in income tax receipts. And that's before you consider the wider benefits that come with a larger consumer base and a greater number of young people who are engaged in the economy.

Now, colleges are one of our main routes for young people to escape the NEET trap. The motion is right to recognise that the record levels of demand are imposing financial pressures on these organisations. Colleges across Wales are being forced to turn students away because they simply do not have the resources to place them on courses. ColegauCymru said in January that the 2026-27 budget risked shutting young people out of education and that it would shatter the then Government's own young person's guarantee. They estimated a funding shortfall of more than £23.5 million across FE institutions.

Now, the young person's guarantee was Labour's promise to every 16 to 24-year-old in the country that they would be offered education, training or help into work. Yet, with some of the highest employability spending per head compared to other parts of the UK, more and more of our young people are being left behind. The Government needs to step up and deliver the funding for institutions and initiatives that can help to solve this problem.

Now, last week, Llywydd, I visited, alongside yourself, a showcase event for Pathways, a pilot project that helped to get young people in the Rhondda out of the NEET trap and on to a positive path for the future. That pilot will publish its evidence this autumn, and I hope that it can be a positive model for young people for improving their lives and continuing to engage with the economy.

Now, Plaid Cymru spend a lot of time talking about their ambitions for Wales, but the ambitions that I'm interested in are the ambitions of our young people and their ability to fulfil those ambitions within the economy. Therefore, I will be supporting the motion before us today, alongside the Conservative amendment calling for closer ties between our institutions and the private sector. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n codi heddiw i gefnogi'r cynnig, nid am fy mod yn cytuno â phopeth a wnaeth Llafur fel Llywodraeth—ac i fod yn glir, nid ydwyf—ond am fod y ffeithiau yn y cynnig heddiw yn wir: mae gormod o bobl ifanc yng Nghymru heb fod mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant. Mae'r galw am leoedd coleg wedi cynyddu, ond nid yw'r cyllid wedi dilyn y galw, ac mae hynny'n fethiant polisi allweddol y mae'n rhaid mynd i'r afael ag ef.

Mae'r cynnig heddiw yn trafod argyfwng ymhlith pobl ifanc nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant, ochr yn ochr â'r creithiau gydol oes sy'n dilyn. Nawr, fe wyddom fod yr ystadegau'n ofnadwy. Fel y rhannodd Sam gyda ni nawr, yn y flwyddyn a ddaeth i ben ym mis Rhagfyr 2025, nid oedd 17 y cant o bobl ifanc 16 i 24 oed mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant. Dyna 56,800 o bobl ifanc na allant gymryd rhan yn yr economi. Cymru oedd yr unig genedl yn y DU lle cynyddodd yr ystadegau hynny o un flwyddyn i'r llall, gyda chynnydd o 5.5 y cant. Mae hynny'n fethiant amlwg ar ran y Llywodraeth yn y lle hwn i gyflawni ar gyfer ein pobl ifanc. Mae hefyd yn gyfle enfawr a gollwyd i'n heconomi ac i'n cyllid cyhoeddus. Pe baem yn gallu cael hanner y bobl ifanc hynny hyd yn oed i gyflogaeth amser llawn, byddai Llywodraeth Cymru yn cynhyrchu dros £90 miliwn mewn derbyniadau treth incwm. A hynny cyn i chi ystyried y manteision ehangach sy'n dod gyda sylfaen ddefnyddwyr fwy a nifer uwch o bobl ifanc yn rhan o'r economi.

Nawr, colegau yw un o'n prif lwybrau i bobl ifanc ddianc rhag y trap NEET. Mae'r cynnig yn iawn i gydnabod bod y lefelau uchaf erioed o alw yn gosod pwysau ariannol ar y sefydliadau hyn. Mae colegau ledled Cymru yn cael eu gorfodi i droi myfyrwyr ymaith am nad oes ganddynt adnoddau i gynnig cyrsiau iddynt. Dywedodd ColegauCymru ym mis Ionawr fod cyllideb 2026-27 mewn perygl o gau pobl ifanc allan o addysg ac y byddai'n chwalu gwarant i bobl ifanc y Llywodraeth ar y pryd. Roeddent yn amcangyfrif diffyg cyllid o fwy na £23.5 miliwn ar draws y sefydliadau addysg bellach.

Nawr, y warant i bobl ifanc oedd addewid Llafur i bob unigolyn 16 i 24 oed yn y wlad y byddent yn cael cynnig addysg, hyfforddiant neu gymorth i mewn i waith. Eto i gyd, gyda pheth o'r gwariant cyflogadwyedd uchaf y pen o'i gymharu â rhannau eraill o'r DU, mae mwy a mwy o'n pobl ifanc yn cael eu gadael ar ôl. Mae angen i'r Llywodraeth gamu i'r adwy a darparu'r cyllid i sefydliadau a mentrau a all helpu i ddatrys y broblem hon.

Nawr, yr wythnos diwethaf, Lywydd, ymwelais â digwyddiad arddangos Pathways, prosiect peilot a helpai i gael pobl ifanc yn y Rhondda allan o'r trap NEET ac ymlaen i lwybr cadarnhaol ar gyfer y dyfodol. Bydd y cynllun peilot hwnnw'n cyhoeddi ei dystiolaeth yr hydref hwn, ac rwy'n gobeithio y gall fod yn fodel cadarnhaol i bobl ifanc allu gwella eu bywydau a pharhau i ymgysylltu â'r economi.

Nawr, mae Plaid Cymru yn treulio llawer o amser yn siarad am eu huchelgeisiau dros Gymru, ond yr uchelgeisiau sydd o ddiddordeb i mi yw uchelgeisiau ein pobl ifanc a'u gallu i gyflawni'r uchelgeisiau hynny o fewn yr economi. Felly, byddaf yn cefnogi'r cynnig sydd o'n blaenau heddiw, ochr yn ochr â'r gwelliant Ceidwadol sy'n galw am gysylltiadau agosach rhwng ein sefydliadau a'r sector preifat. Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Addysg Bellach
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Welsh Labour Debate: Further education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm really pleased to be able to contribute to today's debate. I had the privilege of leading on higher education and further education in the last two years of the previous Welsh Labour Government. I'd just like to echo the point made by my colleague Lynne Neagle about how pleased we were to be able to allocate that additional £20 million to FE. But that need for additional funding is an upward trajectory, Deputy Minister, and this is a really clear message that you need to take from today's debate about that need for additional funding.

One thing I loved when I held that role was the ability to get out and about across Wales, meeting learners and the staff who support them. There were, and are, challenges, but the passion, the dedication to strive and achieve and deliver the very best learning outcomes was clear. That experience will shape my comments today, and I want to start by mentioning the new Welsh Government's higher education review. Now, this is important. The sector does face issues, and it's right that these are looked at, but the focus just on HE stands in direct contrast to the approach that we took in Government. That was based on ensuring the participation and sustainability of the whole tertiary system, and I am concerned that, without that focus, there's a very real danger that the focus on further education will be lost and its funding displaced also. I hope that this is something the Welsh Government will address when responding to the debate.

And what will the impact be if we lose this focus on FE? Well, we know that FE plays a key role in providing both vocational and academic pathways, particularly, as others have mentioned, for those young people most at risk of disengaging from education. Indeed, I would suggest that there is, in fact, a moral imperative for the Government to focus on FE to address this challenge.

On Monday, I visited Coleg y Cymoedd's Aberdare campus in my constituency, and my thanks to the staff and students who took the time to talk to me there as part of Adult Learners Week. There were some really excellent examples of mature learners re-engaging with education, meeting the need in the way that only FE can. This is another area where there is considerable demand, as I mentioned in my education question earlier today. This is a pattern that has been noted in several years. Those adult learners looking to re-engage should not have to lose out.

My conversations with staff and learners in Coleg y Cymoedd sketched out a very similar picture. Overall, that college, just one campus—. That college has over 5,500 full-time learners of all ages on its books, the majority aged 16 to 17, though. But, astonishingly, only just over 83 per cent are funded. Can I take a second just to reinforce that? Nearly one in five of the college's full-time students aren't funded. On the Aberdare campus, that's not just a stat, but 600 individual learners. Without funding, they are in real danger of disengaging.

So, there are 400 learners there at level 1 and level 2 who are not on their first-choice courses. That, in itself, represents a risk of disengagement. And for the first year ever, that particular campus has 40 learners that they haven't been able to place that are on a waiting list and unable to be enrolled, in real danger of disengaging from education forever. There were 80 learners there who they were only able to place on courses for two days a week. They would really like to be able to place them for much longer than that, and, of course, the less time they are placed in college, the more the risk of disengagement. That would need a hire drive for staff recruitment to accommodate, and, of course, that all comes down to funding.

There's been a 47 per cent increase in that campus alone in this year for individual development plans for learners with additional learning needs, and we all know that it needs resource to be able to cater for those needs. Now, I know a review of FE would not be a panacea, but it could shine a spotlight on the issues and help us work together to determine the solutions to put things right for our learners.

I want to close by reflecting on some of the benefits to the individual from engaging in FE: improved educational qualifications, a new path or journey, increased skills or enhanced employment opportunities. And crucially, as Public Health Wales reminds us, education is also one of the biggest preventative mechanisms for mental health as well. So, Deputy Minister, FE can change lives. Please remember that as you take forward your policy decisions over the coming Senedd term.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n falch iawn o allu cyfrannu at y ddadl heddiw. Cefais y fraint o arwain ar addysg uwch ac addysg bellach yn ystod dwy flynedd olaf y Llywodraeth Lafur Cymru flaenorol. Hoffwn adleisio'r pwynt a wnaed gan fy nghyd-Aelod Lynne Neagle ynglŷn â pha mor falch yr oeddem o allu dyrannu'r £20 miliwn ychwanegol hwnnw i addysg bellach. Ond mae'r angen am gyllid ychwanegol yn dal i gynyddu, Ddirprwy Weinidog, ac mae angen i chi ystyried neges glir y ddadl heddiw am yr angen am gyllid ychwanegol.

Un peth yr oeddwn yn hoff iawn ohono pan oeddwn i yn y rôl honno oedd y gallu i fynd allan ledled Cymru i gyfarfod â dysgwyr a'r staff sy'n eu cefnogi. Roedd yna, ac mae yna heriau, ond roedd yr angerdd, yr ymroddiad i ymdrechu a chyflawni a chyflawni'r canlyniadau dysgu gorau yn glir. Y profiad hwnnw fydd yn siapio fy sylwadau heddiw, ac rwyf am ddechrau trwy sôn am adolygiad addysg uwch newydd Llywodraeth Cymru. Nawr, mae hwn yn bwysig. Mae'r sector yn wynebu problemau, ac mae'n iawn fod y rhain yn cael eu hystyried, ond mae'r ffocws ar addysg uwch yn unig yn gwbl groes i'n dull o weithredu ni pan oeddem mewn grym. Roedd hwnnw'n seiliedig ar sicrhau cyfranogiad a chynaliadwyedd y system drydyddol gyfan, a heb y ffocws hwnnw, rwy'n pryderu bod perygl real iawn y bydd y ffocws ar addysg bellach yn cael ei golli a'i gyllid yn cael ei ddisodli hefyd. Rwy'n gobeithio bod hyn yn rhywbeth yr aiff Llywodraeth Cymru i'r afael ag ef wrth ymateb i'r ddadl.

A beth fydd yr effaith os collwn y ffocws hwn ar addysg bellach? Wel, gwyddom fod addysg bellach yn chwarae rôl allweddol yn darparu llwybrau galwedigaethol ac academaidd, yn enwedig, fel y soniodd eraill, i'r bobl ifanc hynny sydd fwyaf mewn perygl o ymddieithrio rhag addysg. Yn wir, carwn awgrymu bod yna reidrwydd moesol ar y Llywodraeth i ganolbwyntio ar addysg bellach i fynd i'r afael â'r her hon.

Ddydd Llun, ymwelais â champws Aberdâr Coleg y Cymoedd yn fy etholaeth, a diolch i'r staff a'r myfyrwyr a roddodd amser i siarad â mi yno yn rhan o'r Wythnos Addysg Oedolion. Roedd yno enghreifftiau gwirioneddol ardderchog o ddysgwyr aeddfed yn ailymgysylltu ag addysg, gan ddiwallu'r angen mewn ffordd na all dim ond addysg bellach ei wneud. Mae hwn yn faes arall lle mae'r galw'n sylweddol, fel y soniais yn fy nghwestiwn addysg yn gynharach heddiw. Mae hwn yn batrwm sydd wedi'i nodi ers sawl blwyddyn. Ni ddylai'r oedolion hynny sy'n dysgu, sy'n awyddus i ailymgysylltu, orfod bod ar eu colled.

Roedd fy sgyrsiau gyda staff a dysgwyr yng Ngholeg y Cymoedd yn cynnig darlun tebyg iawn. Ar y cyfan, y coleg hwnnw, dim ond un campws—. Mae gan y coleg hwnnw dros 5,500 o ddysgwyr amser llawn o bob oed ar ei lyfrau, ac mae'r mwyafrif ohonynt rhwng 16 a 17 oed. Ond yn rhyfeddol, dim ond ychydig dros 83 y cant sy'n cael eu hariannu. A gaf i roi eiliad i egluro hynny? Ni chaiff bron i un o bob pump o fyfyrwyr amser llawn y coleg eu hariannu. Ar gampws Aberdâr, nid ystadegyn yn unig yw hwnnw, ond 600 o ddysgwyr unigol. Heb gyllid, maent mewn perygl gwirioneddol o ymddieithrio rhag addysg.

Felly, mae 400 o ddysgwyr yno ar lefel 1 a lefel 2 nad ydynt ar eu cyrsiau dewis cyntaf. Mae hynny, ynddo'i hun, yn creu risg o ymddieithrio. Ac am y flwyddyn gyntaf erioed, mae gan y campws penodol hwnnw 40 o ddysgwyr ar restr aros na fu modd eu gosod ar gyrsiau, nad ydynt yn gallu cofrestru, ac sydd mewn perygl gwirioneddol o ymddieithrio rhag addysg am byth. Roedd 80 o ddysgwyr yno na allent eu gosod ar gyrsiau am fwy na deuddydd yr wythnos. Byddent yn hoffi'n fawr eu gosod am lawer hirach na hynny, ac wrth gwrs, po leiaf o amser y treuliant yn y coleg, y mwyaf yw'r risg o ymddieithrio. Byddai angen ymgyrch gyflogi ar gyfer recriwtio staff i ddarparu ar gyfer hynny, ac wrth gwrs, mae hynny'n galw am gyllid.

Bu cynnydd o 47 y cant yn y campws hwnnw yn unig eleni mewn cynlluniau datblygu unigol ar gyfer dysgwyr ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, ac rydym i gyd yn gwybod bod angen adnoddau ar y coleg i allu darparu ar gyfer yr anghenion hynny. Nawr, rwy'n gwybod na fyddai adolygiad o addysg bellach yn ateb i bob dim, ond gallai daflu goleuni ar y problemau a'n helpu i weithio gyda'n gilydd i benderfynu ar yr atebion i unioni pethau er mwyn ein dysgwyr.

Rwyf am gloi trwy fyfyrio ar rai o'r manteision i'r unigolyn o gael addysg bellach: gwell cymwysterau addysgol, llwybr neu daith newydd, mwy o sgiliau neu well cyfleoedd cyflogaeth. Ac yn hollbwysig, fel y mae Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru yn ein hatgoffa, addysg hefyd yw un o'r mecanweithiau ataliol mwyaf ar gyfer iechyd meddwl. Felly, Ddirprwy Weinidog, gall addysg bellach newid bywydau. Cofiwch hynny wrth ichi fwrw ymlaen â'ch penderfyniadau polisi dros dymor nesaf y Senedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Welsh Labour Debate: Further education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm glad also that we have the opportunity today to discuss NEETs, so I thank Lynne Neagle as well for bringing forward this really important debate, but also the chance to discuss why young people find themselves in this position as well. Not too long ago, I raised this issue here in the Senedd, particularly the long-term impact that being out of education, employment or training can have on a young person's chances in life. As one of the youngest Members in the Senedd—I think Ben actually might win the award just above me, just about—this is something that is really personal to me as well.

The recent Milburn report highlighted the real scale of this challenge, with around 56,000 young people in Wales. Again, that statistic's been bounced around, but that's 17 per cent of all 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training. 

Now, there are lots of reasons why a young person might find themselves in this position. It could be difficulties at school, mental health, child poverty, transport, or simply not having the right support at the right time. In the constituency that I represent, Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni, we're seeing some of these challenges very clearly. Back in June, I raised this with the First Minister, pointing out that Blaenau Gwent has the highest proportion of residents aged 16 and over with no qualifications in Wales—that's 27.9 per cent—while Caerphilly is fourth among all local authorities.

Now, those figures are really concerning, but what concerns me more is what they can mean for a young person that's growing up in these communities. That's why early intervention really matters as well. We need to support young people before they reach the point of completely disengaging, and I've seen some really good examples of this in my own constituency. A couple of weeks ago, I visited ACT training in Ebbw Vale. They're supporting young people who, for all sorts of reasons, haven't found that typical conventional route from school into further education, training or employment. And I just want to put on the record as well my thanks to all of the staff there for the work that they do, because it was really inspiring, that visit. And there was one thing that really stood out to me that one of the staff said during that visit. They told me that, for some of the young people that they work with, the support that they provide can quite literally be the difference between life and death for that young person, and I think that really brings home again the real seriousness of this situation. Because we can talk about NEET rates and percentages like I did at the start, but, for that young person, this isn't a statistic. It's their life.

Further education and training have a huge role to play, but there are also wider barriers as well that can make it so hard for a young person to take that next step. If they're struggling with their mental health, they may not be in a position to engage. If they’re growing up in child poverty, like so many do in my constituency, they may not have the money for travel, equipment, or the stability that they need to take up an opportunity, if that opportunity's there. And particularly in the Valleys, transport, as we know, can be a real barrier. You can have a college course, apprenticeship or job available, but if a young person can't get there reliably or affordably that opportunity is, effectively, out of reach for them.

And that's why this has to be a cross-Government issue. Education and skills are a big part of the answer, and having those spaces as well is so important. But so are mental health, tackling child poverty, transport, the economy, and support for young people and their families.

Not every young person is going to follow the same path. Some will go to university, some into apprenticeships, some straight into employment, and some might take a little longer to find their route as well, and all of those options are okay. But what matters is that they have the opportunity to find it. A young person growing up in Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni should have the same chances to succeed as someone growing up anywhere else in Wales, because talent is spread equally across the whole of Wales, but opportunity isn't. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwyf innau'n falch hefyd ein bod yn cael cyfle heddiw i drafod pobl ifanc NEET, felly diolch i Lynne Neagle am gyflwyno'r ddadl wirioneddol bwysig hon, ond hefyd am y cyfle i drafod pam y mae pobl ifanc yn wynebu'r sefyllfa hon. Heb fod yn rhy bell yn ôl, codais y mater hwn yma yn y Senedd, yn enwedig yr effaith hirdymor y gall peidio â bod mewn addysg, cyflogaeth neu hyfforddiant ei chael ar gyfleoedd bywyd unigolyn ifanc. Fel un o'r Aelodau ieuengaf yn y Senedd—rwy'n credu efallai mai Ben fyddai'n ennill y wobr honno, o damaid—mae hyn yn rhywbeth sy'n bersonol iawn i mi hefyd.

Tynnodd adroddiad Milburn sylw at raddfa wirioneddol yr her hon yn ddiweddar, gyda thua 56,000 o bobl ifanc yng Nghymru. Unwaith eto, mae'r ystadegyn hwnnw wedi cael ei daflu o gwmpas, ond mae'n golygu bod 17 y cant o'r holl bobl ifanc 16 i 24 oed heb fod mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant.

Nawr, mae yna lawer o resymau pam y gallai unigolyn ifanc fod yn y sefyllfa hon. Gallai ddeillio o anawsterau yn yr ysgol, iechyd meddwl, tlodi plant, trafnidiaeth, neu'n syml am nad ydynt yn cael y gefnogaeth gywir ar yr adeg iawn. Yn yr etholaeth rwy'n ei chynrychioli, Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni, gwelwn rai o'r heriau hyn yn glir iawn. Yn ôl ym mis Mehefin, codais hyn gyda'r Prif Weinidog, gan nodi mai Blaenau Gwent sydd â'r gyfran uchaf o drigolion 16 oed a throsodd heb unrhyw gymwysterau yng Nghymru—sef 27.9 y cant—tra bod Caerffili yn bedwerydd ymhlith yr holl awdurdodau lleol.

Nawr, mae'r ffigurau hynny'n peri pryder mawr, ond yr hyn sy'n fy mhoeni i'n fwy yw beth y gallant ei olygu i unigolyn ifanc sy'n tyfu i fyny yn y cymunedau hyn. Dyna pam y mae ymyrraeth gynnar yn bwysig iawn hefyd. Mae angen inni gefnogi pobl ifanc cyn iddynt gyrraedd y pwynt pan fyddant yn ymddieithrio'n llwyr, ac fe welais enghreifftiau da iawn o hyn yn fy etholaeth fy hun. Ychydig wythnosau yn ôl, ymwelais â hyfforddiant ACT yng Nglynebwy. Maent yn cefnogi pobl ifanc sydd, am bob math o resymau, heb ddod o hyd i'r llwybr confensiynol nodweddiadol o'r ysgol i addysg bellach, hyfforddiant neu gyflogaeth. Ac rwyf am gofnodi fy niolch hefyd i'r holl staff yno am y gwaith a wnânt, oherwydd roedd yr ymweliad hwnnw'n wirioneddol ysbrydoledig. Ac roedd un peth a ddywedodd un o'r staff yn ystod yr ymweliad hwnnw yn sefyll allan i mi. I rai o'r bobl ifanc y maent yn gweithio gyda nhw, meddent, gall y gefnogaeth y maent yn ei darparu olygu'r gwahaniaeth yn llythrennol rhwng bywyd a marwolaeth i'r unigolyn ifanc hwnnw, ac rwy'n credu bod hynny'n crisialu gwir ddifrifoldeb y sefyllfa hon. Oherwydd gallwn siarad am gyfraddau a chanrannau NEET fel y gwneuthum ar y dechrau, ond i'r unigolyn ifanc hwnnw, nid ystadegyn mohono, ond eu bywyd.

Mae gan addysg bellach a hyfforddiant rôl enfawr i'w chwarae, ond mae yna rwystrau ehangach hefyd a all ei gwneud mor anodd i unigolyn ifanc gymryd y cam nesaf. Os ydynt yn cael trafferth gyda'u hiechyd meddwl, efallai na fyddant mewn sefyllfa i ymgysylltu. Os ydynt yn tyfu i fyny mewn tlodi plant, fel y mae cymaint yn fy etholaeth i, efallai nad oes ganddynt arian ar gyfer teithio, offer, neu'r sefydlogrwydd sydd ei angen arnynt i fanteisio ar gyfle, os yw'r cyfle hwnnw yno. Ac yn enwedig yn y Cymoedd, fel y gwyddom, gall trafnidiaeth fod yn rhwystr go iawn. Gall cwrs coleg, prentisiaeth neu swydd fod ar gael, ond os na all unigolyn ifanc ddibynnu ar allu cyrraedd yno neu fforddio'r daith, mae'r cyfle hwnnw allan o'u cyrraedd i bob pwrpas.

A dyna pam y mae'n rhaid i hyn fod yn fater trawslywodraethol. Mae addysg a sgiliau'n rhan fawr o'r ateb, ac mae cael y mannau hynny mor bwysig. Ond felly hefyd iechyd meddwl, mynd i'r afael â thlodi plant, trafnidiaeth, yr economi, a chefnogaeth i bobl ifanc a'u teuluoedd.

Nid yw pob unigolyn ifanc yn mynd i ddilyn yr un llwybr. Bydd rhai'n mynd i'r brifysgol, rhai i brentisiaethau, rhai'n syth i gyflogaeth, ac efallai y bydd rhai'n cymryd ychydig yn hirach i ddod o hyd i'w llwybr, ac mae'r holl opsiynau hynny'n iawn. Ond yr hyn sy'n bwysig yw bod ganddynt gyfle i ddarganfod y llwybr hwnnw. Dylai unigolyn ifanc sy'n tyfu i fyny ym Mlaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni gael yr un cyfleoedd i lwyddo â rhywun sy'n tyfu i fyny yn unrhyw le arall yng Nghymru, oherwydd mae talent wedi'i wasgaru'n gyfartal ar draws Cymru gyfan, ond nid yw cyfle. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Addysg Bellach
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Welsh Labour Debate: Further education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'll be speaking in favour of the motion. There are two issues at the heart of this motion: the number of young people not in education, employment or training, whom I shall refer to as NEETs, and whether our further education colleges have the capacity to meet current demand.

Starting with NEETs, the motion is right to refer to long-term scarring. A Scottish longitudinal study found that young people who are NEET at 16 to 19 were 2.8 times as likely to be unemployed or economically inactive 10 years later. At the societal level, with an ageing population, we need our young people to be productive as older generations leave the workforce. Also, we should develop the skills and potential of young people already living here, rather than relying on recruiting workers from overseas to support an ageing population.

Before moving on from NEETs, I want briefly to address AI. On GCSE results day this year, a young constituent e-mailed me because she was concerned about the impact of artificial intelligence on jobs. Young people are well aware of AI, and I would be misleading the Chamber if I said young people have nothing to worry about, because the Open University’s 2026 business barometer found that 19 per cent of employers surveyed had reduced early career recruitment, and, among those employers, 42 per cent attributed that reduction to the wider adoption of AI doing more entry-level tasks. Our young people are therefore now competing with both human and non-human intelligences for jobs. That makes the role of further education colleges in providing young people with skills and routes into productive work as important as ever.

Turning to FE colleges, I want to focus in the second part of my speech on Coleg y Cymoedd, which serves communities across my constituency of Blaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni, and I thank principal Jonathan Morgan for providing the following figures. Coleg y Cymoedd has provisionally enrolled 5,534 full-time learners this year, compared with 4,888 last year—an increase of more than 13 per cent in a single year. Yet it is funded for only around 4,596 learners, leaving a gap of more than 900 places, which the college estimates equates to a funding pressure of around £3 million. The consequences of supporting substantially more learners than are funded include increased class sizes and greater pressure on teaching staff, potentially compromising the quality of the learning experience.

On top of this, the number of learners with additional learning needs or individual development plans at Coleg y Cymoedd has risen from 309 to 454 in a single year—an increase of 47 per cent. It is absolutely to be welcomed that more young people with additional learning needs are accessing further education, but that increased participation requires additional funding. Without it, greater pressure is placed on specialist support teams, well-being provision and teaching staff. Yet funding has not kept pace—far from it. The Welsh FE sector received £21.5 million of increased participation funding in 2025-26. The equivalent allocation available in 2026-27 is £6.25 million. Coleg y Cymoedd's view is that restoring the previous level would provide an immediate means of addressing current demand pressures. These figures highlight the need to fund increased participation.

I agree with the case for increased participation funding set out in this motion, but funding must also come with scrutiny. As the Welsh Government considers future FE funding, it should look not only at how many places are required, but also at what those places are delivering. Are learners completing their courses? Are they gaining qualifications employers value? And are we training people in the skills Wales actually needs? Because further education should be a bridge into skilled work and genuine opportunity. For these reasons, while funding must come with rigorous scrutiny and proof of outcomes, I support the motion. More of our young people should have the opportunity to progress in life, both for their own sake and for the sake of society as a whole.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Byddaf yn siarad o blaid y cynnig. Mae dau fater wrth wraidd y cynnig hwn: nifer y bobl ifanc nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth na hyfforddiant, y byddaf yn cyfeirio atynt fel pobl ifanc NEET, ac a oes gan ein colegau addysg bellach allu i ateb y galw presennol.

Gan ddechrau gyda phobl ifanc NEET, mae'r cynnig yn iawn i gyfeirio at greithiau hirdymor. Canfu astudiaeth hydredol yn yr Alban fod pobl ifanc NEET rhwng 16 a 19 oed 2.8 gwaith yn fwy tebygol o fod yn ddi-waith neu'n economaidd anweithgar 10 mlynedd yn ddiweddarach. Ar y lefel gymdeithasol, gyda phoblogaeth sy'n heneiddio, mae angen i'n pobl ifanc fod yn gynhyrchiol wrth i genedlaethau hŷn adael y gweithlu. Hefyd, dylem ddatblygu sgiliau a photensial pobl ifanc sydd eisoes yn byw yma, yn hytrach na dibynnu ar recriwtio gweithwyr o dramor i gefnogi poblogaeth sy'n heneiddio.

Cyn symud ymlaen o bobl ifanc NEET, rwyf am fynd i'r afael yn fyr â deallusrwydd artiffisial. Ar ddiwrnod canlyniadau TGAU eleni, anfonodd etholwr ifanc e-bost ataf am ei bod yn pryderu am effaith deallusrwydd artiffisial ar swyddi. Mae pobl ifanc yn ymwybodol iawn o ddeallusrwydd artiffisial, a buaswn yn camarwain y Siambr pe bawn i'n dweud nad oes gan bobl ifanc unrhyw beth i boeni yn ei gylch, oherwydd canfu baromedr busnes 2026 y Brifysgol Agored fod 19 y cant o'r cyflogwyr a arolygwyd wedi lleihau eu lefelau recriwtio gyrfa gynnar, ac ymhlith y cyflogwyr hynny, priodolodd 42 y cant y gostyngiad hwnnw i'r ffaith bod deallusrwydd artiffisial wedi ei fabwysiadu'n ehangach ar gyfer gwneud mwy o dasgau lefel mynediad. Mae ein pobl ifanc felly yn cystadlu â deallusrwydd dynol a heb fod yn ddynol am swyddi erbyn hyn. Mae hynny'n gwneud rôl colegau addysg bellach yn darparu sgiliau a llwybrau i waith cynhyrchiol i bobl ifanc mor bwysig ag erioed.

Wrth droi at golegau addysg bellach, hoffwn ganolbwyntio yn ail ran fy araith ar Goleg y Cymoedd, sy'n gwasanaethu cymunedau ar draws fy etholaeth i ym Mlaenau Gwent Caerffili Rhymni, a diolch i'r pennaeth Jonathan Morgan am ddarparu'r ffigurau canlynol. Mae Coleg y Cymoedd wedi cofrestru 5,534 o ddysgwyr amser llawn yn amodol eleni, o'i gymharu â 4,888 y llynedd—cynnydd o fwy na 13 y cant mewn un flwyddyn. Ond dim ond ar gyfer oddeutu 4,596 o ddysgwyr y caiff ei ariannu, gan adael bwlch o fwy na 900 o leoedd, ac mae'r coleg yn amcangyfrif bod hynny'n cyfateb i bwysau ariannol o tua £3 miliwn. Mae canlyniadau cefnogi llawer mwy o ddysgwyr nag yr ariennir ar eu cyfer yn cynnwys dosbarthiadau mwy o faint a mwy o bwysau ar staff addysgu, a allai beryglu ansawdd y profiad dysgu.

Yn ogystal â hyn, mae nifer y dysgwyr sydd ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol neu gynlluniau datblygu unigol yng Ngholeg y Cymoedd wedi codi o 309 i 454 mewn un flwyddyn—cynnydd o 47 y cant. Mae'n sicr yn galonogol fod mwy o bobl ifanc ag anghenion dysgu ychwanegol yn dewis addysg bellach, ond mae'r cynnydd yn y niferoedd yn galw am gyllid ychwanegol. Hebddo, rhoddir mwy o bwysau ar dimau cymorth arbenigol, darpariaeth les a staff addysgu. Ond nid yw'r cyllid yn cyfateb i hynny—ymhell o fod. Derbyniodd sector addysg bellach Cymru £21.5 miliwn yn fwy o gyllid cyfranogiad yn 2025-26. Y dyraniad cyfatebol sydd ar gael yn 2026-27 yw £6.25 miliwn. Barn Coleg y Cymoedd yw y byddai adfer y lefel flaenorol yn darparu modd uniongyrchol o fynd i'r afael â phwysau'r galw presennol. Mae'r ffigurau hyn yn tynnu sylw at yr angen i ariannu cyfranogiad cynyddol.

Rwy'n cytuno â'r achos dros fwy o gyllid cyfranogiad a nodir yn y cynnig hwn, ond rhaid cael craffu i gyd-fynd â chyllid. Wrth i Lywodraeth Cymru ystyried cyllid addysg bellach yn y dyfodol, dylai edrych nid yn unig ar faint o leoedd sydd eu hangen, ond hefyd ar yr hyn y mae'r lleoedd hynny'n ei ddarparu. A yw dysgwyr yn cwblhau eu cyrsiau? A ydynt yn ennill cymwysterau y mae cyflogwyr yn eu hystyried yn werthfawr? Ac a ydym yn hyfforddi pobl yn y sgiliau sydd eu hangen ar Gymru mewn gwirionedd? Oherwydd dylai addysg bellach fod yn bont i waith medrus a chyfle go iawn. Am y rhesymau hyn, er bod yn rhaid cael craffu trwyadl a phrawf o ganlyniadau i ddod gyda'r cyllid, rwy'n cefnogi'r cynnig. Dylai mwy o'n pobl ifanc gael cyfle i gamu ymlaen mewn bywyd, er eu lles eu hunain ac er lles y gymdeithas gyfan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Addysg Bellach
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Welsh Labour Debate: Further education

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl Llafur Cymru: Addysg Bellach
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Welsh Labour Debate: Further education
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
We know there is a crisis of young people not being in education, employment or training, and the long-term scarring impact this has on their future health, earnings and life chances. If they're not in education between 16 and 18, the chance of them joining education after 18 or reaching employment reduces, and reduces rapidly.

As a former FE college lecturer and college governor, I welcome the increased participation of young people in further education colleges across Wales. It's very welcome, the rising demand for vocational and technical education. We need plumbers, we need hairdressers, we need electricians, we need decorators. We know we need those. In Britain, there were 981,000 young people aged 16 to 24 not in employment, education or training between April and June, according to the Office for National Statistics. But what shifts have happened there? We've got a lost generation of young people, and they're going to be lost forever unless urgent action is taken. And that really does fall on the Welsh Government to start taking some of this action.

What's happened over time has been the composition of this inactive group. The proportion who are inactive due to sickness or disability has more than doubled since 2005. I find it difficult to believe that almost a third of people who were NEETs in 2025 had health problems to such an extent that they were unable to engage in either education, training or employment. Other reasons are people having health and caring responsibilities and those who do not want or need employment. Those who do not want or need employment rose sharply during the same period, to reach 23 per cent of NEETs in 2025. I find it alarming that there will be some, the wealthy—probably sat on the benches opposite us—who actually have no need to work. But there's an awful lot of people who, if they're not in employment, are getting by on benefits.

At the same time, the share of young people inactive due to caring reasons has dropped, which is good news, but, again, the unpaid carers who we all meet fairly regularly keep on telling us about the problems. Those aged 16 and 17 who are likely to have been inactive for other reasons over the past few years, what happens then? They don't want to go to school. Lots of people don't want to carry on in school, school isn't for them, but that's not the end of education, that's not the end of training and that doesn't mean that they can never work. We have the Welsh Government's young person's guarantee scheme and that scheme is greatly welcomed.

Colleges and private training providers are the only option when direct movement into employment is not available. Private training providers, many of whom do an excellent job, lack capacity to train large numbers of young people. Evidence consistently shows that remaining in education post 16 is critical to young people's long-term life outcomes. It's also a point at which young people face a major decision of continuing in academic education or pursuing vocational education—a choice that can be difficult for those with limited guidance or family support. A lot of this comes down to what type of jobs you know, and most young people, what jobs do they know? They know teachers because they see them every day, they know what their families do, they know what their neighbours do, but there's a whole range of jobs that they know nothing about. A former Member of this Senedd who became a barrister did so because he went on training days with a barrister in Swansea. Now, that's something that is incredibly good, but we can't leave the future of young people to that sort of chance, can we?

Many young people want to go to college, and I recognise the financial pressures on colleges, if only because they keep on telling me. But no 16 to 18-year-old should be unable to attend a college because not enough places are funded. For colleges that provide training that is not funded by the Welsh Government, the amount is limited by financial pressure. There is a need for the Welsh Government to fund all the places that are needed. If we don't want NEETs, let's not be the people who create the NEETs by not providing training places for young people. And if young people who cannot get a job or get on a college course become NEET, it's not their fault, it's ours, or should I say, the Welsh Government's. The Government needs to fund further education colleges so that everyone who wants to go to college can go. This is why I support this motion today. It's important that every young person gets the opportunity they deserve.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rydym yn gwybod bod yna argyfwng ynghylch pobl ifanc nad ydynt mewn addysg, cyflogaeth neu hyfforddiant, a'r creithiau hirdymor y mae hyn yn ei achosi i'w hiechyd, eu henillion ac i'w cyfleoedd bywyd yn y dyfodol. Os nad ydynt mewn addysg rhwng 16 a 18 oed, mae'r gobaith y byddant yn ymuno ag addysg ar ôl 18 oed neu'n cyrraedd cyflogaeth yn lleihau, ac yn lleihau'n gyflym.

Fel cyn-ddarlithydd mewn coleg addysg bellach a llywodraethwr coleg, rwy'n croesawu cyfranogiad cynyddol pobl ifanc mewn colegau addysg bellach ledled Cymru. Mae'r galw cynyddol am addysg alwedigaethol a thechnegol i'w groesawu'n fawr iawn. Mae angen plymwyr, mae angen pobl trin gwallt, mae angen trydanwyr, mae angen peintwyr ac addurnwyr arnom. Fe wyddom fod angen y rheini arnom. Ym Mhrydain, roedd 981,000 o bobl ifanc rhwng 16 a 24 oed heb fod mewn gwaith, addysg na hyfforddiant rhwng mis Ebrill a mis Mehefin yn ôl y Swyddfa Ystadegau Gwladol. Ond pa newidiadau sydd wedi digwydd? Mae gennym genhedlaeth goll o bobl ifanc, ac maent yn mynd i fod ar goll am byth oni roddir camau ar waith ar frys. A lle Llywodraeth Cymru yw dechrau rhoi rhai o'r camau hynny ar waith.

Yr hyn sydd wedi digwydd dros amser yw cyfansoddiad y grŵp anweithgar hwn. Mae'r gyfran sy'n anweithgar oherwydd salwch neu anabledd wedi mwy na dyblu ers 2005. Rwy'n ei chael hi'n anodd credu bod gan bron i draean o bobl a oedd yn NEET yn 2025 broblemau iechyd i'r fath raddau fel na allent gyfranogi mewn addysg, hyfforddiant na chyflogaeth. Rhesymau eraill yw bod pobl â chyfrifoldebau iechyd a gofal a'r rheini nad ydynt eisiau neu angen cyflogaeth. Cododd y rhai nad ydynt eisiau neu angen cyflogaeth yn sydyn yn ystod yr un cyfnod, i gyrraedd 23 y cant o bobl ifanc NEET yn 2025. Mae'n frawychus y bydd rhai, y rhai cyfoethog—sy'n eistedd ar y meinciau gyferbyn â ni yn ôl pob tebyg—nad oes angen iddynt weithio mewn gwirionedd. Ond mae yna lawer iawn o bobl sy'n goroesi ar fudd-daliadau os nad ydynt mewn gwaith.

Ar yr un pryd, mae cyfran y bobl ifanc sy'n anweithgar am resymau'n gysylltiedig â gofalu wedi gostwng, sy'n newyddion da, ond unwaith eto, mae'r gofalwyr di-dâl y mae pawb ohonom yn cyfarfod â nhw'n weddol rheolaidd yn parhau i ddweud wrthym am y problemau. Y rhai 16 a 17 oed sy'n debygol o fod wedi bod yn anweithgar am resymau eraill dros y blynyddoedd diwethaf, beth sy'n digwydd wedyn? Nid ydynt eisiau mynd i'r ysgol. Mae llawer o bobl nad ydynt eisiau parhau yn yr ysgol, nid yr ysgol yw eu lle, ond nid dyna ddiwedd addysg, nid dyna ddiwedd hyfforddiant ac nid yw hynny'n golygu na allant byth weithio. Mae gennym gynllun gwarant i bobl ifanc Llywodraeth Cymru ac mae'r cynllun hwnnw i'w groesawu'n fawr.

Colegau a darparwyr hyfforddiant preifat yw'r unig opsiwn pan nad oes modd symud yn uniongyrchol i gyflogaeth. Nid oes gan ddarparwyr hyfforddiant preifat, gyda llawer ohonynt yn gwneud gwaith rhagorol, allu i hyfforddi nifer fawr o bobl ifanc. Mae tystiolaeth yn dangos yn gyson fod aros mewn addysg ar ôl 16 yn hanfodol i ganlyniadau bywyd hirdymor pobl ifanc. Mae hefyd yn bwynt lle mae pobl ifanc yn wynebu penderfyniad mawr ynghylch parhau mewn addysg academaidd neu fynd ar drywydd addysg alwedigaethol—dewis a all fod yn anodd i'r rheini na chânt fawr o arweiniad neu gefnogaeth deuluol. Mae llawer o hyn yn deillio o ba fath o swyddi rydych chi'n gwybod amdanynt, a'r swyddi y mae'r rhan fwyaf o bobl ifanc yn gwybod amdanynt? Maent yn adnabod athrawon am eu bod yn eu gweld bob dydd, maent yn gwybod beth y mae eu teuluoedd yn ei wneud, maent yn gwybod beth y mae eu cymdogion yn ei wneud, ond mae yna ystod eang o swyddi nad ydynt yn gwybod dim amdanynt. Gwnaeth cyn-Aelod o'r Senedd hon a ddaeth yn fargyfreithiwr wneud hynny am iddo fynd ar ddiwrnodau hyfforddi gyda bargyfreithiwr yn Abertawe. Nawr, mae hynny'n rhywbeth sy'n anhygoel o dda, ond ni allwn adael dyfodol pobl ifanc i ddigwyddiad ar hap o'r fath, allwn ni?

Mae llawer o bobl ifanc eisiau mynd i'r coleg, ac rwy'n cydnabod y pwysau ariannol ar golegau, pe bai ond oherwydd eu bod yn parhau i ddweud wrthyf. Ond ni ddylai unrhyw un 16 i 18 oed fethu gallu mynychu coleg am nad oes digon o leoedd wedi'u hariannu. Ar gyfer colegau sy'n darparu hyfforddiant na chaiff ei ariannu gan Lywodraeth Cymru, mae'r swm wedi'i gyfyngu gan bwysau ariannol. Mae angen i Lywodraeth Cymru ariannu'r holl leoedd sydd eu hangen. Os nad ydym eisiau i bobl ifanc fod yn NEET, gadewch inni beidio â bod y bobl sy'n gwneud iddynt fod yn NEET trwy beidio â darparu lleoedd hyfforddi i bobl ifanc. Ac os yw pobl ifanc sy'n methu cael swydd neu fynd ar gwrs coleg yn dod yn NEET, nid eu bai nhw yw hynny ond ein bai ni, neu Lywodraeth Cymru, dylwn ddweud. Mae angen i'r Llywodraeth ariannu colegau addysg bellach fel y gall pawb sydd eisiau mynd i'r coleg wneud hynny. Dyna pam rwy'n cefnogi'r cynnig hwn heddiw. Mae'n bwysig fod pob unigolyn ifanc yn cael y cyfle y maent yn ei haeddu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Further education is the door to young people having an opportunity to get a great start in their working life. Not only that, but it is the door to a skilled workforce of young people here in Wales. It allows them to remain in Wales, work here, buy properties, raise their families. We know that too many young people are leaving Wales. Funding further education is literally an invest-to-save opportunity and programme. 

I want to talk about Black Mountains College, which is a further education college based in Talgarth. It provides qualifications in green skills and renewable energy. Black Mountains College provides the skills that Wales desperately needs, here in mid Wales—sorry, there in mid Wales; we're not in mid Wales, are we? I'm used to saying that—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Addysg bellach yw'r drws i bobl ifanc gael cyfle i gael dechrau gwych yn eu bywyd gwaith. Nid yn unig hynny, mae'n ddrws hefyd i weithlu medrus o bobl ifanc yma yng Nghymru. Mae'n caniatáu iddynt aros yng Nghymru, i weithio yma, i brynu eiddo, i fagu eu teuluoedd. Gwyddom fod gormod o bobl ifanc yn gadael Cymru. Mae ariannu addysg bellach yn llythrennol yn gyfle a rhaglen buddsoddi i arbed.

Rwyf am siarad am Goleg y Mynydd Du, sy'n goleg addysg bellach yn Nhalgarth. Mae'n darparu cymwysterau mewn sgiliau gwyrdd ac ynni adnewyddadwy. Mae Coleg y Mynydd Du yn darparu'r sgiliau sydd eu hangen yn ddirfawr ar Gymru, yma yng nghanolbarth Cymru—mae'n ddrwg gennyf, yno yng nghanolbarth Cymru; nid ydym yng nghanolbarth Cymru, ydym ni? Arfer yw dweud hynny —

Thank you.

—in mid Wales, where we are desperately in need of our young people to stay there. Black Mountains College has a road map to growth and yet, with a shrinking budget, it is having to say 'no' to young people who want to get on these courses, and like we've heard, has a waiting list of young people as well, who are desperate to get onto their range of courses.

Companies are crying out for skilled young people in the green agenda and renewable energy. In the case of Black Mountains College, the environment is crying out, as well, for those skilled young people. Mid Wales is crying out for our young people to stay, but most importantly, our young people are crying out for these courses. This literally is an invest-to-save opportunity and programme for this Government. And therefore, I agree with what's been said: further education must have the money it needs to be able to offer our young people that opportunity to remain here in Wales. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

Diolch.

—yng nghanolbarth Cymru, lle mae dirfawr angen i'n pobl ifanc aros yno. Mae gan Goleg y Mynydd Du gynllun ar gyfer twf ac eto, gyda chyllideb sy'n crebachu, mae'n gorfod dweud 'na' wrth bobl ifanc sydd eisiau mynd ar y cyrsiau hyn, ac fel y clywsom, mae ganddo restr aros o bobl ifanc sy'n awyddus iawn i fynd ar eu hystod o gyrsiau.

Mae cwmnïau'n crefu am bobl ifanc medrus yn yr agenda werdd ac ynni adnewyddadwy. Yn achos Coleg y Mynydd Du hefyd, mae'r amgylchedd yn crefu am y bobl ifanc medrus hynny. Mae canolbarth Cymru yn crefu ar ein pobl ifanc i aros, ond yn bwysicaf oll, mae ein pobl ifanc yn crefu am y cyrsiau hyn. Mae hwn yn llythrennol yn gyfle a rhaglen buddsoddi i arbed i'r Llywodraeth hon. Ac felly, rwy'n cytuno â'r hyn sydd wedi'i ddweud: rhaid i addysg bellach gael yr arian sydd ei angen i allu cynnig cyfle i'n pobl ifanc aros yma yng Nghymru. Diolch yn fawr iawn.
