XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. The following Members will be speaking after my opening remarks: Sarah Rees, Natasha Asghar, Matthew Jones, Cristiana Emsley, Huw Thomas and Joe Martin.

Over the past few weeks, my e-mails, like others, have been flooded with messages from people, distraught and disorientated. People who had surgeries cancelled at the eleventh hour with no explanation or option to reschedule. Patients, friends and family members desperate for answers as to why this had happened, what went wrong and how they could move forward.

On Friday, 28 August, three and a half weeks ago, hundreds of patients had their surgeries and surgical assessments suddenly paused while a clinical review was undertaken into Welsh gender services referrals. Many of these patients found out that their surgery would not be taking place while they were already in hospital. These are people who had spent years preparing, both physically and mentally, for this life-affirming surgery, which is recognised by medical organisations, professionals and NHS providers as being clinically effective at improving health outcomes and quality of life. They had jumped through every hoop asked of them, had arranged and rearranged their lives around this day. I listened to people who explained that they were left feeling abandoned, alone and confused, having had the rug pulled from under them at the very last second by the system that is supposed to care for them.

Now, I wasn't planning on sharing this. However, when listening to the stories from my constituents and others, in my own way, I was able to relate to that agonising wait in the days leading up to planned surgery. Over recess, I underwent scheduled and serious surgery. Many of you might have noticed that I was somewhat absent over the summer, and the reason for that was I was preparing for surgery, in hospital and then in recovery. Over the summer, I experienced the reality of what prepping for surgery entailed, the physical and mental stress—something so many here will be able to relate to. When I walked onto that silent ward at 5.00 a.m., the wave of emotion I felt is difficult to put into words—the silence of the sleeping ward, the uncertainty, the fear.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Bydd yr Aelodau canlynol yn siarad ar ôl fy sylwadau agoriadol: Sarah Rees, Natasha Asghar, Matthew Jones, Cristiana Emsley, Huw Thomas a Joe Martin.

Dros yr wythnosau diwethaf, mae fy mewnflwch e-bost, fel rhai pobl eraill, wedi gorlifo â negeseuon gan bob sydd mewn trallod ac yn ddryslyd. Pobl y cafodd eu llawdriniaethau eu canslo ar yr unfed awr ar ddeg heb esboniad nac opsiwn i aildrefnu. Cleifion, ffrindiau ac aelodau teuluol sy'n daer am gael atebion ynghylch pam y mae hyn wedi digwydd, beth aeth o’i le a sut y gallent symud ymlaen.

Ddydd Gwener, 28 Awst, dair wythnos a hanner yn ôl, canslwyd llawdriniaethau ac asesiadau llawfeddygol cannoedd o gleifion yn ddirybudd tra bod adolygiad clinigol yn cael ei gynnal i atgyfeiriadau gwasanaethau rhywedd Cymru. Darganfu llawer o'r cleifion hyn na fyddai eu llawdriniaeth yn digwydd a hwythau eisoes yn yr ysbyty. Dyma bobl a oedd wedi treulio blynyddoedd yn paratoi, yn gorfforol ac yn feddyliol, ar gyfer y llawdriniaeth amhrisiadwy hon, sy'n cael ei chydnabod gan sefydliadau meddygol, gweithwyr proffesiynol a darparwyr GIG fel un sy'n effeithiol yn glinigol am wella canlyniadau iechyd ac ansawdd bywyd. Roeddent wedi bod drwy bob melin y gofynnwyd iddynt fynd drwyddynt, wedi trefnu ac aildrefnu eu bywydau o amgylch y diwrnod hwn. Gwrandewais ar bobl a eglurodd eu bod yn teimlo fel pe baent wedi'u hanghofio, ar eu pen eu hunain ac yn ddryslyd, wedi i'r tir gael ei dynnu o dan eu traed ar yr eiliad olaf gan y system sydd i fod i ofalu amdanynt.

Nawr, nid oeddwn wedi bwriadu rhannu hyn. Ond wrth wrando ar y straeon gan fy etholwyr ac eraill, yn fy ffordd fy hun, roeddwn yn gallu uniaethu â'r aros poenus yn y dyddiau cyn cael llawdriniaeth a gynlluniwyd. Yn ystod y toriad, cefais lawdriniaeth a gynlluniwyd, llawdriniaeth fawr. Efallai fod llawer ohonoch wedi sylwi fy mod wedi bod yn absennol braidd dros yr haf, a'r rheswm am hynny oedd fy mod wedi bod yn paratoi ar gyfer llawdriniaeth, yn yr ysbyty ac yna'n gwella. Dros yr haf, profais realiti'r hyn roedd paratoi ar gyfer llawdriniaeth yn ei olygu, y straen corfforol a meddyliol—rhywbeth y bydd llawer ohonoch yma'n gallu uniaethu ag ef. Pan gerddais i'r ward dawel honno am 5.00 a.m., mae'n anodd disgrifio'r don o emosiwn a deimlwn—tawelwch ward yn cysgu, yr ansicrwydd, yr ofn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
But what does provide solace in those scary moments? It's the knowledge that you are in the place where everyone is working around the clock to treat you, to care for you, to listen to you. You trust the system around you. Now, for some, that trust has been broken. To think that, today, right here in Wales, we have a system that, for a certain group of people, is felt to be actively working in opposition to their well-being is a terrifying thought, one that, had it been something that I had had to consider alongside everything else, would've made my personal experience exponentially so much more traumatic. To think that the right to access health and care for some people in this country is now up for debate is unthinkable. It is not how this system was designed to run.

Now, my personal story is not what's important here. What is important is that the voices and experiences of the trans community are amplified and understood. One of the key principles on which our NHS is based is equal access to healthcare for all, regardless of age, gender or background. Another is that it has a patient-centred approach, putting individuals at the heart of their operations, providing a service that is reflective of their needs and their preferences.

Gender-affirming surgery has been available on the NHS since the 1960s, with thousands of surgeries performed each year. This is not experimental treatment and this should not be considered a controversial area of medicine. It is a well-established and highly studied area of medicine that the NHS has a legal and statutory duty to provide. The decision to pause these surgeries was ill-thought-out and callous. But it also demonstrates a failure of governance within NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee and sadly, a breakdown in communication with the Welsh Government. For patients to be told, just hours away from surgery, vulnerable but prepared, that their operation would not be going ahead, with no explanation, no indication of a rescheduled date and with no communication in the days following demonstrates a failure of the duty of care that patients are entitled to during one of the most significant events of their lives—a decision made seemingly without evidence of imminent or direct risk to patients and with no clear safety justification. How have we found ourselves in a situation where some of the supposed core values of the NHS appear to be less applicable to some patients than others? Why is the Welsh Gender Service being punished for being more efficient and effective than its English and Scottish counterparts?

The Welsh Greens are shouting loudly about this, because there's a dangerous precedent that this decision sets for human rights. This is not an ideological debate; everyone in Wales is entitled to NHS healthcare. Gender-affirming healthcare saves lives. We know, based on conversations with key stakeholders in the community, that, in June, the Welsh Gender Service was not aware of any concerns. But just two months later, the drastic escalation was made by the NWJCC to suspend all referrals and surgeries. NHS Wales's very own oversight and escalation framework, section 28, is designed to identify and address emerging issues before they have a material impact. This raises legitimate questions about how this situation rapidly evolved without any oversight or involvement from the Welsh Government. The Welsh Government should never have been surprised by this issue, nor should the NWJCC have been baffled by the discrepancy in referral numbers.

Patients who had their surgeries paused had been referred in 2020, meaning that they'd waited six years just to get to this point, with months of mental and physical preparation for surgery. Now, trans people in this country disproportionately experience poorer mental health, and the impact of this uncertainty and of cancellations have only caused further harm and distrust. Key stakeholder groups and community members have been calling on Welsh Government Ministers to use their powers under the NHS (Wales) Act 2006 to overturn this pause and resume surgery. This was clearly a disproportionate and drastic decision given the lack of evidence of harm or malpractice. So, my question is: what powers do the Welsh Government have to intervene?

The trans community are constantly left fearing that they are an afterthought, that their health and well-being are always under attack, that their right to safety and security in Wales is not a given. What this community needs now more than ever is decisive action—proof that their Government will stand up for them and take the lead, not tiptoe around the edges. The trans community should not be left waiting yet again whilst having to justify their right to healthcare and justify their very existence. Again, this is not up for debate.

When I walked into the Heath this summer with a clear timeline for surgery and recovery, there was not a doubt in my mind that I would be operated on, no doubt that I would be receiving aftercare and that my treatment plan would be thoroughly communicated. To think that there are some patients in Wales for whom that is now not their reality is horrifying. This decision has lost the trust of a vulnerable and consistently targeted group of people. Is this really the future we see in Wales, where healthcare becomes selective? The Welsh Government needs to act now, and I call on the Minister to answer the unanswered questions from community stakeholders. What is the exact nature of the so-called concerns cited by the NWJCC? How do these reflect a clear and immediate risk to patients to the extent that it required overnight cancellation of all planned surgeries?

Second, will the Welsh Government review the failure of governance that led to both patients and the Government being blindsided and put in place robust measures in consultation with the affected stakeholders to hold the NWJCC to account? Will the Welsh Government apologise to the trans community for the clear failure of communication that has left them in this unbearable limbo? Healthcare in Wales must be based on evidence, fairness and dignity, not on uncertainty, fear or political pressure. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Ond beth sy'n rhoi cysur yn yr eiliadau pryderus hynny? Yr wybodaeth eich bod chi mewn man lle mae pawb yn gweithio o gwmpas y cloc i'ch trin, i ofalu amdanoch chi, i wrando arnoch chi. Rydych chi'n ymddiried yn y system o'ch cwmpas. Nawr, i rai, mae'r ymddiriedaeth honno wedi torri. Mae meddwl, heddiw, yma yng Nghymru, fod gennym system y teimlir ei bod, i grŵp penodol o bobl, yn gweithio yn erbyn eu lles yn syniad brawychus, yn un a fyddai, pe bai wedi bod yn rhywbeth y bu'n rhaid imi ei ystyried ochr yn ochr â phopeth arall, wedi gwneud fy mhrofiad personol i cymaint yn fwy trawmatig. Mae meddwl bod yr hawl i gael mynediad at iechyd a gofal i rai pobl yn y wlad hon bellach yn destun dadl yn anhygoel. Nid dyna sut y cynlluniwyd y system hon i redeg.

Nawr, nid fy stori bersonol i yw'r hyn sy'n bwysig yma. Yr hyn sy'n bwysig yw bod lleisiau a phrofiadau'r gymuned draws yn cael eu chwyddo a'u deall. Un o'r egwyddorion allweddol y seiliwyd ein GIG arni yw mynediad cyfartal at ofal iechyd i bawb, beth bynnag y bo'u hoedran, eu rhywedd neu eu cefndir. Egwyddor arall yw dull o weithredu sy'n canolbwyntio ar y claf, gan roi unigolion yn y canol yn ei weithgarwch, gan ddarparu gwasanaeth sy'n adlewyrchu eu hanghenion a'u dewisiadau nhw.

Mae llawdriniaethau cadarnhau rhywedd wedi bod ar gael drwy'r GIG ers y 1960au, gyda miloedd o lawdriniaethau'n cael eu cyflawni bob blwyddyn. Nid triniaeth arbrofol mohoni ac ni ddylid ei hystyried yn faes meddygol dadleuol. Mae'n faes meddygol hirsefydledig a astudiwyd yn helaeth y mae gan y GIG ddyletswydd gyfreithiol a statudol i'w ddarparu. Roedd y penderfyniad i oedi'r llawdriniaethau hyn yn ddifeddwl ac yn greulon. Ond mae hefyd yn dangos methiant y trefniadau llywodraethu yng Nghyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru ac yn anffodus, methiant i gyfathrebu â Llywodraeth Cymru. Mae dweud wrth gleifion, oriau cyn eu llawdriniaeth, cleifion sy'n fregus ond wedi eu paratoi, na fyddai eu llawdriniaeth yn digwydd, heb unrhyw esboniad, dim arwydd o ddyddiad wedi'i aildrefnu a heb unrhyw gyfathrebu yn y dyddiau canlynol yn dangos methiant yn y ddyletswydd o ofal y mae gan gleifion hawl iddi yn ystod un o ddigwyddiadau mwyaf arwyddocaol eu bywydau—penderfyniad yr ymddengys iddo gael ei wneud heb dystiolaeth o risg uniongyrchol i gleifion a heb unrhyw gyfiawnhad clir mewn perthynas â diogelwch. Sut y cawsom ein hunain mewn sefyllfa lle mae rhai o werthoedd craidd tybiedig y GIG yn ymddangos yn llai perthnasol i rai cleifion nag i eraill? Pam y mae Gwasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru yn cael ei gosbi am fod yn fwy effeithlon ac effeithiol na'r cyrff sy'n cyfateb iddo yn Lloegr a'r Alban?

Mae Plaid Werdd Cymru yn codi ei llais yn gryf ynglŷn â hyn, oherwydd mae'r penderfyniad hwn yn gosod cynsail peryglus o ran hawliau dynol. Nid dadl ideolegol yw hon; mae gan bawb yng Nghymru hawl i ofal iechyd y GIG. Mae gofal iechyd sy'n cadarnhau rhywedd yn achub bywydau. Ar sail sgyrsiau gyda rhanddeiliaid allweddol yn y gymuned, fe wyddom nad oedd Gwasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru yn ymwybodol o unrhyw bryderon ym mis Mehefin. Ond gwta ddeufis yn ddiweddarach, gwelwyd uwchgyfeirio eithafol gan Gyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru i atal pob atgyfeiriad a llawdriniaeth. Mae adran 28 o fframwaith goruchwylio ac uwchgyfeirio GIG Cymru ei hun wedi'i lunio i nodi a mynd i'r afael â materion a ddaw i'r amlwg cyn iddynt gael effaith sylweddol. Mae hyn yn codi cwestiynau dilys ynglŷn â sut y datblygodd y sefyllfa hon yn gyflym heb unrhyw oruchwyliaeth na chyfranogiad gan Lywodraeth Cymru. Ni ddylai Llywodraeth Cymru fod wedi ei synnu gan y mater hwn, ac ni ddylai'r anghysondeb yn niferoedd yr atgyfeiriadau fod wedi achosi penbleth i'r cyd-bwyllgor comisiynu.

Roedd cleifion y cafodd eu llawdriniaethau eu hoedi wedi cael eu hatgyfeirio yn 2020 sy'n golygu eu bod wedi aros chwe blynedd i gyrraedd y pwynt hwn, gyda misoedd o baratoi meddyliol a chorfforol ar gyfer cael llawdriniaeth. Nawr, mae pobl draws yn y wlad hon yn profi lefel anghymesur o iechyd meddwl gwael, ac mae effaith yr ansicrwydd hwn a'r canslo wedi achosi niwed pellach a diffyg ymddiriedaeth. Mae grwpiau rhanddeiliaid allweddol ac aelodau o'r gymuned wedi bod yn galw ar Weinidogion Llywodraeth Cymru i ddefnyddio'u pwerau o dan Ddeddf GIG (Cymru) 2006 i wyrdroi'r oedi ac ailddechrau llawdriniaethau. Roedd hwn yn amlwg yn benderfyniad anghymesur ac eithafol o ystyried y diffyg tystiolaeth o niwed neu gamymarfer. Felly, fy nghwestiwn i yw: pa bwerau sydd gan Lywodraeth Cymru i ymyrryd?

Mae'r gymuned draws yn cael ei gadael mewn ofn yn barhaus eu bod yn ôl-ystyriaeth, fod eu hiechyd a'u lles bob amser dan ymosodiad, nad oes ganddynt hawl diamod i ddiogelwch yng Nghymru. Yr hyn sydd ei angen ar y gymuned hon nawr yn fwy nag erioed yw gweithredu pendant—prawf y bydd eu Llywodraeth yn sefyll drostynt ac yn gafael yn yr awenau, nid tincran ar yr ymylon. Ni ddylai'r gymuned draws gael ei gadael i aros unwaith eto a gorfod cyfiawnhau eu hawl i ofal iechyd a chyfiawnhau eu bodolaeth. Unwaith eto, nid oes dadl ynglŷn â hyn.

Pan gerddais i mewn i ysbyty Mynydd Bychan yr haf hwn gydag amserlen glir ar gyfer llawdriniaeth ac adferiad, nid oedd unrhyw amheuaeth yn fy meddwl na fyddwn i'n cael fy llawdriniaeth, dim amheuaeth na fyddwn yn cael ôl-ofal ac y byddai fy nghynllun triniaeth yn cael ei gyfathrebu'n drylwyr. Mae meddwl bod yna rai cleifion yng Nghymru nad yw hynny'n realiti iddynt mwyach yn ddychrynllyd. Mae'r penderfyniad hwn wedi arwain at golli ymddiriedaeth grŵp o bobl fregus a gaiff eu targedu'n gyson. Ai dyma'r dyfodol a welwn yng Nghymru mewn gwirionedd, lle mae gofal iechyd yn ddetholedig? Mae angen i Lywodraeth Cymru weithredu nawr, ac rwy'n galw ar y Gweinidog i ateb y cwestiynau gan randdeiliaid cymunedol na chawsant ateb iddynt. Beth yw union natur y pryderon honedig sydd gan Gyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru? Sut y mae'r rhain yn adlewyrchu risg glir ac uniongyrchol i gleifion i'r graddau fod angen canslo pob llawdriniaeth a gynlluniwyd dros nos?

Yn ail, a wnaiff Llywodraeth Cymru adolygu'r methiant yn y trefniadau llywodraethu a arweiniodd at daflu cleifion a'r Llywodraeth oddi ar eu hechel a rhoi mesurau cadarn ar waith mewn ymgynghoriad â'r rhanddeiliaid yr effeithir arnynt i ddwyn Cyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru i gyfrif? A wnaiff Llywodraeth Cymru ymddiheuro i'r gymuned draws am y methiant cyfathrebu amlwg sydd wedi eu gadael yn y limbo annioddefol hwn? Rhaid i ofal iechyd yng Nghymru fod yn seiliedig ar dystiolaeth, tegwch ac urddas, nid ar ansicrwydd, ofn a phwysau gwleidyddol. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Members are going to have to help each other. It's 15 minutes maximum for the contributions here in the opening remarks. Sarah Rees.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr. Bydd yn rhaid i Aelodau helpu ei gilydd. Mae uchafswm o 15 munud ar gyfer y cyfraniadau yma yn y sylwadau agoriadol. Sarah Rees.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. I speak here as a representative of a recognised, protected minority group, not only for transgender and non-binary people in my own constituency, but for transgender people right across Wales. I heard their voices, almost 100 of whom came to a public meeting that I hosted with Matthew Jones MS in the days after the shocking news of this pause in surgery for Welsh patients, to understand the true impact of this unprecedented action. The strongest thing I heard, 'Nothing about us without us.'

The parameters of the assessment were to ensure that no clinical harm came to patients, yet patients subjected to this review have already faced what the NWJCC have accepted is a significant level of psychiatric harm. The NWJCC have also confirmed today that the pause will remain in place until the necessary clinical assurances have been received. So, I must ask the Minister their question and not mine: are you assured that the evidence gathered by the NWJCC warrants this completely unprecedented pause? And will the Welsh Government individually review how a decision of this magnitude can be made without warning to Government, the Welsh Gender Service, or to patients?

Finally, I call on every decent human being to stand with the trans community. When you hear someone question a person's identity, call it out. This isn't harmless banter. It results in people surviving instead of thriving. Minority groups are not a political tool. Trans lives matter and trans healthcare is a human right.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Rwy'n siarad yma fel cynrychiolydd grŵp lleiafrifol cydnabyddedig a gwarchodedig, nid yn unig ar ran pobl drawsryweddol ac anneuaidd yn fy etholaeth fy hun, ond ar ran pobl drawsryweddol ledled Cymru. Clywais eu lleisiau, daeth bron i 100 ohonynt i gyfarfod cyhoeddus a gynhaliais gyda Matthew Jones AS yn y dyddiau yn dilyn y newyddion syfrdanol am yr oedi hwn i lawdriniaethau i gleifion o Gymru, er mwyn deall effaith wirioneddol y cam digynsail hwn. Y neges gryfaf a glywais oedd: 'Dim byd amdanom ni hebom ni.'

Paramedrau'r asesiad oedd sicrhau na ddeuai unrhyw niwed clinigol i gleifion, ond mae cleifion sy'n destun yr adolygiad hwn eisoes wedi wynebu'r hyn y mae Cyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru wedi derbyn ei fod yn lefel sylweddol o niwed seiciatrig. Mae'r cyd-bwyllgor hefyd wedi cadarnhau heddiw y bydd yr oedi'n parhau hyd nes y bydd y sicrwydd clinigol angenrheidiol wedi'i dderbyn. Felly, rhaid imi ofyn eu cwestiwn nhw, nid fy un i, i'r Gweinidog: a ydych chi'n sicr fod y dystiolaeth a gasglwyd gan Gyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru yn cyfiawnhau'r oedi cwbl ddigynsail hwn? Ac a fydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn adolygu'n unigol sut y gellir gwneud penderfyniad o'r maint hwn heb rybudd i'r Llywodraeth, i Wasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru, nac i gleifion?

Yn olaf, galwaf ar bob unigolyn gweddus i sefyll gyda'r gymuned draws. Pan fyddwch chi'n clywed rhywun yn cwestiynu hunaniaeth rhywun, codwch eich llais. Nid tynnu coes diniwed mohono. Mae'n arwain at bobl yn goroesi yn hytrach na ffynnu. Nid offerynnau gwleidyddol yw grwpiau lleiafrifol. Mae bywydau traws yn bwysig ac mae gofal iechyd traws yn hawl ddynol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Before I begin, I'd like to thank the Member for giving me a minute and also I hope that your surgery went well and continues to go well, as well.

The title of this short debate suggests that pausing sex-change operations is unacceptable, but that couldn't be further from the truth. There is nothing unacceptable about pausing irreversible surgery at the Welsh Gender Service while serious concerns are investigated. Clearly, the NHS believes there is a case to answer for here over the abnormally high rates of people being referred for irreversible gender surgeries, hence why this action was taken. Patient safety and well-being should always be the No. 1 priority, and pausing treatment in light of this review is absolutely the right thing to do. This decision was based on clinical and safety concerns, and patients deserve the strongest possible safeguards before a referral is made, yet the rhetoric that I've been hearing and seeing from certain politicians in relation to the current situation of the Welsh Gender Service is deeply worrying and, in my view, amounts to putting ideology before patient safety. The Welsh Gender Service has been referring patients for surgery at rates three to four times higher than clinics across the border in England. That is alarming and must be investigated. So, I would like to ask the Cabinet Minister today: will you confirm the timetable for this review, provide a guarantee that this probe will be genuinely independent and put patient welfare before gender ideology? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Cyn imi ddechrau, hoffwn ddiolch i'r Aelod am roi munud i mi a hefyd rwy'n gobeithio bod eich llawdriniaeth wedi mynd yn dda ac yn parhau i fynd yn dda.

Mae teitl y ddadl fer hon yn awgrymu bod oedi llawdriniaethau newid rhywedd yn annerbyniol, ond ni allai hynny fod ymhellach o'r gwir. Nid oes unrhyw beth annerbyniol ynglŷn ag oedi llawdriniaeth na ellir ei gwrthdroi yng Ngwasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru tra cynhelir ymchwiliad i bryderon difrifol. Yn amlwg, mae'r GIG yn credu bod achos i'w ateb yma dros y cyfraddau anarferol o uchel o bobl sy'n cael eu hatgyfeirio am lawdriniaethau rhywedd na ellir eu gwrthdroi, a dyna pam y cymerwyd y camau hyn. Dylai diogelwch a lles cleifion bob amser fod yn brif flaenoriaeth, ac oedi triniaeth yng ngoleuni'r adolygiad hwn yw'r peth hollol iawn i'w wneud. Seiliwyd y penderfyniad ar bryderon clinigol a diogelwch, ac mae cleifion yn haeddu'r mesurau diogelu cryfaf posibl cyn i atgyfeiriad gael ei wneud, ond mae'r rhethreg a glywais ac a welais gan rai gwleidyddion mewn perthynas â sefyllfa bresennol Gwasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru yn destun pryder mawr ac yn fy marn i, mae'n gosod ideoleg o flaen diogelwch cleifion. Mae Gwasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru wedi bod yn atgyfeirio cleifion am lawdriniaeth ar gyfraddau tair i bedair gwaith yn uwch na chlinigau ar draws y ffin yn Lloegr. Mae hynny'n frawychus ac mae'n rhaid ymchwilio i'r mater. Felly, hoffwn ofyn i'r Gweinidog Cabinet heddiw: a wnewch chi gadarnhau'r amserlen ar gyfer yr adolygiad hwn, darparu gwarant y bydd yr ymchwiliad yn wirioneddol annibynnol a rhoi lles cleifion o flaen ideoleg rhywedd? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I thank Anthony for this debate. I want to begin by thanking you, Mabon, the Minister. I value every conversation that we've had and I recognise your commitment to standing up for trans people and trying to make sure that this situation is resolved. Also, to all Government Ministers, it's clear that you support trans people. But this decision was made by the NWJCC at arm's length from the Government, and the NWJCC has urgent questions to answer. Its lack of transparency is highly concerning. More than three weeks ago, I wrote, with backbenchers, to the NWJCC with urgent questions about the decision and how people would be supported. We've had no reply. A recent virtual briefing on the pause raised more questions than answers. These have not been answered yet. And today, the NWJCC sent some Members a list of FAQs about its review process, but not to me—I've had to have it from another Member. The FAQs raise even further questions about the timeline, which I want the NWJCC to answer. If they've reviewed all the patients and are satisfied, or aren't satisfied, what next? At what point will the pause stop? Is it 10 patients, or 60? Is it for patients registered for surgery in 2027? Many people have put their lives on hold, including taking months off work to recover after surgery. Their health, livelihoods and finances are all now in limbo. We must reassure a community already experiencing fear and anxiety, made worse because the NWJCC has not publicly or adequately explained their concerns. Any independent review must quickly provide answers to those awaiting surgery and restore confidence across the wider trans community. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i Anthony am y ddadl hon. Rwyf am ddechrau trwy ddiolch i chi, Mabon, y Gweinidog. Rwy'n gwerthfawrogi pob sgwrs a gawsom ac rwy'n cydnabod eich ymrwymiad i sefyll dros bobl draws a cheisio sicrhau bod y sefyllfa hon yn cael ei datrys. Hefyd, i holl Weinidogion y Llywodraeth, mae'n amlwg eich bod chi'n cefnogi pobl draws. Ond gwnaed y penderfyniad hwn gan Gyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru ar sail hyd braich o'r Llywodraeth, ac mae gan y cyd-bwyllgor gwestiynau pwysig i'w hateb. Mae ei ddiffyg tryloywder yn peri pryder mawr. Dros dair wythnos yn ôl, ysgrifennais i ac aelodau o'r meinciau cefn at y cyd-bwyllgor yn gofyn cwestiynau pwysig am y penderfyniad a sut y byddai pobl yn cael eu cefnogi. Nid ydym wedi cael ateb. Roedd cyfarfod briffio rhithwir diweddar ar yr oedi yn codi mwy o gwestiynau nag a gynigiai o atebion. Nid yw'r rhain wedi'u hateb eto. A heddiw, anfonodd y cyd-bwyllgor restr o gwestiynau cyffredin i rai o'r Aelodau am ei broses adolygu, ond nid i mi—bu'n rhaid i mi ei chael gan Aelod arall. Mae'r cwestiynau cyffredin yn codi cwestiynau pellach am yr amserlen, ac rwyf am i'r cyd-bwyllgor eu hateb. Os ydynt wedi adolygu'r holl gleifion ac yn fodlon, neu heb fod yn fodlon, beth nesaf? Pryd y daw'r oedi i ben? Ai 10 claf ydyw, neu 60? Ai ar gyfer cleifion sydd wedi cofrestru ar gyfer llawdriniaeth yn 2027 y mae'r oedi'n digwydd? Mae llawer o bobl wedi rhoi eu bywydau ar stop, gan gynnwys cymryd misoedd i ffwrdd o'r gwaith i wella ar ôl llawdriniaeth. Mae eu hiechyd, eu bywoliaeth a'u harian i gyd mewn limbo nawr. Rhaid inni dawelu meddyliau cymuned sydd eisoes yn profi ofn a phryder, a waethygwyd am nad yw'r cyd-bwyllgor wedi egluro eu pryderon yn gyhoeddus nac yn ddigonol. Rhaid i unrhyw adolygiad annibynnol ddarparu atebion yn gyflym i'r rhai sy'n aros am lawdriniaeth ac adfer hyder ar draws y gymuned draws yn ehangach. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We're over time, but I'm going to give very short contributions here to the final two speakers so that everybody is called. Cristiana Emsley.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r amser ar ben, ond rwy'n mynd i roi cyfraniadau byr iawn yma i'r ddau siaradwr olaf fel bod pawb yn cael eu galw. Cristiana Emsley.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Llywydd. In line with your instructions, I'll keep this very brief, and I'd like to thank the Member for allowing me this intervention. Whatever our political differences, truth and patient safety must unite us. I accept that this pause may cause distress and patients must be supported, but what would be unacceptable is continuing irreversible referrals when serious concerns exist about referral appropriateness, clinical governance and patient safeguards—concerns I have already raised directly with the Cabinet Minister for health. As lawmakers, our duty is therefore not to pressure clinicians towards a preferred conclusion, it is to safeguard their clinical independence, to follow the science and the evidence, wherever they lead. Distress demands compassion and support, but compassion cannot lower the evidential threshold for irreversible treatment. Medicine demands evidence. Patient safety demands both. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Yn unol â'ch cyfarwyddiadau, fe gadwaf hyn yn fyr iawn, a hoffwn ddiolch i'r Aelod am ganiatáu i mi gael yr ymyriad hwn. Beth bynnag yw'r gwahaniaethau gwleidyddol rhyngom, rhaid i'r gwirionedd a diogelwch cleifion ein huno. Rwy'n derbyn y gallai'r oedi achosi gofid a bod rhaid cefnogi cleifion, ond byddai'n annerbyniol parhau ag atgyfeiriadau na ellir eu gwrthdroi pan fo pryderon difrifol ynghylch priodoldeb atgyfeiriadau, llywodraethu clinigol a diogelwch cleifion—pryderon rwyf eisoes wedi'u codi'n uniongyrchol gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros iechyd. Fel deddfwyr, ein dyletswydd ni felly yw peidio â phwyso ar glinigwyr i ddod i gasgliad a ffafrir, ond diogelu eu hannibyniaeth glinigol, dilyn y wyddoniaeth a'r dystiolaeth lle bynnag y byddant yn arwain. Mae gofid yn galw am dosturi a chefnogaeth, ond ni all tosturi ostwng trothwy'r dystiolaeth ar gyfer triniaeth na ellir ei gwrthdroi. Geilw meddygaeth am dystiolaeth. Geilw diogelwch cleifion am dosturi a thystiolaeth. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for giving me some time to speak. I'll respect that, Llywydd, by being as quick as I can and just reading the end of what I wanted to say. The Welsh Gender Service should be closed forever and the doctors in the UK who performed surgeries on children should be imprisoned for what they've done. And if Reform form a government in Westminster in 2029, I'll be making representations to our colleagues there that justice be served to the liars and the butchers responsible for what's happened to what's left of the young people who have had surgery performed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am roi ychydig o amser imi siarad. Fe barchaf hynny, Lywydd, drwy fod mor gyflym ag y gallaf a dim ond darllen diwedd yr hyn roeddwn eisiau ei ddweud. Dylai Gwasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru gael ei gau am byth a dylai'r meddygon yn y DU a roddodd lawdriniaethau i blant gael eu carcharu am yr hyn a wnaethant. Ac os bydd Reform yn ffurfio llywodraeth yn San Steffan yn 2029, byddaf yn cyflwyno sylwadau i'n cymheiriaid yno y dylid gweinyddu cyfiawnder i'r celwyddgwn a'r bwtsieriaid sy'n gyfrifol am beth a ddigwyddodd i'r hyn sy'n weddill o'r bobl ifanc a gafodd lawdriniaeth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn am hwnna. Gaf i ymbellhau fy hun a'r Llywodraeth o sylwadau Joe Martin, sydd yn gwbl annerbyniol yng nghyd-destun y drafodaeth yma heddiw? Gaf i hefyd ddiolch i'r Aelod am gyflwyno'r ddadl bwysig yma a dymuno'n dda iddo ar ei daith i wellhad llwyr?

Dyma'r cyfle gwirioneddol cyntaf i'r Senedd hon drafod y mater yma ac i mi roi ein hymateb ni, felly, ar gofnod. Yn gyntaf, dwi am gydnabod y boen a'r trallod y mae llawer wedi'u teimlo ers cyhoeddi'r penderfyniad. I lawer, roedd hwn yn cael ei weld fel penderfyniad arall mewn cyfres hir o benderfyniadau er mwyn tynnu hawliau pobl draws oddi arnynt, yn erydu eu hunaniaeth, ac rwy'n deall yr ofn yma. Gadewch imi bwysleisio, felly, mai penderfyniad clinigol oedd hwn, wedi'i wneud ar sail tystiolaeth glinigol heb ymyrraeth wleidyddol. Gadewch imi hefyd fod yn glir: mi ydym ni—rydw i—yn sefyll gyda’r gymuned draws.

Fel Llywodraeth, rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i ddiogelu hawliau pob person LGBTQ+ yng Nghymru, ac, fel y gŵyr yr Aelodau, chwaraeodd Plaid Cymru ran allweddol wrth sicrhau bod y cynllun gweithredu LGBTQ+ yn cael ei gyflawni. Mae ein maniffesto yn nodi ein hymrwymiad i'r gymuned draws, a gallwch fod yn sicr bod Llywodraeth Cymru yn sefyll gyda'r gymuned draws ac y bydd yn parhau i amddiffyn hawliau pobl draws yn unol â'n hymrwymiad i Gymru groesawgar a chynhwysol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much. May I distance myself and the Government from the comments made by Joe Martin, which are entirely unacceptable in the context of today's debate? May I also thank the Member for bringing forward this important debate and wish him well on his journey towards a full recovery?

This is the first real opportunity for the Senedd to discuss this matter and for me to place our response on the record. Firstly, I would like to acknowledge the pain and distress that many have felt since the decision was announced. For many, this was seen as another decision in a long series of decisions to strip trans people of their rights, eroding their very identity, and I understand these concerns and fears. So, let me emphasise that this was a clinical decision, made on the basis of clinical evidence without political intervention. Let me also be clear that we—that I—stand with the trans community.

As a Government, we are committed to safeguarding the rights of every LGBTQ+ person in Wales, and, as Members know, Plaid Cymru played a key role in ensuring the delivery of the LGBTQ+ action plan. Our manifesto sets out our commitment to the trans community, and you can be assured that the Welsh Government stands with the trans community and will continue to defend the rights of trans people in line with our commitment to a welcoming and inclusive Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I recognise that some people accessing gender identity services will already be experiencing emotional distress, and I understand the additional distress, anxiety and uncertainty of this situation. I want to be clear that we remain committed to ensuring access to high-quality specialist gender identity services in Wales. I also want to reassure people that this decision is a temporary pause, not a stop, and a decision made by the NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee in the interest of patient safety.

The decision to pause gender-affirming surgery was made through established clinical governance processes. These apply to all services commissioned by the NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee. It isn't unusual for the JCC to place services in escalation when there is a need to seek assurance on clinical or quality issues. These processes exist to ensure patient safety, and we need to be led by them, based on their independent clinical assessment of the evidence.

Welsh Ministers don't have a role in the clinical governance and escalation processes within the JCC. The NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee are responsible for the commissioning and oversight of specialised services, including gender identity services, and are formally accountable to health boards in Wales. This provides a consistency of offer, with the necessary governance and monitoring and clinical oversight in place to ensure services are safe and effective. The JCC brings together health boards for services that need to be commissioned once for Wales. This includes specialist gender identity services. As a Government, we have been clear that we will be led by the evidence when it comes to ensuring the quality and safety of our NHS services. This is vital if we are to ensure safe services and good outcomes for our patients in Wales.

For the avoidance of doubt, and let me be clear, this was a clinically-led decision made by the JCC due to concerns with the quality of assessments and the volume of referrals for gender surgery. The decision was primarily based on data provided by the gender dysphoria national referral support services. Gender surgery for Welsh patients is commissioned by NHS England, who are responsible for managing and validating referrals for surgery. The centrally held data showed higher rates of referral from Wales, but lower rates of progression to some surgeries. Concerns were also raised by clinical colleagues in NHS England about appropriateness of referrals and clinical suitability. The JCC has a duty of care to all patients who receive specialist services that it commissions to ensure that those services are safe and effective. Taken together, these concerns highlighted potential issues that the JCC needed to take seriously.

Given the level of concerns across parties, I'm grateful that the JCC offered technical briefing sessions to all parties to provide more information about the data and the decisions taken. I hope you took the opportunity to engage in these sessions with the JCC to seek assurances on the questions or concerns that you have.

Following the escalation of the service, the JCC committed to an urgent clinical review of those individuals on the waiting list for gender-affirming surgery. The JCC has already appointed the independent clinical review panel, and, subject to final governance approval, it is anticipated that the review will commence imminently. This review will prioritise those individuals who are further along the pathway to allow appropriate referrals to proceed as soon as possible. The JCC has identified that approximately 60 patients were due surgery between the pausing of surgery in August and the end of December. Our priority is to bring certainty to these people as quickly as possible, and the JCC are confident that all 60 of these cases can be reviewed before the end of December.

There is also a wider, independent review of the Welsh Gender Service. It was always intended by the JCC that this planned review would follow the independent Levy review, which looked at adult gender identity services in England. The independent review has already commenced and comprises both quality and clinical governance elements. The review will focus primarily on assessment, referral and non-surgical aspects of the pathway, while considering relevant pathway interfaces. It will engage key stakeholders, including health boards, partner organisations, patients and carers. Initial findings are expected later this year, with recommendations to be reported to the JCC thereafter.

Both reviews will include independent reviewers and are a clinical process. It is entirely consistent with existing governance arrangements of this nature that the Welsh Government will have no role or involvement in these reviews or the recommendations that they make. We will, of course, expect that both the JCC and Cardiff and Vale University Health Board act on the findings from the reviews as a matter of priority.

I've met with the JCC and been clear that the urgent clinical review needs to be swift to minimise the disruption and distress for individuals on the waiting list. I've also been clear that I expect all patients impacted by this pause to have access to the necessary support whilst the review is undertaken. This includes emotional and psychological support. I've written to Cardiff and Vale University Health Board and received assurances about the support available for those who are affected by the pause.

The JCC has now published the equality and Welsh language impact assessment and the quality impact assessment and other papers related to the decisions on their website.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n cydnabod y bydd rhai o'r bobl sy'n defnyddio gwasanaethau hunaniaeth rhywedd eisoes yn profi trallod emosiynol, ac rwy'n deall y trallod, y pryder a'r ansicrwydd ychwanegol yn y sefyllfa hon. Rwyf am fod yn glir ein bod yn parhau'n ymrwymedig i sicrhau mynediad at wasanaethau hunaniaeth rhywedd arbenigol o ansawdd uchel yng Nghymru. Rwyf hefyd eisiau sicrhau pobl mai oedi dros dro yw'r penderfyniad hwn, nid terfyniad, ac mae'n benderfyniad a wnaed gan Gyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru er budd diogelwch cleifion.

Gwnaed y penderfyniad i oedi llawdriniaeth cadarnhau rhywedd trwy brosesau llywodraethu clinigol sefydledig. Mae'r rhain yn berthnasol i bob gwasanaeth a gomisiynwyd gan Gyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru. Nid yw'n anarferol i'r cyd-bwyllgor osod camau uwchgyfeirio ar wasanaethau pan fo angen ceisio sicrwydd ynghylch materion clinigol neu ansawdd. Mae'r prosesau hyn yn bodoli er mwyn sicrhau diogelwch cleifion, ac mae angen inni gael ein harwain ganddynt, yn seiliedig ar eu hasesiad clinigol annibynnol o'r dystiolaeth.

Nid oes gan Weinidogion Cymru rôl yn y prosesau llywodraethu clinigol ac uwchgyfeirio yn y cyd-bwyllgor. Mae Cyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru yn gyfrifol am gomisiynu a goruchwylio gwasanaethau arbenigol, gan gynnwys gwasanaethau hunaniaeth rhywedd, ac maent yn atebol yn ffurfiol i fyrddau iechyd yng Nghymru. Mae hyn yn sicrhau cynnig cyson, gyda'r trefniadau llywodraethu a monitro angenrheidiol a goruchwyliaeth glinigol ar waith i sicrhau bod gwasanaethau'n ddiogel ac yn effeithiol. Daw'r cyd-bwyllgor â byrddau iechyd at ei gilydd ar gyfer gwasanaethau sydd angen eu comisiynu unwaith i Gymru. Mae hyn yn cynnwys gwasanaethau hunaniaeth rhywedd arbenigol. Fel Llywodraeth, rydym wedi dweud yn glir y byddwn yn cael ein harwain gan y dystiolaeth er mwyn sicrhau ansawdd a diogelwch ein gwasanaethau GIG. Mae hyn yn hanfodol os ydym am sicrhau gwasanaethau diogel a chanlyniadau da i'n cleifion yng Nghymru.

Er mwyn osgoi amheuaeth, gadewch i mi fod yn glir, roedd hwn yn benderfyniad clinigol a wnaed gan y cyd-bwyllgor yn sgil pryderon ynghylch ansawdd yr asesiadau a nifer yr atgyfeiriadau ar gyfer llawdriniaethau rhywedd. Roedd y penderfyniad yn seiliedig yn bennaf ar ddata a ddarparwyd gan y gwasanaethau cymorth atgyfeirio cenedlaethol ar gyfer dysfforia rhywedd. Caiff llawfeddygaeth rhywedd i gleifion o Gymru ei gomisiynu gan GIG Lloegr, sy'n gyfrifol am reoli a dilysu atgyfeiriadau ar gyfer llawdriniaeth. Roedd y data a gedwir yn ganolog yn dangos cyfraddau atgyfeirio uwch o Gymru, ond cyfraddau is yn symud ymlaen at rai mathau o lawdriniaethau. Codwyd pryderon hefyd gan gydweithwyr clinigol yn GIG Lloegr ynghylch priodoldeb atgyfeiriadau ac addasrwydd clinigol. Mae gan y cyd-bwyllgor ddyletswydd gofal i bob claf sy'n derbyn gwasanaethau arbenigol y mae'n eu comisiynu i sicrhau bod y gwasanaethau hynny'n ddiogel ac yn effeithiol. Gyda'i gilydd, tynnai'r pryderon hyn sylw at faterion posibl yr oedd angen i'r cyd-bwyllgor eu cymryd o ddifrif.

O ystyried lefel y pryderon ar draws y pleidiau, rwy'n ddiolchgar fod y cyd-bwyllgor wedi cynnig sesiynau briffio technegol i bob plaid i ddarparu mwy o wybodaeth am y data a'r penderfyniadau a wnaed. Gobeithio eich bod wedi manteisio ar y cyfle i gymryd rhan yn y sesiynau hyn gyda'r cyd-bwyllgor i geisio sicrwydd ynghylch y cwestiynau neu'r pryderon sydd gennych.

Yn dilyn uwchgyfeirio'r gwasanaeth, ymrwymodd y cyd-bwyllgor i adolygiad clinigol brys o'r unigolion ar y rhestr aros am lawdriniaeth cadarnhau rhywedd. Mae'r cyd-bwyllgor eisoes wedi penodi'r panel adolygu clinigol annibynnol, ac yn amodol ar gymeradwyo'r trefniadau llywodraethu terfynol, disgwylir y bydd yr adolygiad yn dechrau'n fuan. Bydd yr adolygiad hwn yn blaenoriaethu'r unigolion hynny sydd ymhellach ar hyd y llwybr i ganiatáu i atgyfeiriadau priodol fynd rhagddynt cyn gynted â phosibl. Mae'r cyd-bwyllgor wedi nodi bod tua 60 o gleifion yn aros am lawdriniaeth rhwng oedi llawdriniaethau ym mis Awst a diwedd mis Rhagfyr. Ein blaenoriaeth yw dod â sicrwydd i'r bobl hyn cyn gynted â phosibl, ac mae'r cyd-bwyllgor yn hyderus y gellir adolygu pob un o'r 60 achos cyn diwedd mis Rhagfyr.

Mae yna adolygiad ehangach ar waith hefyd, yn annibynnol ar Wasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru. Roedd y cyd-bwyllgor wedi bwriadu o'r dechrau i'r adolygiad arfaethedig hwn ddilyn adolygiad annibynnol Levy, a edrychai ar wasanaethau hunaniaeth rhywedd oedolion yn Lloegr. Mae'r adolygiad annibynnol eisoes wedi dechrau ac mae'n cynnwys elfennau ansawdd a llywodraethiant clinigol. Bydd yr adolygiad yn canolbwyntio'n bennaf ar asesu, atgyfeirio ac agweddau ar y llwybr nad ydynt yn llawfeddygol wrth ystyried y rhyngwyneb rhwng llwybrau perthnasol. Bydd yn ymgysylltu â rhanddeiliaid allweddol, gan gynnwys byrddau iechyd, sefydliadau partner, cleifion a gofalwyr. Disgwylir y canfyddiadau cychwynnol yn ddiweddarach eleni, gydag argymhellion i'w hadrodd i'r cyd-bwyllgor wedi hynny.

Bydd y ddau adolygiad yn cynnwys adolygwyr annibynnol ac maent yn broses glinigol. Mae'n gwbl gyson â threfniadau llywodraethu presennol o'r natur hon na fydd gan Lywodraeth Cymru unrhyw rôl na chyfranogiad yn yr adolygiadau hyn na'r argymhellion a wnânt. Byddwn yn disgwyl i'r cyd-bwyllgor a Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Caerdydd a'r Fro weithredu ar ganfyddiadau'r adolygiadau fel mater o flaenoriaeth wrth gwrs.

Rwyf wedi cyfarfod â'r cyd-bwyllgor ac wedi bod yn glir fod angen i'r adolygiad clinigol brys ddigwydd yn gyflym er mwyn lleihau'r aflonyddwch a'r trallod i unigolion ar y rhestr aros. Rwyf hefyd wedi bod yn glir fy mod yn disgwyl i'r holl gleifion yr effeithir arnynt gan yr oedi hwn gael mynediad at y cymorth angenrheidiol tra bod yr adolygiad ar y gweill. Mae hyn yn cynnwys cymorth emosiynol a seicolegol. Rwyf wedi ysgrifennu at Fwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Caerdydd a'r Fro ac wedi cael sicrwydd ynghylch y cymorth sydd ar gael i'r rhai yr effeithir arnynt gan yr oedi.

Mae'r cyd-bwyllgor bellach wedi cyhoeddi'r asesiad o'r effaith ar gydraddoldeb a'r Gymraeg a'r asesiad o'r effaith ar ansawdd a phapurau eraill sy'n gysylltiedig â'r penderfyniadau ar eu gwefan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Rwy'n cydnabod y trallod a'r ansicrwydd y mae'r seibiant hwn yn ei achosi i'r rhai yr effeithir arnynt. Rwyf wedi clywed yn bersonol gan bobl yr effeithir arnynt gan y penderfyniad yma, ac rwy'n ddiolchgar i gydweithwyr yn y Senedd am eu gweithredoedd wrth wrando, cefnogi ac eirioli ar ran cymaint o bobl. Rwy'n gweithio gyda'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb i sicrhau bod yr effaith ar y gymuned draws yn cael ei hystyried yn llawn wrth i'r JCC a Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Caerdydd a'r Fro ymgymryd â'r gwaith adolygu a dilynol.

Rwy'n cael fy niweddaru'n rheolaidd am gynnydd gan y JCC a Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Caerdydd a'r Fro, a chyfarfu swyddogion â'r JCC ddoe i gael y wybodaeth ddiweddaraf am gynnydd. Rwy'n disgwyl i unrhyw gamau angenrheidiol gael eu cymryd ymlaen fel blaenoriaeth i sicrhau bod Gwasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru yn darparu'r ansawdd gwasanaeth y byddem yn ei ddisgwyl.

Rwyf wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau bod ein cyrff cyhoeddus yn darparu'r lefel uchaf o wasanaeth i bawb sy'n dibynnu arnynt. Gyda hynny mewn golwg, mae'n hanfodol ein bod yn dysgu yn barhaus o benderfyniadau fel yr un hwn, felly, rwyf wedi gofyn i'r prif swyddog meddygol gynnal ymarfer myfyriol mewnol ar y broses sy'n gysylltiedig â'r penderfyniad hwn. Bydd hyn yn ystyried sut y cyfathrebwyd â chleifion ac eraill, amseriad cyfathrebu a'r prosesau sy'n eu cefnogi, gan gynnwys llais y gymuned draws. Bydd lleisiau'r gymuned draws yn ganolog i'r gwaith yma. Mae gwrando a dysgu'n hanfodol.

Felly, diolch, unwaith eto, i Anthony, am gyflwyno'r ddadl, a diolch i bawb a gyfrannodd mewn modd adeiladol i'r ddadl yma.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I acknowledge the distress and uncertainty that this pause has caused for those affected. I have heard personally from people affected by this decision, and I'm grateful to colleagues in the Senedd for their actions in listening to, supporting and advocating on behalf of so many people. I'm working with the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice and Equality to ensure that the impact on the trans community is fully considered as the JCC and Cardiff and Vale University Health Board undertake the review and follow-up work.

I'm being regularly updated on progress by the JCC and Cardiff and Vale University Health Board, and officials met with the JCC yesterday to receive a progress update. I expect any necessary steps to be taken forward as a priority to ensure that the Welsh Gender Service delivers the quality of service that we would all expect.

I'm committed to ensuring that our public bodies provide the highest level of service to everyone who relies on them. With that in mind, it is essential that we continue to learn from decisions such as this one, therefore, I have asked the chief medical officer to conduct a reflective exercise regarding the processes associated with this decision. This will consider methods of communication with patients and others, the timing of that communication and the supporting processes, including the voice of the trans community. The voices of the trans community will be central to this review. Listening and learning are essential.

So, thank you once again, Anthony, for presenting this debate, and thank you to everyone who has contributed in a constructive manner to this debate.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: May I raise a point of order under 13.9(v) of our Standing Orders? Llywydd, you will be aware that each Member here is governed by a code of conduct. We are also obliged to act lawfully and be mindful of different laws, including the Equality Act 2010. I would ask you to review Joe Martin MS's comments on the cofnod and determine if you are of the view that he is guilty, in your view, of using disorderly, discriminatory or offensive language or language that detracts from the dignity of the Senedd. I would suggest strongly that the comments were not in line with our Standing Orders.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A gaf i godi pwynt o drefn o dan 13.9(v) o'n Rheolau Sefydlog? Lywydd, fe fyddwch chi'n ymwybodol fod pob Aelod yma'n cael ei lywodraethu gan god ymddygiad. Mae'n ofynnol i ni hefyd weithredu'n gyfreithlon a chadw gwahanol gyfreithiau mewn cof, yn cynnwys Deddf Cydraddoldeb 2010. Hoffwn i chi adolygu sylwadau Joe Martin AS ar y cofnod a phenderfynu a ydych chi o'r farn ei fod yn euog, yn eich barn chi, o ddefnyddio iaith sy'n groes i'r drefn, yn wahaniaethol, neu'n sarhaus ac sy'n amharu ar urddas y Senedd. Carwn awgrymu'n gryf nad oedd y sylwadau'n cydymffurfio â'n Rheolau Sefydlog.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 9. Dadl Fer: Yr oedi annerbyniol mewn triniaeth wedi'i threfnu ar gyfer cleifion traws
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 9. Short Debate: The unacceptable pause in scheduled treatment for trans patients
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for raising that point of order and giving me notice that you were going to do so. I think there is merit within the point of order and I'm happy to review the Record of Proceedings. I will, indeed, return to the matter if I consider that a ruling is necessary. There are clear guidelines and Standing Orders in terms of language within the Chamber. So, I will happily take this away and review the Record of Proceedings. Thank you for raising it. Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am godi'r pwynt o drefn a rhoi rhybudd i mi eich bod chi'n mynd i wneud hynny. Rwy'n credu bod teilyngdod yn y pwynt o drefn ac rwy'n hapus i ailedrych ar Gofnod y Trafodion. Byddaf yn sicr o ddychwelyd at y mater os credaf fod angen dyfarniad. Mae canllawiau clir a Rheolau Sefydlog yn bodoli ar gyfer yr iaith a ddefnyddir yn y Siambr. Felly, rwy'n hapus i ystyried y mater ac i ailedrych ar Gofnod y Trafodion. Diolch yn fawr am ei godi.
